## D.7 The autonomy hold gate (D16)

`autoApplyHoldActive` (`weeklyCoach.js:1496-1506`) is the **single** emitted "is a hold open right now" flag, true when any of: `deloadSuggested`, `matrixDeload`, `poorRecovery`, `safetyHold`, `ffmFloorHeld`, `edPatternHeld`, `rapidWeightLossFlag`, `scoffPositive`, `calmMode`.
Founder ruling 2026-07-10: "Coached never auto-applies while a safety hold / ED-flag / suppression is active." Whatever autonomy mode is active, an open hold forces confirm-first behaviour — a more autonomous mode changes **who** confirms, never whether the apply path's clamps run (`:1483-1495`).
`CoachOutputScreen` reads this one flag rather than re-deriving the hold list. Guard: `CoachOutputScreen.d16Autonomy.guard.test.js`.

## D.8 The five-part coach response (`coachResponse.js`)

| Part | Builder | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Acknowledgement | `buildAcknowledgement` (`:76`) | Names something real from this week; returns null rather than fabricating. Weigh-in counts ride along only when ≥5 (or carry it alone at ≥3) and **never under suppression**. A fully quiet week gets "A quieter week. Your plan is ready whenever you are." (T8, `:117-122`) |
| 2 Interpretation | `buildInterpretation` (`:169`) | Under suppression: direction-only, rate dropped entirely. On-target streak uses ordinal words 2nd–6th then a numeric fallback (`ORDINAL_WORDS`, `:60`) |
| 3 Decision | `buildDecision` (`:214`) | Safety holds lead and reuse their locked reason strings **verbatim**. **Register-blind always** (`coachRegister.js:311`) |
| 4 Cue | `buildCue` (`:256`) | Exactly one, deterministic 7-step priority: thin weigh-ins (skipped under suppression) → sleep <6.5 h → missed sessions → joint pain → untracked calories (skipped under suppression) → adherence off ('under' allowed under suppression, 'over' skipped) → default |
| 5 Forward pull | `buildForward` (`:309`) | Anchors the next check-in by name |
| 6 Pre-commitment | `buildPreCommitment` (`:388`) | Names in advance what the next read will check; null under suppression |
| 6b Commitment answer | `buildCommitmentAnswer` (`:397`) | Reuses `pairAppliedWithOutcome` so the prose and the history chip can never disagree |

`clamped` handling (`:350-356`): when the ED floor caught a cut below the proposed change, the number is dropped and the copy says "this week's calorie change" instead, so the figure never overstates what landed.

Every exported string passes `clean()` (`:41-52`): the shared jargon blocklist **plus** a hard block on em and en dashes.

## D.9 Register + science layer (`coachRegister.js`)

`resolveRegister({coachTone, experienceLevel, trainingAgeYears})` (`:80`): explicit preference wins; automatic maps advanced/competitive → precise, beginner/intermediate → supportive (the user's self-identification outranks training age), and with no experienceLevel, `trainingAgeYears >= 5` → precise. Everything ambiguous lands supportive.
`TONE_PREFERENCES` = automatic | supportive | precise (`:64`).

**SAFETY CARVE-OUT, register-blind** (`:21-27`, enforced at `:292-294`): under suppression, or with no output, the **supportive** rendering is returned untouched whatever the preference. Part 3 is register-blind always.
Structural parity is guaranteed by construction — a precise part renders only where the supportive part rendered (`:298-323`), and `coachRegister.test.js` fails if the ladders drift.

`withScience(plainTerm, technicalTerm, showScience)` (`coachResponse.js:159`, re-exported at `coachRegister.js:340`): the plain term always leads and the technical term **never appears alone** — no plain term means no output at all (`:161`).
Live call sites: `coachResponse.js:188`, `coachRegister.js:165`, `CoachOutputScreen.js:2529`. All three render "7-day average"/"7-day trend" with "(EWMA)" bracketed after it when the Settings opt-in is on.

## D.10 Coach outcome memory (`coachOutcome.js`)

`pairAppliedWithOutcome(historyDesc)` (`:45`) pairs each week's **applied** decision with the FOLLOWING week's trend verdict.
Honesty rules baked in (`:12-19`): only a **calendar-consecutive** next week counts (6–8 day window, absorbing DST), so a verdict is never misattributed across a gap; the newest week is never paired; the scorecard hides below `MIN_SCORECARD_SAMPLE = 2` (founder call 2026-07-03) so too small a sample reads as neither boast nor accusation.
Suppression is the caller's job — the screen passes `[]`/null; it is never softened here (`:19-20`).
Domains checked in order: calories, training, steps (`:25`).

## D.11 Week-one proof (`coachLedger.js`)

`buildCoachLedger({weighIns7d, completedSessions, firstWeightAt, checkinDay, edFlagOpen, now})` (`:72`).
Three rows (`:98-123`): "N of M morning weigh-ins in the last 7 days" (label corrected by X11 — the window was always trailing-7, the copy said "this week"); "Day N of M days of data" / "First morning weight starts the clock"; "N training sessions logged" / "No training sessions yet".
Title "What your coach is reading".
**ED variant** (`:83-92`): `variant: 'neutral'`, title "Your coach is getting to know you", **zero rows** — no weigh-in counts and no weight ask.
Gate constants are imported from `trialActivation.js` so the ledger can never disagree with the check-in gate (`:11-13`).
`buildHoldReceipt` (`:143`) adds `rule` (the engine's own hold message, or the published thresholds) and `unlockLine`, which says "around {date}" in the neutral variant because that variant cannot mention the weigh-in requirement (`:148-155`).
`formatCheckinCountdown` (`:50`): "Check-in is today" / "Check-in is tomorrow" / "N days to your next check-in" — day-count only, so it stays safe under the neutral variant.

# PART E — EXPLANATION / EDUCATION SYSTEM

## E.1 The glossary — ALL 26 entries

`src/lib/coachGlossary.js`. A single **static, authored, deterministic map** — no dynamic generation, no AI (`:1-9`). The tone layer decides *whether* to show a gloss, never what it says.

| # | Key | Gloss (verbatim) | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `precisionCoaching` | "Every week it reads your weight trend, check-in and training, compares what happened to what was expected, and explains the decision. Nothing is random." | `:11` |
| 2 | `volume` | "The total work for a muscle: the hard sets you do for it in a week." | `:13` |
| 3 | `deload` | "A lighter planned week so you recover: lighter loads, full recovery, no PRs." | `:15` |
| 4 | `maintenanceCalories` | "The daily calories that keep your weight steady: the starting point a change is measured from." | `:17` |
| 5 | `refeed` | "A planned higher-carb day on an aggressive cut, to ease fatigue." | `:19` |
| 6 | `macroCycle` | "Alternating higher- and lower-carb days across the week." | `:21` |
| 7 | `estMax` | "An estimate of the most you could lift once, worked out from your recent sets. You never have to test it." | `:23` |
| 8 | `effort` | "How close to failure the set should feel: 5 = leave nothing, 0 = very easy." | `:25` |
| 9 | `volumeBands` | "How much you've trained a muscle this week vs the helpful range. 'Over limit' = past the point of extra benefit, not dangerous." | `:27` |
| 10 | `repRegression` | "Your average reps for a lift have trended down over recent weeks." | `:29` |
| 11 | `adaptiveTdee` | "Our running estimate of the calories you burn a day, updated from your weight trend." | `:31` |
| 12 | `ewma` | "A smoothed version of your weight that ignores day-to-day noise." | `:33` |
| 13 | `mesocycle` | "A training block: a few weeks that ease in, build, push, then recover." | `:35` |
| 14 | `rir` | "Reps in reserve: how many reps you'd have left; 'stop 2 short' means leave 2 in the tank." | `:37` |
| 15 | `strengthLevel` | "Where your estimated max sits against typical lifters at your bodyweight." | `:39` |
| 16 | `bodyFatMethod` | "How a body fat % was measured: Visual (eyeballed), BIA…, Caliper…, DEXA (a clinical scan, the most accurate)." | `:43` |
| 17 | `engineLog` | "A plain record of what Precision Coaching changed in your training, and why." | `:46` |
| 18 | `division` | "The category you'd compete in… your plan is tailored to what that division is judged on." | `:48` |
| 19 | `phase` | "Your current aim: lose fat (cut), gain muscle slowly (lean-gain) or hold steady (maintain)." | `:50` |
| 20 | `macros` | "Protein, carbs and fat: the three nutrients your daily calories are made of." | `:52` |
| 21 | `proteinTier` | "How high your protein target is set: Standard, Optimised…, Advanced… Based on your bodyweight, or your lean mass if you have logged a measured body-fat reading." | `:54` |
| 22 | `recomposition` | "Your weight held steady while your shape or strength kept improving…" | `:56` |
| 23 | `autoregulation` | "Adjusting your training and targets week to week based on how you're actually recovering and performing, rather than following a fixed plan regardless." | `:60` |
| 24 | `redS` | "Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport: when the body runs on too little energy, for too long… Your coach watches for the early signals so your plan stays safe." | `:62` |
| 25 | `superset` | "Two or more exercises done back-to-back with no rest between them, then a full rest before repeating." | `:68` |
| 26 | `set` | "A set is a number of reps done one after another, then a rest before the next set." | `:74` |
| 27 | `rep` | "A rep is one full repetition of an exercise, like one push-up or one squat." | `:76` |
| 28 | `streakWeeks` | "Your run counts weeks where you hit your weekly session target… Deload weeks always count… forgiven once every six weeks…" | `:90` |
| 29 | `volyumeScore` | "…a progress read from your own photos, controlled for pose and lighting… It is not a body fat measurement, a medical assessment, or a comparison with anyone else." | `:104` |
| 30 | `workingSets` | "Every set you logged this block, not counting warm-ups." | `:112` |
| 31 | `tonnage` | "The total weight moved: every set's weight times reps, added up across the block." | `:119` |

**31 entries.** (`autoregulation` and `redS` are now orphaned — their only call site, the CoachOutput credential row, was removed by D86, `CoachOutputScreen.js:2837-2841`. See §E.6.)

Provenance notes worth recording:
- `streakWeeks` exists because of finding **O24**: the streak criterion was only ever explained by ConsistencyEcho's **one-time dismissable** explainer, "so it becomes unlearnable after the first dismissal" (`:78-89`). It is now shared verbatim by ConsistencyEcho and WeeklyStreakStrip so the wording can never diverge.
- `volyumeScore` exists because of finding **O2**: the meaning moment "is shown once ever and never reachable again" (`:92-105`). Body-image-adjacent: no praise/shame language, no targets. The marker-shape clause is kept in sync with `markerShapeForTier`.
- `workingSets` is deliberately NOT the "effort checked" framing that finding **O27** flagged as wrong on WorkoutSummaryScreen — counting is by set TYPE, never by how a set felt (`:106-111`).
- `tonnage` is deliberately distinct from `volume`; BlockReflection keeps its own "Volume" label but the tooltip stops it being confused with the app's other Volume (`:114-118`).
- `set` / `rep` are self-naming baseline vocabulary added by **NV-4** for the "never lifted" persona (`:70-73`).

## E.3 The tooltip mechanism

`src/components/InfoTooltip.js` — an ⓘ glyph opening a modal.
- Touch target reaches ≥44 px via `hitSlop` so the region grows invisibly with no layout reflow (U-F-2/U-F-5, `:55-57`).
- **AX-01 screen-reader focus management**: focus moves INTO the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close (`:22-48`), both best-effort and guarded.
- **AX-01 semantics**: the backdrop and the dialog are **siblings**, never parent/child, because an accessible parent wrapping the card would group/suppress its descendants on iOS VoiceOver and expose only "Close, button", hiding the explanation (`:65-72`). `accessibilityViewIsModal` on the dialog.
- A real, visible 44×44 Close control in addition to the backdrop tap (`:127-140`).
- Honours `reduceMotion` (`:16, :64`).

## E.5 The jargon blocklist — what is BANNED

`JARGON_PATTERNS` (`whyThisTemplates.js:40-62`), enforced by `checkJargon(str)` (`:604`) and by `clean()` in `whyThisTemplates.js`, `coachResponse.js`, `coachRegister.js` and `progressScanCoachResolver.js` (dev-time throw).

| Category | Banned tokens |
|---|---|
| Gym abbreviations | `MEV`, `MAV`, `MRV`, `RIR`, `RPE`, `mesocycle` (case-insensitive), `junk volume` |
| Science jargon | `metabolic adaptation`, `training stimulus`, `stimulus-to-fatigue ratio` |
| Bare researcher surnames | `Helms`, `Schoenfeld`, `Morton`, `Mountjoy`, `Eikey`, `Refalo`, `Trexler` |

Word boundaries avoid false positives ("helmsman" does not match "Helms", `:37-39`).
Sanctioned replacements (`:24-27`): metabolic adaptation → "your body has adjusted"; training stimulus → "muscle growth signal"; stimulus-to-fatigue ratio → "training payoff".
Citations belong in InfoTooltip panels, not surface copy (`:21-22`).
Additionally: **em and en dashes are banned everywhere** in coach copy (`coachResponse.js:47-50`, `coachRegister.js:52-55`, `whyThisTemplates.js:76-81`, `progressScanCoachResolver.js:18-20`) and lint-enforced per CLAUDE.md §3.

Pinned by `src/lib/__tests__/jargonBlocklist.test.js` — regression cases for all 7 gym abbreviations, all 3 science phrases, all 7 surnames, plus positive cases for the plain-English alternatives.

**Consequence:** `GLOSSARY.rir` and `GLOSSARY.mesocycle` exist as *definitions* of banned terms. They can only appear inside a tooltip panel, never in coach prose — and `GLOSSARY.mesocycle` currently has **no call site at all** (see §E.6).

## E.8 Where the app makes a decision WITHOUT explaining it

1. **The recovery grade and performance grade (1–4) that drive the entire volume decision are never surfaced.** `getRecoveryScore` (`weeklyCoach.js:203`) and `getPerformanceScore` (`:239`) are not in the emitted output object. The user sees the *result* (volume up/down) and a copy line, never the two grades or the matrix cell.
2. **The autoregulation matrix itself is unpublished.** `MethodologyScreen` says volume moves "-2 to +3 sets… based on how your energy, soreness and completed sessions scored together" (`:75-78`) but never the mapping.
3. **The stress→recovery downgrade is silent.** Stress ≥4 forces the recovery read to 3 (`weeklyCoach.js:217`). No copy anywhere tells the user their stress answer changed the decision.
4. **Peak-week fatigue softening.** `contextAdjustedRecovery` silently converts a grade 3 to a 2 for the push branch. It produces one line of copy only when it results in a push (`:907-909`); when it merely prevents a hold, nothing is said.
5. **The sustained over-performance escalation (D15).** `exceededEscalationApplied` fires a specific `WHY_LIBRARY.exceeded_escalation` line (`:416-418`) **only when it actually moves a number** — correct, but the three-week eligibility rule itself is never stated.
6. **The on-target band width is never disclosed.** `onTargetBand = max(0.2×|goalRate| + 0.05, 0.15)` (`:812`). The user is told "on target" / "off the pace" with no band.
7. **Which trend the decision used.** The user sees a 7-day EWMA number, but the on/off-target verdict is computed from the *robust tracking* trend (`:803`). Two different smoothers, one displayed number, no disclosure.
8. **`offTargetWeeksRequired` (2 at high confidence, 3 otherwise).** Surfaced only indirectly as "N more weeks of the same trend needed before adjusting" (`:1473`); the confidence dependency is not stated.
9. **The 3-weigh-in `data_hold` counts distinct calendar days, not readings.** The copy says "at least 3 morning weights" (`:122`); a user who weighs three times in one morning will be held and will not know why.
10. **The rapid-loss threshold (−1.5 %/wk with energy ≤2) is never published.** `RAPID_LOSS_CORRECTED_COPY` says "more than 1.5%" (`whyThisTemplates.js:572`) only *after* it fires.
11. **`safetyHold` from free-text note parsing.** `parseNoteFlags` (`:444`) scans the check-in note for travel/illness/injury/missed-logging/menstrual keywords and can cap progression. The user is never told their free text was parsed, nor which words matter.
12. **Cycle-flagged weeks hold weight-based changes.** The hint explains it at the point of asking (`WeeklyCheckInScreen.js:1006`) — good — but the held-decision reason is the only later trace.
13. **The photo-corroboration confidence step (D18).** A scan can raise the displayed confidence one level. `CoachOutputScreen.photoCorroborationCaption.test.js` exists, but no user-facing copy says the caption moved because of photos.
14. **The deload dose share (60 % → 40 % by strain).** The note stays qualitative — "Ease your sets right back" (`weeklyCoach.js:1284`) — after `getAutoRegMessage`'s "half the sets" was corrected as over-promising (`whyThisTemplates.js:214-216`). The user is never told the percentage or that strain scaled it.
15. **Fail-closed suppression.** When a wellbeing read *fails*, every surface silently degrades to the neutral variant. The user sees a quieter app with no indication that a read failed.
16. **`jointPain` unanswered saves as `false`.** `WeeklyCheckInScreen.js:777` — a skipped question is recorded as an explicit "no", which can only relax a safety cap. Not disclosed.
17. **Progress-scan classification is recorded on every check-in.** `recordScanClassification` (`:793`) writes enum labels the user never sees and cannot read back.
18. **Which lift the plateau banner picked, and why that one.** `selectPlateauForBanner` ranks by longest stall, then most sets, then recency (`plateauSurfacing.js:83-89`); the banner states only the lift and the week count.
19. **Insight suppression thresholds.** Rule 1 needs ≥6 completed sessions spanning ≥3 weeks (`insightsEngine.js:79-80`); a new user simply never sees volume insights and is told nothing.
20. **`Rule 4` removal from the coach brief.** Correctly removed, but a user who saw "Muscle groups need attention" in an older build gets no explanation of its disappearance. (Historical only.)

# PART F — WELLBEING SURFACES

## F.1 Calm mode

`src/lib/wellbeing.js` (36 ln). Key `@volyume_wellbeing_mode` (`:14`); values `'calm' | 'normal' | 'unspecified'` (`:8-10`). Default `'unspecified'` = normal UX.
`getWellbeingMode` (`:19`) **swallows read errors to 'unspecified'** — which is why every safety-critical consumer reads the raw key instead.
`isCalm(mode)` (`:34`).

**Entry points:**
| Where | Action | Line |
|---|---|---|
| First run | asked once (`wellbeing.js:3-4`) | `FirstRunScreen.js` |
| Settings → Coaching | `setWellbeingMode` toggle, the **only** writer in the app | `SettingsCoachingScreen.js:11, :76, :103` |
| FAQ | "Can I make the coaching feel gentler?" | `SettingsFaqScreen.js:101` |

**Raw fail-closed readers (16 call sites):** `useWeeklyStreak.js:88`, `usePhotoSuppression.js:68`, `blockLedgerRunner.js:81`, `partners/moments.js:94`, `coachReport.js:259`, `widgets/writer.js:66`, `NutritionTargetsScreen.js:304`, `BodyMetricsScreen.js:612`, `WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:544`, `CoachOutputScreen.js:1126` and `:1491`, `WeeklyStoryScreen.js:85`, `CoachHeldHistoryScreen.js:139`, `HomeScreen.js:585, :636, :824, :881`, `YearOfLiftsScreen.js:525, :543`, `ProgressPhotosScreen.js:282`, `ProSetupCompleteScreen.js:111`, `YouScreen.js:229`.
Every one maps a failure to a **suppressing** sentinel.

## F.2 SCOFF screen

`src/screens/WellbeingCheckScreen.js`. Five questions (`SCOFF_QUESTIONS`, `:16-22`):
1. "Have you ever made yourself sick after eating because you felt uncomfortably full?"
2. "Do you worry that you have lost control over how much you eat?"
3. "Have you lost a significant amount of weight in the past three months?"
4. "Do you think of yourself as overweight even when others say you are not?"
5. "Would you say that thoughts about food take up a large part of your day?"

Answers persisted at `@volyume_scoff_answers` (`:24`); the score lands on the body profile via `saveUserBodyProfile`. All five must be answered (`:57`).
Threshold **≥2** = `scoffPositive` (`coachReport.js:264`).
Reached from YouScreen → Safety checks → "Wellbeing check" (`YouScreen.js:558`).
Theming note in-source: the colour conversion was ED-SAFETY-ADJACENT and every string plus the calm-mode/threshold logic is byte-identical; the selected/unselected colours are a plain selection indicator, **not a valence mapping** (`:38-42`).

**Engine consequence:** `scoffPositive` blocks calorie adjustment entirely (`canAdjustCals`, `weeklyCoach.js:954`), pushes a held decision "Calories held. Wellbeing screen flagged restriction concerns." (`:1464`), gates the D15 escalation (`:1541`), blocks photo corroboration (`:1709`), and sets `autoApplyHoldActive` (`:1504`).

## F.3 ED-pattern flag

`src/lib/edPatternDetector.js` (157 ln): `detectEdPatternFlag(trend, recentWeeklyHistory, goalLockAdvanced)` and `hasEdPatternCleared(trend, history)`.
Run from `weeklyCoach.js:1386-1405`. `goalLockAdvanced` raises the firing threshold from 2 signals to 3 (`:616-617`).
Clearance requires the signals to settle for **two weeks** (`:1429`).
The flag lives in the DB (`getOpenEdPatternFlag`) and is read fail-closed by `usePhotoSuppression`, `useWeeklyStreak`, `coachReport`, `partners/moments`, `blockLedgerRunner`, `widgets/writer`.

| `WELLBEING_HELPLINE` — "If you're struggling, Beat Eating Disorders UK: 0808 801 0677 (free, confidential)." | BodyMetrics confirm dialog | `wellbeing.js:16-17` → `BodyMetricsScreen.js:1000` |

# UNCERTAINTIES

1. **`MIN_WEIGH_INS` and `FIRST_CHECKIN_MIN_DAYS` numeric values** — imported from `src/lib/trialActivation.js` throughout, but I did not open that file, so the constants are referenced by name only, never by value.
2. **`PROGRESS_SCAN_ESTIMATOR_VERSION`** resolves from `assets/ml/progress_scan_bf_estimator_v1.json` (`progressScanAnalysis.js:8`). I did not open the asset, so the estimator's own internals (features, coefficients, provenance) are unverified.
3. **`computeVisualLeannessScore` / `calibrateVolyumeScore` internals** (`progressScanAnalysis.js:551, :631`) — I read the surrounding contract, constants and withhold rules but not the full ~1,300 lines of scoring maths. The weightings of the four ratios are unverified here.
4. **`progressScanVision.js` lines 200–1059** — `measureMaskSignals`, `blurScoreFromRgb`, `analyseProgressScanPhoto`. Model contract, versions, fallback and retake vocabulary are verified from the header and exported constants; the band-placement geometry is not.
5. **`formTips.js`** — I confirmed the shape (`FORM_TIPS`, exercise-name keyed, single export) and sampled ~60 entries. The **exact entry count** is unverified. Note: several entries contain en dashes ("45–75°"), which the coach-copy dash ban does not apply to since `FORM_TIPS` never passes through `clean()`.
6. **`NutritionEducationScreen.js` (355 ln)** — confirmed to exist and be reachable; its section list was not enumerated (my grep for `title:` returned only style keys, so the content is structured differently).
7. **`ProgressPhotosScreen.js` (2643 ln)** — gating, suppression, tier contract and capture routes are verified. The full section-by-section layout is not enumerated.
8. **`progressScanStore.js` `finishProgressScanSession` (`:282`, ~160 ln)** — the orchestration of analysis → persist → coach summary is not traced line by line.
9. **`progressPhotoMeta.js` / `progressPhotoTimeline.js` / `progressPhotoOrientation.js`** — consumers identified, internals not read.
10. **`getRecapData` / RecapStory screen** — referenced from `AnalyticsScreen.js:604, :836` and `coachReport.js:269`, but `RecapStory` does not appear in the `src/screens` listing under that name. **Its file location is unresolved.**
11. **`SnapshotsScreen.js`** — exists in `src/screens` but no route or consumer was traced in this lane.
12. **`buildScanEvidencePacket` (`progressScanCheckInEvidence.js:377-500`)** — the classification ladder and enums are verified from the header and `classifyAgainstWeightAndGoal`'s documented order; the packet's full field list and the `eligibleForAssessment` computation were not read line by line.
13. **`stepsAvg`** — the check-in writes `null` (`WeeklyCheckInScreen.js:773`) while the engine branches on it. I found no other writer, but I did not exhaustively search every `saveWeeklyCheckin` caller, so a second write path may exist. Flagged rather than asserted.
14. **`sessionAdjustments.js` (234 ln)** — the reason codes and messages are documented in `whyThisTemplates.js:442-524`, but the decision logic in `computeSessionAdjustments` (in `algorithms.js:1242`) was not read.
15. **`learnedRange.js` (184 ln)** — named in the comprehension matrix as a concept with no user-facing definition; its actual mechanics were not read.
16. **Free/Pro boundaries** — I recorded the gates I observed (`tier !== 'pro'` NavTile locks, `withProGuard`, `withReadOnlyProGuard`). I did not audit this lane against `proGate.js`, so a surface I marked LIVE may carry a tier gate I did not see.
17. **`GLOSSARY` orphan claims (`mesocycle`, `macros`, `strengthLevel`, `autoregulation`, `redS`)** rest on a `grep -rn "GLOSSARY\."` sweep across `src` excluding tests. A call site using destructuring (`const { macros } = GLOSSARY`) would not have matched. I saw no such pattern, but the sweep is not proof.
18. **The `PR` concept having no glossary entry** is asserted from the 31-entry list above; there is no `GLOSSARY.pr`. Whether a PR tooltip exists as a hard-coded inline string somewhere (rather than via GLOSSARY) was not exhaustively checked.

# CHAPTER B2 — SETTINGS, PROFILE, ONBOARDING, AUTH, CONSENT, SUBSCRIPTION (covers PARTS 10, 18; auth/consent/subscription machines of 14)

# VOLYUME FULL PRODUCT MAP -- LANE B2

## Settings, Profile, Onboarding, Auth, Consent, Subscription/Tier, Payments

Read-only archaeology of `/home/user/ADPhysique` at `git HEAD = 1267c568`
("Record the full product map campaign and its recovery path"), working tree
clean. Every claim below carries a repo-relative reference. British English
throughout.

### Evidence key

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **LIVE** | Reachable and effective for a normal user in a production build today. |
| **LIVE-CONDITIONAL** | Live only when the named condition holds (tier, platform, recorded sex, device capability, permission). |
| **INTERNAL** | Exists and works, but is not a user-facing product surface (support gestures, seeded review accounts, dev-only paths). |
| **LEGACY-UNREACHABLE** | Code exists and would work, but nothing in the shipped navigation or UI reaches it. |
| **PLANNED-DOCUMENTED-ONLY** | Described in code/comments as intended, not wired. |
| **UNCERTAIN** | Recorded in the UNCERTAINTIES section; never guessed at. |

### Two structural facts that govern the whole lane

1. **Preference sync is allow-by-prefix, not allow-list.** `src/lib/sync.js:1300`
   `shouldSyncPref(key)` returns true for **every** `@volyume_` AsyncStorage key
   that does not match one of the `PREF_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` at
   `src/lib/sync.js:1255-1298`. `_pushAllUserPrefs` (`src/lib/sync.js:1327`)
   enumerates `AsyncStorage.getAllKeys()` and upserts every survivor into the
   cloud `user_prefs` table; `_pullUserPrefs` (`src/lib/sync.js:1767`) mirrors
   them back with **cloud-wins, no per-key updated_at comparison** (its own
   docstring says so at `src/lib/sync.js:1762-1764`). So the default answer to
   "is this setting synced?" is **yes**, and the interesting cases are the
   exclusions. The code comments this model as deliberately fail-open
   (`src/lib/sync.js:1288-1292`).
2. **Tier is binary and server-owned.** `src/lib/proGate.js:28`
   `PRO_BETA_ACTIVE = false`; `_resolveTier` (`src/lib/proGate.js:39-53`) maps
   `trial_state` to `'pro' | 'free'`. `tier` is excluded from the profile push
   payload entirely (`src/lib/sync/tables/profiles.js:16-19`: "the server owns
   tier exclusively via the upgrade_tier RPC + play-billing-rtdn webhook").

# A. EVERY USER-CONFIGURABLE SETTING

## A.0 Where settings live (the map before the table)

`src/screens/SettingsScreen.js` is a pure row-list hub (148 lines, no toggles of
its own since CP-6 moved the inline "Workout & units" block out, see its header
comment at lines 13-16). It links to eleven sub-pages plus three Pro-conditional
shortcuts:

| Row | Destination | Visibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account | `SettingsAccount` | always |
| Profile | `SettingsProfile` | always |
| Coaching | `SettingsCoaching` | always |
| Workout & units | `SettingsWorkout` | always |
| Nutrition targets | `NutritionTargets` | `tier === 'pro'` (`SettingsScreen.js:59`) |
| Per-day targets | `PerDayTargets` | `tier === 'pro'` (`:71`) |
| Dietary needs | `SettingsDietary` | `tier === 'pro'` (`:79`) |
| Notifications and reminders | `NotificationSettings` | always |
| Coaching reminders | `CoachingReminders` | `tier === 'pro'` (`:93`) |
| Display and accessibility | `SettingsDisplay` | always |
| Home screen widget | alert only (instructions, no setting) | always |
| Health provider | `SettingsHealth` | `isHealthAvailable()` (`:119`) |
| Your data | `SettingsData` | always |
| Privacy and legal | `SettingsPrivacy` | always |
| Help and about | `SettingsAbout` | always |

A further set of genuine settings live **outside** the Settings tree entirely:
in the diary (water target), the meal plan (meals/day, variety, peri-workout),
the progress-photo capture sheet (camera facing, timer), the exercise/volume
charts (window + metric), the active workout (per-side logging), the Coach tab
(goal lock, wellbeing check), the Plans tab (block-advice snooze), and the
athlete profile (avatar). These are flagged in §A.3.

| Goal lock | Coach > Goal lock (`YouScreen.js:550-554` -> `GoalLockConsentScreen.js`) | Radio, 2 | `standard` | `standard` \| `advanced` | `user_body_profile.goal_lock_advanced` (migration in `database.js:1066-1067`) | **Raises the ED-pattern threshold**: standard is the more protective 2-signal setting; advanced is an explicit opt-in for people with prior experience or a coach (`ProOnboardingScreen.js:722-731`, `GoalLockConsentScreen.js:20-28`) | Coach copy | Local SQLite column; `user_body_profile` is in the wipe/backup table lists (`database.js:4811, 5193, 8173`) | no | **ED-SAFETY.** The aggressive-cuts interstitial was removed from onboarding (founder 2026-05-29); everyone starts on the protective setting and must deliberately opt in from the Coach tab | signed-in user | `setGoalLockAdvanced` / `getGoalLockAdvanced` (`database.js:8096-8110`) |
| Wellbeing check (SCOFF) | Coach > Wellbeing check (`YouScreen.js:556-560` -> `WellbeingCheckScreen.js`) | 5 yes/no questions + calm-mode choice | unanswered | 0-5 score | `@volyume_scoff_answers`, `userProfile.scoffScore`, `user_body_profile.scoff_score` (`database.js:562`) | Feeds `edPatternDetector` | Offers calm mode and Beat UK signposting (`wellbeing.js:16-17`) | **Raw answers are explicitly EXCLUDED from sync** (`sync.js:1293`, pinned at `syncPrefExclusions.test.js:66`); the derived score rides the profile/body-profile | raw answers yes | **ED-SAFETY CRITICAL.** The screen promises the answers stay device-only, and the exclusion is what keeps that promise | none | `WellbeingCheckScreen.js:16-77` |

## A.2 Prose: what actually happens when the complex ones change

**Biological sex.** `changeSex` writes to two places in sequence: the store
profile blob (`saveLocalProfile`, which also fires a `syncAll` on a signed-in
session, `useAppStore.js:288-295`) and the SQLite `user_body_profile` row,
merging over the existing row so height and DOB survive (`SettingsProfileScreen.js:166-170`).
On failure it reverts the local chip state (`:171-173`). The change is
**immediate** for anything that reads sex live (the cycle-tracking row, the FFM
floor's sex term), **on next sync** for the cloud profile, and **on the next
weekly coach run** for the actual nutrition targets: the screen deliberately does
not recompute targets, per founder direction (`:159-161`), and the confirmation
dialog says exactly that (`:180-183`). The floor itself is not deferred: the
calorie floor is re-enforced inside `coachApply` on every apply.

**Calm mode.** `setWellbeingMode('calm')` writes a single AsyncStorage string
(`wellbeing.js:28-32`). It takes effect the moment any consumer next reads it,
and consumers read it **fail-closed** (for example `NutritionTargetsScreen.js:301`
reads the raw flag rather than the helper, and `BodyMetricsScreen.js:515-520`
treats the recomp reframe as suppressed until the async safety reads resolve).
Because `coachAutonomy` is overridden by any safety hold, turning calm mode on
also forces confirm-first on coach adjustments regardless of the autonomy mode
(`SettingsCoachingScreen.js:217-222`).

**Autonomy.** Purely an apply-control preference on a local-only profile field.
It changes **who confirms** a coach adjustment, never the decision or its
reason. Every mode shows the same decision and the same reason. A safety hold
(deload, poor recovery, safety hold, FFM floor, ED flag, rapid loss, calm mode)
always forces confirm-first, so "Coached" is never a promise to bypass a hold
(D16, `:217-222`). It is read on the next coach output render, not retroactively.

**Session readiness check.** Stored inverted: the key
`@volyume_intent_prompt_off` exists only when the ask is OFF (`:96-99`). The Home
start path re-reads it fresh each session (`HomeScreen.js:2206`), so the change
lands on the **next session start**, not immediately. With it off there is no
readiness input at all, so session adjustments never fire; the code is explicit
that absent input is never filled in with a guess (`:86-90`).

**Rest finished alert.** Uniquely among the workout prefs, this one acts
**mid-rest**: turning it off cancels the already-scheduled OS notification, and
turning it on reschedules for the remaining rest if a timer is running
(`useAppStore.js:1704-1717`). There is also a hydration-order guard: if the pref
loads as `false` after a rest already started under the default-on value,
`loadWorkoutPrefs` cancels the stale schedule (`:1664-1674`).

**Reduce motion.** The Settings switch writes `reduceMotionUserPref`; the
EFFECTIVE value every consumer reads is `accessibility.reduceMotion`, recomputed
as `systemReduceMotion || userPref` at both write sites (`:1957-1959` and
`:1973-1979`). `systemReduceMotion` mirrors the OS setting live via
`AccessibilityInfo` from `App.js` and is **never persisted**. There is a
one-time migration for installs that pre-date the split: the legacy
`reduceMotion` field seeds `reduceMotionUserPref` on first load (`:1935-1946`).

**Quiet hours.** Persisting a change does two things: it saves the window, then
**re-lays everything already scheduled** so existing reminders are recomputed
against the new window rather than the one they were laid under
(`NotificationSettingsScreen.js:512-531`). Schedules that would land inside the
window are pushed to the first minute after it ends, with correct midnight-wrap
handling (`quietHours.js:90-124`).

**Per-day calorie offsets.** Immediate in the diary display, and **invisible to
the engine forever**. The module header is unambiguous: the stored nutrition
target is never written; the coach's 7-day rolling average, the rapid-loss gate
and the ED-pattern detector all keep seeing the real target
(`perDayTargets.js:6-13`). Offsets are kcal deltas so they auto-track base-target
changes, and they are hard-clamped against the sex floor and the FFM floor at
resolution time. They apply only on an otherwise-plain day; a refeed, carb cycle
or banked day takes precedence.

**Allergen excludes.** Written through `setAllergenExcludes` specifically so the
per-field timestamp is stamped. `setMealPlanPrefs` deliberately refuses to carry
`mealPlanExcludeTags` because an unstamped write would never push and could be
silently reverted by the next pull (`useAppStore.js:1849-1854`). Effect on plan
generation is immediate on the next generate/swap; on the cloud, on the next
sync.

**Cardio logging off.** Hides the cardio surfaces. It does **not** delete
anything: logged history is kept, just not shown (`SettingsCoachingScreen.js:31-33`).

**App lock.** The only setting stored in `expo-secure-store` rather than
AsyncStorage, because it is a security flag, and it is per DEVICE not per account
(`biometricLock.js:11-16`). The enable path re-checks biometric availability LIVE
immediately before writing, so a user can never arm a lock they cannot satisfy
(`SettingsPrivacyScreen.js:70-77`); the switch stays interactive to turn OFF even
if biometrics later disappear. The gate wraps `MainTabs` only, so it never runs
against Welcome, Article 9 consent or the onboarding stacks (`biometricLock.js:37-43`).

**Switch to Free.** Writes only the local tier. The alert is honest about the
consequence: everything logged stays, past coach decisions, check-ins, training
blocks and PRs remain readable, and only new weekly coaching adjustments stop
(`SettingsAccountScreen.js:47-50`). The server tier is untouched, so the next
`refreshTierFromCloud` will restore Pro if the subscription is still live.

## A.3 Settings that materially change behaviour but are HARD TO FIND

Flagged for the founder, ordered by how much behaviour they move relative to how
buried they are.

1. **Goal lock (advanced ED threshold)** -- Coach tab > Goal lock, not in
   Settings at all (`YouScreen.js:550-554`). It raises the ED-pattern detection
   threshold. This is the single most safety-consequential user-facing control
   in the app and it is two taps off the main Settings tree.
2. **Wellbeing check / calm mode entry point** -- also Coach tab
   (`YouScreen.js:556-560`), while the calm-mode toggle itself is in
   Settings > Coaching. Two doors to one concept, in two different trees.
3. **Session readiness check** -- Settings > Coaching. Turning it off silently
   disables the entire session-adjustment feature. The row copy says "Off.
   Sessions start straight away", which does not say that adjustments stop.
4. **Autonomy** -- Settings > Coaching, Pro only. Changes who applies weekly
   changes. Buried below Cardio logging and Coaching tone in a scrolling card.
5. **Per-day calorie offsets** -- a whole Settings row (Pro) whose effect looks
   like a target change but is display-only. Easy to mistake for a coaching
   input.
6. **Water daily target** -- editable only by tapping the water VALUE in the
   diary (`DiaryScreen.js:2054-2066`). No Settings row, no visible affordance
   beyond an accessibility hint.
7. **Meal plan meals/day, variety, peri-workout, fat convention** -- only inside
   the meal plan's own prefs sheet, and they are local-only profile fields that
   do NOT sync, so they are lost on a device change.
8. **Progress scan camera facing and timer** -- only inside the photo capture
   sheet. They affect Volyume Score consistency.
9. **Per-side (unilateral) logging** -- armed by a one-time in-workout prompt per
   exercise, with no central list to review or undo it. It changes what rep
   count the engine sees (the lower side).
10. **Skip name on label scans** -- hidden in Settings > Your data rather than a
    food/nutrition surface, and Pro-only.
11. **Getting-started nudges** -- under a "Getting started" heading in
    Notifications, easy to miss.
12. **Rest-alert exactness (Android 12+)** -- a row that only appears when the
    grant is missing AND the rest alert is on.
13. **DebugLog** -- 7 taps on the version value within 3 seconds in
    Settings > Help and about (`SettingsAboutScreen.js:19-20, 92-129`).
    Deliberately unadvertised, INTERNAL, support-only.
14. **Hide exact scan numbers** -- defaults ON and has no control at all
    (see A.1.12).

# B. ONBOARDING

## B.1 RootNavigator routing order (`src/navigation/RootNavigator.js:1565-1614`)

`renderNavigator()` decides in this exact order:

1. `if (!user) return <WelcomeStack />` (`:1576`). The gate is on being SIGNED
   IN, not on tier. Keying it on `!tier` previously parked a signed-in user on
   the login screen forever (`:1566-1575`).
2. `if (user && !user.isLocal && !firstRunComplete && !healthConsentChecked)
   return <SplashScreen />` (`:1589`). A blocking resolver: a brand-new Pro-path
   account has `tier = null` and `firstRunComplete = false`, so without this the
   free FirstRunStack would flash before the consent gate and the trial grant
   land (ONB-001/ONB-002, `:1577-1588`).
3. **Article 9 gate** (`:1604-1606`): shown when `healthConsent === false`, OR
   when a NEW user (`!firstRunComplete`) has UNRESOLVED consent (`null`) after a
   transient read failure. This is the fail-closed rule: previously a `null` fell
   straight through to onboarding, so a user processed health data with no
   recorded consent, and a Pro-intent signup landed in the free stack because the
   cascade only fires once consent is granted (`:1591-1603`). A RETURNING user
   with a null read is not re-prompted.
4. `if (!firstRunComplete) return tier === 'pro' ? <ProOnboardingStack /> :
   <FirstRunStack />` (`:1607-1609`).
5. `return <LockedMainTabs />` (`:1613`), which is `MainTabs` wrapped in the
   opt-in biometric app-lock overlay.

The header comment at `:1560-1564` states the intended sequence: consent is where
`start_cascade` grants the 14-day Pro trial, which sets `tier='pro'` for a new
user, and that is why step 4 branches on tier.

## B.2 The stacks

- **`WelcomeStack`** (`:673-683`): `Welcome`, `QuizTraining`, `PlanPreview`,
  `Login`.
- **`FirstRunStack`** (`:686-701`): `FirstRunBranch`, `FreeStarter`,
  `PlanLibrary`, `PlanDetail`, `ActiveWorkout`.
- **`Article9ConsentStack`** (`:709-717`): `Article9Consent`, `PrivacyPolicy`.
- **`ProOnboardingStack`** (`:721-735`): `ProOnboarding`, `PlanLibrary`,
  `PlanDetail`, `ActiveWorkout`, `ProSetupComplete`, `NutritionEducation`,
  `Methodology`.

## B.3 Welcome (`src/screens/WelcomeScreen.js`) -- LIVE

Trial-first by founder decision OB-1 (2026-07-02, `:20-26`). ONE CTA. The old
Free/Pro pair was a dead control: both cards routed to the same sign-up and the
intent param had no consumer. The card states "The full app, free for 14 days",
lists four trial bullets (`:28-33`), states what stays free afterwards
(`:35-40`), and shows the **store's localised monthly price via `usePlayPrices`
or drops the figure entirely** (`:120-124`) -- never a hardcoded price (PLAY-002).
`startTrial()` navigates to `Login` with `intent: 'pro_signup'` (`:75`).

**Quiz-first front door is OFF.** `ONBOARDING_QUIZ_FIRST = false`
(`lib/onboarding/quizFlow.js:24`), turned off by founder decision 2026-06-26
because a free-style quiz on the Pro CTA broke the Pro flow. So `QuizScreen`,
`PlanPreviewScreen`, `lib/onboarding/planPreview.js`, `QUIZ_STEPS` and the
`onboardingQuiz` store slice are **LEGACY-UNREACHABLE behind a flag** (reversible
by flipping one constant). The privacy property of that path, if ever re-enabled,
is that pre-account answers live only in JS process memory: never AsyncStorage,
never SQLite, no device id, no network (`quizFlow.js:12-16`,
`useAppStore.js:1153-1168`).

## B.4 Free first-run (`src/screens/FirstRunScreen.js` + `FreeStarterScreen`) -- LIVE

Two steps only.

1. **Name** (`FirstRunScreen.js:75-89`). Mandatory (`hasName` gates the button
   at `:96`). Gym weights are kg-only, no unit choice (`:33-34`). Saves
   `{ units:'kg', firstName }` to the profile, then navigates to `FreeStarter`
   with `fromFirstRun: true` (`:49-54`).
2. **FreeStarter micro-quiz** (`lib/onboarding/freeStarter.js:24-52`): three
   plain questions -- goal (`build_muscle` / `get_stronger` / `general_fitness`),
   equipment (`full_gym` / `dumbbell` / `home`), days per week (2/3/4). Visibly
   skippable (`FirstRunScreen.js:100-107`). It calls `completeFirstRun` itself
   after a plan is installed or the user skips (`:52-53`).

The scoring is pure and deterministic with two hard rules, both tested: only
difficulty-0 plans are ever candidates, and equipment is a hard FILTER not a
score bump, so a home trainee is never handed a barbell plan
(`freeStarter.js:9-14`, `isStarterCandidate` `:73-80`). Ties break by plan name
so the result never depends on arrival order (`:143-150`).

## B.5 Pro onboarding wizard (`src/screens/ProOnboardingScreen.js`, 2355 lines) -- LIVE

`TOTAL_STEPS = 6` (`:65`), labels
`['Account','Baseline','Body composition','Training week','Targets','Check-in rhythm']`
(`:66`). Step 2 was split into 2 and 3 in L04-6 because it had bundled up to
seven fields at the highest-abandon-risk moment (`:58-64`).

### Step 1 -- Account
OAuth buttons only in this screen (`handleOAuthOnboarding`, `:600-641`). On
success it sets `proOnboardingAccountCreated` in the STORE, not screen state, so
it survives the wizard stack being unmounted by the consent gate
(`useAppStore.js:206-213`). **Apple's returned given name pre-fills the first-name
field** when Apple provides it (App Review Guideline 4, `:614-621`). An
already-authenticated user auto-advances past step 1 (`:456-483`), which is what
stops the OAuth loop (auth -> splash -> step 1).

### Step 2 -- Baseline (`:1130-1367`). ALL MANDATORY.
`canContinue` (`:1144`) and `advanceFrom2` (`:655-694`) enforce the same rules
through shared resolvers:

| Field | Rule | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First name | non-empty after trim | `:656-659` |
| **Biological sex** | must be exactly `male` or `female`. **No default: `useState(null)`** | `:660-665`, `:357` |
| Body weight | parses to 30-300 kg; starts EMPTY, example lives in the placeholder | `:666-679`, `:340-343` |
| Age | 13-100; starts EMPTY | `:680-683`, `:359` |
| Height | `isValidHeightCm`, band `MIN_HEIGHT_CM = 120` upward; starts BLANK | `:684-692`, `:139-140`, `:367-369` |

**The sex gate** (OB-5/F11) is the most heavily defended thing in the wizard.
`SEX_OPTIONS` and `ACCEPTED_SEX_VALUES` are derived from one another
(`:115-117`) so the picker and the validator can never drift. A restored draft
with an invalid sex **clamps the step back to 2**:
`setStep((s) => Math.max(s, sexValid ? draft.step : Math.min(draft.step, 2)))`
(`:542`). Five source-level regression guards pin all of this in
`src/lib/__tests__/proOnboarding.sexGate.test.js:25-56`, including that the state
starts `null` and that the Continue button is genuinely `disabled`, not merely
alert-on-tap. A parallel suite pins the height gate
(`proOnboarding.heightGate.test.js`).

The rationale is recorded in the source: sex drives the ED calorie floor
(1500 male / 1200 female) and BMR, so a silent `male` default could mis-floor a
female (`:353-357`). Similarly, the old prefills of 80 kg and age 30 were removed
because they were real editable values that validated untouched, so plausible
calorie targets could be computed on someone else's body (`:337-342`), and the
old `175 cm` seed was removed for the same reason (`:363-368`).

### Step 3 -- Body composition (`:1375-1442`). ENTIRELY OPTIONAL.
Body fat % and its source (`Best estimate` / `BIA` / `Caliper` / `DEXA`,
`:118-124`). `advanceFrom3` carries no gate at all, by design (`:696-703`). When
a MEASURED source is given the engine uses the lean-mass (Katch-McArdle) BMR
path, matching Nutrition Targets, so onboarding and the targets screen compute
the SAME maintenance; without it onboarding used to under-estimate maintenance by
about 300 kcal (`:344-350`).

### Step 4 -- Training week (`:1445-1527`). MANDATORY: experience, session length, equipment.
`canContinue = !!experience && !!sessionLengthMinutes && !!equipment` (`:1446`),
enforced again in `advanceFrom4` (`:705-716`). Days per week defaults to 4
(`DEFAULT_DAYS_PER_WEEK`, `:106`) and is not itself gated.

### Step 5 -- Targets (`:1531-1717`). MANDATORY: training goal and phase.
`trainingGoal` defaults to `'general'` (not competing) with an optional
"Competing in a category?" dropdown (`:376-378`); `trainingPhase` defaults to
`'lean_gain'` deliberately, so the screen lands on the most common phase rather
than an empty greyed picker (`:379-381`). Weak points are capped at 3 and are
division-scoped: changing division drops any muscle the new division does not
offer (`changeGoal` `:409-413`, `toggleWeakPoint` `:415-421`). Protein override
is optional; left null the engine picks `advanced` for physique divisions and
`optimised` for everyone else (`:390-397`).

**The aggressive-cuts goal-lock interstitial was REMOVED from onboarding**
(founder 2026-05-29, `:722-731`): it fired for anyone picking a competition
division even when lean-gaining. Everyone now keeps the more protective 2-signal
ED threshold; the advanced opt-in lives on the Goal lock screen under Coach.

### Step 6 -- Check-in rhythm (`:1721-1957`). MANDATORY: recovery rating.
`canContinue = !!recoveryRating` (`:1722`). Also collects morning-weight reminder
hour (`HOURS`), weekly check-in day (`DAYS`), and a Cardio availability switch
defaulting ON (`:430-436`). Both reminders are labelled "Part of your coaching"
rather than "Required" -- tone only, they remain non-optional (FR-4/D7,
`:1826-1829`).

### What Step 6 (`advanceFrom6`, `:788-1085`) seeds downstream

In order:

1. **Notification prefs** written to `@volyume_notification_prefs` BEFORE the
   permission dialog, so denying the permission does not discard the chosen
   check-in day (OB-2, `:814-820`). On `granted`: morning weight notification,
   evening weight backstop, check-in reminder with
   `earliestMs = now + FIRST_CHECKIN_MIN_DAYS * 86400000` so the first reminder
   can never invite a brand-new user into a locked "wait a few days" screen
   (`:821-829`), plus the missed-check-in follow-up pair.
2. **Units**: `setUnits('kg')`, `setBodyWeightUnits(localBWUnits)` (`:846-847`).
3. **A re-validation gate** (`:855-869`): if sex, weight, height or age fail
   validation at this point it **sends the user back to step 2** with
   "Volyume will not build targets from fallback body data".
4. **Nutrition targets** via `calculateNutritionTargets(buildNutritionEngineInputs({...}))`
   (`:884-897`) -- the shared builder exists so onboarding and "Update Your Plan"
   can never feed the engine different shapes.
5. **Profile merge** (`:906-943`): firstName, units, bodyWeightUnits, sex, age,
   heightCm, weightKg, trainingGoal, trainingPhase, goalPhase, phaseStartedAt,
   `goalStartDate` (set only when the phase is a cut, so a bulk is never
   misread as a long-running cut by `weeklyCoach`'s diet-break timing,
   `:902-905`), cardioEnabled, trainingFreq bucket, daysPerWeek, experience,
   sessionLengthMinutes, equipment, recoveryRating, planWeakPoints,
   proteinApproach, bodyFatPct, bodyFatSource, goal.
6. **Body metric log + morning weight seed** (`:947-965`): the morning-weight
   seed exists so the weekly check-in gate (3 readings in the last 7 days) counts
   enrolment day.
7. **`user_body_profile`** (`:967-978`): sex, heightCm, dateOfBirth, primaryGoal.
8. **Nutrition targets** to `@volyume_nutrition_targets` AND SQLite (`:980-1003`).
9. **Plan auto-generation** (`generateAndSavePlan`, `:1005-1043`) from
   `{experience, daysPerWeek, sessionLengthMinutes, equipment, trainingGoal,
   trainingPhase, planWeakPoints, recoveryRating}`. On failure the profile and
   targets are still saved, the staged sequence aborts instantly (no celebratory
   hold, no completion tick) and the user still reaches `ProSetupComplete`.
   Raw error text is never shown (D88, `:1035-1040`).

**Landmark seeding.** `recoveryRating` and `experience` are exactly the two
inputs to `computeLandmarks(experience, recoveryRating, nutritionPhase, age)`
(`planEngine.js:103-105`), which sets the MEV/MRV/MAV volume landmarks. That is
why step 6's hint says "Be honest here. This sets how much volume your plan
includes, so it can protect your recovery" (`:1808-1809`).

**The staged build sequence** (COMP-013, `:100-107`, `:760-786`) shows four
honest stage lines mapped to real `_generatePlanInner` phases, 800 ms dwell each
(3.2 s total), and never completes before the real work does. Reduce Motion skips
it entirely and keeps the plain button spinner (`:816-820`).

## B.6 Draft persistence (`src/lib/proOnboardingDraft.js`) -- LIVE

Per-user AsyncStorage draft `@volyume_pro_onboarding_draft_<uid>`, version 1,
debounce 600 ms, persistable steps 2-6 only (step 1 is auth-owned)
(`:16-27`). `parseDraft` never invents values, so a draft saved with `sex: null`
restores with `sex: null` and Continue stays disabled exactly as on a fresh run
(`:10-12`). Malformed drafts return null and the wizard starts fresh (`:42-55`).
The draft is cleared when the wizard completes, on both the success and
plan-failed paths (`:1046-1048`). **Excluded from sync** as transient in-progress
answers including sex and goals (`sync.js:1298`, pinned at
`syncPrefExclusions.test.js:73`).

## B.7 Completion

`completeFirstRun` (`useAppStore.js:1124-1151`) writes `FIRST_RUN_KEY`, the
per-uid cache `FIRST_RUN_KEY_PFX + uid`, sets `firstRunComplete: true` and
`proOnboardingAccountCreated: false`, and fire-and-forget mirrors
`first_run_complete: true` to `users_profile`.

`resetFirstRun` (`:1093-1110`) forces the navigator back into the onboarding
stack for a Free -> Pro upgrade, and **refuses while a workout is in progress**
(`{ ok:false, error:'workout_in_progress' }`) because flipping the flag would
unmount MainTabs and lose the live set log.

# C. AUTH AND IDENTITY

## C.1 Methods -- all ungated

| Method | Platform | Where | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in with Apple | iOS only | `LoginScreen`, `ProOnboardingScreen` step 1, `ProUpgradeScreen` | `components/auth/OAuthButtons.js:40-70`. Uses Apple's OWN `AppleAuthenticationButton` (Guideline 4.8) in WHITE style on dark backgrounds per Apple's HIG, with a styled fallback if the native component is unavailable |
| Continue with Google | Android only (`Platform.OS !== 'ios'`) | as above | `OAuthButtons.js:71-86`. The comment records why: the iOS Google OAuth client id is not wired, and iOS still satisfies Guideline 4.8 through Apple + email |
| Email + password (sign in AND sign up in one toggled form) | both | `LoginScreen` only | `LoginScreen.js:11, 16-22, 28-31, 207-282`. Re-added by founder 2026-07-21 for App Review demo accounts and users who prefer email |

**Important divergence to flag**: email/password exists **only on
`LoginScreen`**. Both `ProOnboardingScreen` step 1 (`:439-443`) and
`ProUpgradeScreen` (`:92-94`) still carry the 2026-07-01 "OAuth only, the email +
password path was removed" comment and render OAuth buttons only. So a user
entering via the wizard's own account step or via the upgrade modal has no email
option; a user entering via Welcome -> Login does.

Email sign-up with confirmation ON returns a user but no session, and the screen
says "Check your email to confirm your account, then sign in"
(`LoginScreen.js:142-147`). Error text is mapped to calm sentences and never
shows raw provider text (`:126-141`). Password has a show/hide control (A5,
`:32-35, 250-262`).

## C.2 No anonymous mode

- `initLocalUser` was **deleted** from the store; the comment cites
  `IDENTITY_AND_OWNERSHIP_LOCKED.md` rule 1 and states every user must sign up to
  a real account via WelcomeScreen -> LoginScreen, and that the RootNavigator
  bootstrap no longer auto-restores a local-only user (`useAppStore.js:267-271`).
- `RootNavigator.js:1571-1575`: "Identity is cloud-only (no anonymous mode per
  IDENTITY_AND_OWNERSHIP_LOCKED.md), so a non-null `user` means signed in."
- `LoginScreen.js:285` carries the same lock reference.
- **Mechanical guard**: `scripts/check-identity-invariant.sh` greps `SET user_id`
  across `src/` excluding tests and fails unless each site is annotated
  `LOCKED-OK` within the preceding lines.
- **Regression tests**: `src/lib/__tests__/identityGate.proOnboarding.test.js`,
  and the store still exports `generateUUID` specifically so the identity
  anti-patterns test can call it through the store (`useAppStore.js:178-181`).
- `user.isLocal` branches survive throughout (sign-out copy, delete copy,
  navigator gates). They are dead-but-guarded paths, not a reachable mode.

## C.3 Session restore (`useAppStore.restoreSessionFromCloud`, `:783-984`)

Optimistic-UI: route INSTANTLY from local cues, then sync from the cloud in the
background. No splash, no blocking cloud read on the routing path (`:765-769`).

Three cues in priority order (`:771-777`):
1. Per-uid cache `@volyume_first_run_complete_<uid>` -- exact answer from a prior
   session.
2. `session.user.created_at` age. Older than 60 s means assume returning, route
   to MainTabs.
3. Default: younger than 60 s means a fresh signup, route to the wizard.

Only a cue-2 heuristic guess may be flipped back to the wizard by the cloud read;
a cue-1 cache hit is never flipped, because that would be the wizard-flash bug
(A2-021, `:810-816`, `:963-983`).

Anti-cross-user guard (AUTH-2 / I5): `staleUid()` is re-checked before every
state write after every await, so a late-resolving restore for user A cannot
write over user B (`:789-797`, `:821-822`, `:902-903`, `:952-954`).

The cloud read is bounded at 10 s and tries the profile select WITH `sex` first,
falling back to the proven sex-less select on ANY read error, so routing is never
coupled to whether migrate_094 has been applied (`:869-894`).

`noteSignupPendingOnboarding(uid)` (`:1119-1122`) seeds the per-uid flag to
`'false'` at signUp time so a slow email confirmation cannot let the created_at
heuristic mistake a brand-new user for a returning one.

## C.4 Sign-out (`clearAuthStateForSignOut`, `useAppStore.js:313-584`)

The locked design is "sign-out wipes local SQLite": every sign-in is a fresh
cloud pull, so two users on one device can never see each other's data
(`:298-301`).

Sequence:
1. Telemetry `sign_out`, cancel the debounced sync timer.
2. **Push-first safety**: `syncAll({triggeredBy:'sign_out'})` bounded at 20 s,
   with a retry loop while the runner lock is contended (up to 6 attempts inside
   the same budget) because a single attempt sent every user who had just edited
   something to the scary "Sync incomplete" prompt (founder device report
   2026-07-13, `:362-394`).
3. Abort with `{ok:false, reason:'unsynced'}` on `status==='error'`,
   `status==='skipped'`, or `errored_count > 0`. It deliberately does NOT block
   on `pending` -- that depth is the live retry queue and its data is covered by
   the same cycle's full push (`:404-424`).
4. **Delete-tombstone drain** (AC-04): the push is UPSERT-only and cannot express
   a DELETE, so `drainSyncQueue` runs and sign-out is refused while any delete op
   remains unshipped, or a workout deleted offline would resurrect on next
   sign-in (`:425-455`).
5. `setSignOutWiping(true)` (`sync/signOutGuard.js`) so a lifecycle sync trigger
   cannot pull cloud rows back into the DB about to be wiped, then
   `whenSyncIdle({timeoutMs:5000})` (`:469-485`).
6. `unregisterPushToken(prevUid)` (`:487-498`).
7. `wipeAllUserDataWithRetry(prevUid)`; on failure, lower the guard and return
   `{ok:false, reason:'wipe_failed', step}` so the alert names the failing step
   (`:504-526`).
8. `AsyncStorage.clear()` (`:532-537`) and SecureStore token deletion for both
   the modern `sb-<projectref>-auth-token` and legacy `supabase.auth.token`
   (`:543-554`).
9. Reset store state and cancel any scheduled rest-end notification (`:556-582`).

UI layer (`useAccountActions.handleSignOut`): blocks sign-out mid-workout
(`:60-67`); on `unsynced` offers an explicit "Sign out anyway" escape hatch
(AUTH-5, `:118-146`); retries the cloud `signOut()` once (AUTH-3/I4, `:87-95`);
**never reloads the JS bundle on any platform** because `Updates.reloadAsync()`
after a native modal leaves a permanent black screen, first on iOS TestFlight and
then reproduced on Android (`:97-105`).

## C.5 Account deletion

`performDeleteAccount` (`useAccountActions.js:196-380`):
- Primary: Supabase Edge Function `delete-account` with `{reason, app_version,
  platform}` so `account_deletions_log` gets a rich row.
- Fallback: RPC `delete_user_data` (v3, migrate_008, tolerates missing tables).
  The RPC cannot reach `auth.users`, so it sets `authRemovalPending = true` and
  also calls `record_rpc_fallback_deletion` so the scheduled server sweeper
  (migration 098) finishes the auth-row removal even if the user never signs in
  again (`:269-282`).
- **CRITICAL abort**: if the cloud wipe failed, do NOT sign out or wipe locally.
  The old behaviour left the user logged out locally with the cloud account
  intact, and on next sign-in they were dumped into the main app because
  `first_run_complete=true` still lived in the cloud profile they thought they
  had deleted (`:288-302`).
- Then local `wipeAllUserDataWithRetry`, `clearAuthStateForSignOut`,
  `AsyncStorage.clear()` (needed because three legacy keys lack the `@` prefix,
  `:312-322`), the pending marker written AFTER the clear so it survives
  (`:324-329`), and a belt-and-braces SecureStore wipe (`:331-347`).
- Honest partial-success alert when credentials could not be removed (`:349-362`).

`src/lib/deletionRetry.js`: per-uid marker `@volyume_deletion_auth_pending_<uid>`.
`RootNavigator`'s auth listener **AWAITS** `retryPendingAuthDeletion` at the TOP
of the sign-in pipeline (Wave-3 review fix: it used to run alongside restore and
could silently erase a just-restored account mid-session). While a marker exists
for that uid the sign-in never proceeds into restore/sync; the navigator signs
the session out with a calm explanation either way (`deletionRetry.js:13-20`).
One attempt per JS lifetime (`:59-61`). Tested in
`src/lib/__tests__/deletionRetry.test.js`.

## C.6 Biometric lock

See A.1.6. The gate is `useAppLockGate()` wired into `LockedMainTabs` in
`RootNavigator`, scoped to `MainTabs` only. Because the pref can only ever be
switched on from Settings, which lives inside MainTabs, the hook never gates
Welcome, Article 9 consent or onboarding: auth and consent are untouched and this
is a purely additive gate in front of already-signed-in, already-consented,
already-onboarded content (`biometricLock.js:37-43`). Tested in
`src/lib/__tests__/biometricLock.test.js`.

# D. ARTICLE 9 CONSENT AND PRIVACY

## D.1 The gate (`src/screens/Article9ConsentScreen.js`)

Copy is compliance-locked in `docs/PRIVACY_CONSENT_LOCKED.md` (`:20`). Consent
version pinned in the audit trail as `CONSENT_VERSION = '2026-07-04'` (`:37`),
because Art 7(1)/EDPB expect the record to capture WHICH consent copy was
presented, not just the app version (`:33-36`).

`handleContinue` (`:59-173`), in order:
1. Upsert a `users_profile` row if missing, because both
   `record_health_consent` (an UPDATE) and `start_cascade` (raises "profile not
   found") need it. Without this the post-beta trial never starts for a new user
   and they fall into the free setup (`:66-78`).
2. `sb.rpc('record_health_consent', {_granted:true, _app_version, _platform})`.
3. On RPC error: **queue** the consent via `queuePendingConsent` so the audit
   evidence is not lost, and still proceed on the local flag (founder decision
   2026-06-18, `:84-107`).
4. Cache `@volyume_health_consent_<uid> = 'true'` (`:108-110`).
5. Telemetry `article9_consent_recorded` (`:114-129`).
6. **`await cascade.startCascade()`** -- awaited, not fire-and-forget, so the
   trial grant (`tier='pro'`) lands before the navigator re-renders; otherwise a
   new user briefly flashes the free setup (`:130-147`).
7. `healthConsentGranted()` sets `{healthConsent: true, healthConsentChecked:
   true}` (`useAppStore.js:202`).
8. Kick a `syncAll`: the sign-in cloud restore is consent-gated and fails closed,
   so for a user who granted consent on THIS screen it never ran (F2/SC-1,
   `:149-164`).

**Un-skippable.** The Continue button is `disabled={!agreed || busy}` with
matching `accessibilityState` (`:240-248`). The only additive escape is OB-6's
quiet "What if I don't agree?" disclosure (`:261-300`), which sits BELOW the
existing actions, rewords none of the locked copy, and offers exactly two
factual routes: sign out, or delete the account. Its body states plainly:
"Without this consent, Volyume cannot process your health data, so the app cannot
be used. Nothing is processed until you agree." (`:279`).

**Art 7(3) pre-disclosure**: the right to withdraw is stated BEFORE consent is
given, with the exact location -- "You can withdraw this consent at any time in
Settings > Privacy & legal" (`:234-238`).

**Fails closed for new users**: see §B.1 step 3.

## D.2 Consent state (`useAppStore.js:193-204`)

Three values: `null` = not yet checked, `true` = granted, `false` = not granted
so route to the gate. Cached per user under `@volyume_health_consent_<userId>`.
`healthConsentChecked` is set true in **every** branch of the check (granted,
ungranted, or transient read failure) and only resets on sign-out, which is why
the blocking splash resolver at `RootNavigator.js:1589` always terminates
(`:1583-1587`).

## D.3 Pending-consent retry (`src/lib/consent/pendingConsent.js`)

Single pending record under `pendingHealthConsent.v1` (note: no `@volyume_`
prefix, so it never rides the prefs sync). `flushPendingConsent` retries
`record_health_consent` on the next sync, recording the ORIGINAL consent's app
version and platform so the audit row reflects the grant, not the retry
(`:34-38`). Safe to call on every sync; no-ops when nothing is queued.

## D.4 Withdrawal (`useAccountActions.handleWithdrawConsent`, `:396-...`)

Two-step confirm, then: `record_health_consent(false)` (soft-fail -- the user's
intent is clear and delaying for a server hiccup is worse than a missing audit
row), `setHealthConsent(false, true)`, telemetry
`article9_consent_withdrawn`, then the **standard delete-account pipeline**. The
rationale is recorded verbatim: withdrawing Article 9 consent is the legal end of
the lawful basis, so it must queue account deletion, not merely flip a flag; the
earlier flag-only behaviour left the data on the servers without a lawful basis,
itself a UK GDPR breach (`:381-395`).

## D.5 What the consent screen tells the user leaves the device

Bullets at `:191-222`: weight and its trend, body fat and lean mass, everything
in the food diary, weekly check-ins, ED screening answers, progress photos plus
their quality/confidence/leanness/Volyume Score/change metadata, and
**anonymous measurement numbers from photo analysis (never the photos, never
name or account)**. Storage: encrypted local storage on the phone with photo
image files staying on the device unless shared or exported; Supabase in the EU
region with row-level security; on deletion, cloud removal starts immediately,
the device is wiped, and backup copies are purged within 30 days.

## D.6 Privacy preferences and export

- `analyticsOptOut` -- see A.1.6 and UNCERTAINTIES U1.
- **Sentry** (summary only; another agent owns the detail): `src/lib/sentry.js`
  with scrubbing in `src/lib/observability/sentryScrub.js`; no PII leaves the
  device.
- **Backup** (`lib/dataBackup.js`): JSON of database records only; private photo
  image files are never bundled (`SettingsDataScreen.js:196`, `:207`, `:345`).
- **CSV export**: workout sets only (`database.buildWorkoutCSV`,
  `SettingsDataScreen.js:131-158`); food CSV export lives in
  `src/lib/food/` with `src/lib/__tests__/csvExport.test.js`.
- **Coach handover report PDF** (`lib/coachReport.js`): has an ED-neutral variant
  and fail-closed wellbeing reads; the screen handler is only busy-state and calm
  failure paths (`SettingsDataScreen.js:160-189`).
- **Device-only promises kept by the sync exclusions**
  (`sync.js:1288-1298`, pinned by `syncPrefExclusions.test.js:60-77`):
  raw SCOFF answers, cycle tracking, the error-log ring buffer, last-crash
  metadata, pending feedback and prompt history, and the in-progress onboarding
  draft.

# E. SUBSCRIPTION AND TIER

## E.1 Resolution (`src/lib/proGate.js`)

```
PRO_BETA_ACTIVE = false            // proGate.js:28, production launch 2026-06-06
_resolveTier(trialState, betaActive):
  betaActive              -> 'pro'
  'paid_pro'              -> 'pro'
  'pro_trial_active'      -> 'pro'
  'paid_complete'         -> 'pro'   // legacy, migration 030 compat
  'complete_trial_active' -> 'pro'   // legacy
  'free' | 'cascade_expired' | 'unstarted' | default -> 'free'
```
(`proGate.js:39-53`.) `isPaidTier(userProfile)` reads
`userProfile.trialState`, which mirrors `users_profile.trial_state` via the
registry (`:62-64`). A granular per-feature entitlement layer (FEATURE_MAP,
hasFeature, PRO_ROUTES, isProRoute, isProUser, getProLabel) was built and tested
but never wired into a single screen, and was removed 2026-05-29 once the founder
confirmed Pro is binary (`:12-20`). Safety logic stays tier-blind: guardrails
MUST NOT consult tier (`:22-23`). Tested in `src/lib/__tests__/proGate.test.js`.

The store's own runtime resolution order is:
1. `checkTier()` at boot reads `@volyume_tier`, and **enforces trial expiry
   locally**: if the cached tier is `pro`, `trial_state` is `pro_trial_active`
   and `pro_trial_ends_at` is past, it drops to `free` and rewrites the cache
   (C-3/H1, `useAppStore.js:688-711`). Paid lapses are server/RTDN-driven because
   the device cannot know a paid sub lapsed. The legacy "first-run done implies
   pro" grant was removed (audit M-3, `:694-697`).
2. `refreshTierFromCloud(client, uid)` (`:993-1070`) reads
   `tier, billing_period, trial_state, pro_trial_ends_at` with a 5 s timeout,
   applies the C-1 optimistic-window guard (never downgrade pro -> free while
   `_optimisticPaidUntil > now`, `:1020-1025`), persists BEFORE setting in-memory
   state, caches trial state/end, refreshes `@volyume_paid_verified_at` when the
   server reports `paid_pro`, and rides `trialState`/`proTrialEndsAt` onto
   `userProfile`.
3. `cascade.reconcilePaidEntitlement` at launch as a client safety net (E.6).

| Route | Label |
| --- | --- |
| WeeklyCheckInScreen | `Weekly check-in` |
| NutritionTargetsScreen | `Nutrition targets` |
| MealNamesScreen | `Meal names` |
| PerDayTargetsScreen | `Per-day targets` |

(21 distinct components; `Cardio`, `Nutrition` and `Recipes` labels repeat.)

**Read-only guard (`withReadOnlyProGuard`) -- 3 routes** (`:218-236`):

| --- | --- | --- |
