Soft-delete semantics per the registry header: "deletes set `deleted_at`
and propagate as UPDATE; hard-delete happens server-side after 30 days"
(`registry.js:18-19`).

### Legacy track (`src/lib/sync.js`, 1,995 lines)

**Push** (`bulkUploadLocalData`, `sync.js:639-769`), in order:
`syncExercises` → completed `workouts` + their `workout_sets` (batched
10 at a time with a 50 ms yield) → `_pushProgrammes` →
`_pushRoutinesAndExercises` → `_pushMesocycles` (+ `mesocycle_weeks`) →
`_pushMorningWeights` → `_pushCoachOutputs` → `_pushUserBodyProfile` →
`_pushUserInsights` → `_pushExerciseUserNotes` → `_pushWorkoutNotes` →
`_pushExerciseGoals` → `_pushPeakWeekPlans` → `_pushPlannedMuscleVolume`
→ `_pushAdaptationEvents` → `_pushAllUserPrefs`.

**Pull** (`pullFromCloud`, `sync.js:1354-1549`), in order:
`_pullExercises` FIRST (so FK targets exist) → `workouts` (delta) →
`workout_sets` (chunked by workout id) → `_pullProgrammes` →
`_pullRoutinesAndExercises` → `_pullMesocycles` (+ weeks) →
`_pullMorningWeights` → `_pullCoachOutputs` → `_pullUserBodyProfile` →
`_pullUserInsights` → `_pullExerciseUserNotes` → `_pullWorkoutNotes` →
`_pullExerciseGoals` → `_pullPeakWeekPlans` → `_pullPlannedMuscleVolume`
→ `_pullAdaptationEvents` → `_pullCustomExercises` → `_pullUserPrefs`.

**Retired legacy per-save writers** (E12 step 1): `syncProfile`,
`syncWeeklyCheckin`, `syncBodyMetric` are gone (`sync.js:10-13`,
`:596-600`); residual queued `check_in` / `body_metric` ops fall back to
the bulk push (`syncQueue.js:189-224`).

## C.2 Triggers

- **write** — `scheduleSync()` (`sync.js:516-548`), a 2 s debounce called
  by essentially every mutating DAO in `database.js` via
  `_scheduleSync()` (`database.js:48-53`, lazy-required to break the
  cycle). Since AC-02 it routes through `syncAll`, NOT
  `bulkUploadLocalData` directly, so it passes the Article 9 gate
  (`sync.js:538-545`). No-ops under Jest via `JEST_WORKER_ID`; tested
  with the guard removed by `src/lib/__tests__/sync.scheduleSync.test.js`.
- **foreground / background / network reconnect / 15-min periodic** —
  wired in `App.js`, all four routed through `syncAll`
  (`runner.js:4-7`).
- **sign_out** — the push-first safety, `triggeredBy: 'sign_out'`
  (`useAppStore.js:375`).
- **manual** — Settings.

## C.3 Gates before any row moves

Both `syncAll` (`runner.js:94-136`) and, independently, EVERY
`pushTable`/`pullTable` call (`transport.js:159-179`, F5 Phase A —
because on-save pushes invoke `pushTable` directly and would otherwise
bypass the runner):

1. **Sign-out wipe guard** — `isSignOutWiping()` → `skipped:
   'sign_out_wiping'`. Also re-checked BETWEEN each migrated-table pull
   (`runner.js:254`) and at seven named stages inside the legacy pull
   (`sync.js:1368-1373`, `bailForWipe`).
2. **Article 9 fail-closed consent gate** — `healthConsent !== true` →
   `skipped: 'health_consent_unresolved'`. ANY read failure counts as
   unresolved, never as consent.
3. **Live-session guard, fail-OPEN** — only an explicit `false` from
   `hasLiveSession()` blocks (`runner.js:127-136`). Rationale in
   `src/lib/__tests__/sessionGuard.sync.test.js`: on a locked phone the
   Keychain refuses the session read, pushes go out with no JWT,
   `auth.uid()` is NULL and RLS rejects with 42501 — the write was LOST
   (VOLYUME-2D/2F/2H). But a check that CANNOT answer must never switch
   sync off for everybody, so the test is written to FAIL if anyone
   tightens it into a fail-closed guard. The same guard is duplicated in
   `sync.js:624-637` (`_blockedByDeadSession`) because four screens call
   `bulkUploadLocalData`/`pullFromCloud` directly, and in
   `syncQueue.js:83-91`.
4. **Run lock** — a single in-memory `_runLock` de-duplicates concurrent
   calls → `skipped: 'already_running'`. `whenSyncIdle({timeoutMs})`
   (`runner.js:65-79`) lets sign-out wait for an in-flight run to drain.

## C.4 Watermarks (incremental delta)

`src/lib/sync/watermark.js`. Cursors live in **AsyncStorage**, keyed
`@volyume_pull_wm_<uid>_<table>` / `@volyume_push_wm_<uid>_<table>`.

- **Self-healing by design**: sign-out clears AsyncStorage, so the next
  sign-in has no cursor and does a FULL pull (`watermark.js:14-18`).
- Advancement: `newCursor = max(existing, max updated_at received)`;
  never moves backwards. Queries use `.gte(cursorIso)` so the boundary
  row is re-pulled — an idempotent `INSERT OR REPLACE`
  (`watermark.js:20-23`).
- **Advance only on a CLEAN pass.** Every call site holds the cursor when
  any row failed: workouts+sets (`sync.js:1449-1451`), programmes
  (`:1825`), routines+exercises (`:1868-1870`), mesocycles+weeks
  (`:1899-1901`), morning weights (`:1923`), coach outputs (`:1941`).
- Push watermarks are used only for `workouts` (`sync.js:667-712`),
  legitimate because a completed workout is immutable — the header warns
  never to key one on a table whose rows can change without
  `updated_at` advancing (`watermark.js:92-103`).
- The food domain has its OWN cursors,
  `@volyume_food_last_pushed_<uid>` / `@volyume_food_last_pulled_<uid>`,
  with two deliberate asymmetries: the PUSH cursor stores
  `maxLocalUpdatedAt - 1` and is compared on the LOCAL clock
  (`foodDomain.js:318-344`, SYNC-5 + D-M1), and the PULL cursor stores
  `serverTimestamp - 1` and MUST stay on server time — never
  `Date.now()`, because a fast device clock would write a future
  watermark and stall all food pulls until server time caught up
  (`foodDomain.js:430-447`, D1-#7 / D1-#1).

## C.5 Pagination and chunking

- `fetchAllRows` (`sync.js:129-149`) — pages `.range()` in 1,000s.
  A mid-pagination transport error THROWS (LS-03/H-12), so the caller
  holds its cursor rather than treating a partial view as complete.
- `fetchByIdsChunked` (`sync.js:153-191`) — 200 ids per IN-list chunk,
  AND paginates within each chunk. Both error paths throw for the same
  reason. Pinned by `src/lib/__tests__/sync.fetchByIdsChunked.test.js`.

## C.6 Error isolation, and the "benign skip" taxonomy

- **Per-table isolation.** The runner wraps every `pushTable`/`pullTable`
  in `.catch()`, counts errors per table, and emits a Sentry breadcrumb
  `sync.push.<table>.errors` / `.threw` so the next real error carries
  the trail (`runner.js:197-271`).
- **Legacy isolation.** Each `_pushX` helper swallows its own PostgREST
  `{error}` via `logPgErr` so one table cannot abort the rest — but that
  resilience once HID failures from the sign-out push-first safety, so
  `_bulkPushTracking` counts them and reports a total back to the runner
  (`sync.js:83-124`, `:766-768`).
- **Food-domain isolation.** The push sends one `food_sync_push` call PER
  non-empty table, not one call carrying all of them, because a single
  RPC is one transaction and a column drift on `daily_water` used to roll
  back the whole food domain (`foodDomain.js:23-34`). Empty tables are
  skipped entirely.
- **Benign skips** (`errors: 0`, so they cannot trip the sign-out guard):
  - `pull_only` on `pushTable` (`transport.js:186-188`).
  - `no_handler`, `no_client`.
  - `sign_out_wiping`, `health_consent_unresolved`.
  - **Missing TABLE** — `isMissingTableError`
    (`sync/tables/_missingTable.js`): `PGRST205` ("Could not find the
    table … in the schema cache") or `42P01`. Used only for genuinely
    additive tables whose cloud migration may not be applied yet.
  - **Missing COLUMN is explicitly NOT benign**: `PGRST204` and `42703`
    are excluded first, because the message names a column and real
    schema drift must still surface (`_missingTable.js:24-36`, tested in
    `sync/tables/__tests__/missingTable.test.js`). The one exception is
    `profiles`, which retries with progressively fewer optional columns
    (`sex`, `allergen_excludes`) rather than failing the sync.
  - **Deleted-account FK rejection** — `23503` on a `*_user_id_fkey` is
    demoted from Sentry error to an info breadcrumb
    (`sync/telemetry.js:82-107`), and the runner then asks Auth whether
    the user still exists and drops the local session if the account is
    gone (`runner.js:296-306`, `_clearSessionIfAuthUserGone`
    `:354-372`). The check is deliberately narrow (401/403 + a
    "does not exist"/"user_not_found"/"sub claim" message), so flaky
    connectivity can never sign a real user out.

## C.7 The retry queue

`src/lib/syncQueue.js` over the `pending_sync_ops` table.

- Ops: `workout`, `workout_delete`, `workout_set_delete`, `body_metric`,
  `morning_weight`, `check_in`.
- Backoff: `[0, 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 8 h]`, `MAX_RETRIES = 6`
  (`syncQueue.js:26-27`). After give-up the row STAYS with its
  `last_error` and `next_attempt_at = now + 1 year`
  (`syncQueue.js:133-148`).
- Drained on app foreground (`App.js` AppState `active`), 50 rows per
  pass, ordered by `created_at`.
- Draining against a dead session is DEFERRED wholesale, because burning
  the retry budget on guaranteed 42501 rejections is silent data loss by
  attrition (`syncQueue.js:74-91`).
- Upsert ops use `rethrow: true` so a failed cloud write throws and the
  queue records a real retry, instead of the helper re-enqueuing and the
  drain reporting a false success with a reset counter (audit F-003,
  `syncQueue.js:167-173`). Delete ops return their real outcome
  (`ok === true`), because returning true would strand the cloud copy and
  a later pull would resurrect the deleted session
  (`syncQueue.js:174-188`).
- A missing sync function drops the row rather than halting the drain
  (`safeCall`, `syncQueue.js:160-166`); a thrown `_scheduleRetry` is
  itself wrapped so one bad row cannot strand the rest
  (`syncQueue.js:114-122`).
- `getQueueStats` feeds the status line; `getPendingDeleteOpCount`
  (`syncQueue.js:264-277`) is the AC-04 sign-out guard.
- **The registry `sync_queue` was deleted (E12 step 0)**: it was built,
  never fed and never drained, so its depth could only mislead. The LIVE
  queue is `pending_sync_ops` (`runner.js:17-21`). Tested by
  `src/lib/__tests__/syncQueue.test.js`.

## C.8 Sync telemetry

`src/lib/sync/telemetry.js` → `engineTelemetry.track` → local
`engine_telemetry` → the `record_engine_telemetry` RPC (allow-listed
server-side).

- `sync_run` — status, duration, `triggered_by`, per-table pull/push
  counts, rejected/errored counts, queue depth before/after
  (`telemetry.js:24-47`; allow-listed by `migrate_037`).
- `sync_conflict_resolved` — `{table, record_id, strategy, winner}`,
  fired on EVERY `conflict.resolve()` call
  (`sync/conflict.js:61-66`; allow-listed by `migrate_043`).

# D. CLOUD SCHEMA (Supabase EU-Dublin)

**Canonical source: `supabase/migrate_NNN_*.sql` — 128 migration files on
this tree (001-131 with gaps at 011, 026, 082, 083; two files share the
085 number: `migrate_085_food_quality_telemetry.sql` and
`migrate_085_notification_preferences_checkin_missed.sql`).
`schema.sql` and `setup_complete.sql` are stale snapshots and are NOT
authoritative** (stated repeatedly, e.g. `database.js:2015-2017`).

**Pair-scoped tables** (membership-based RLS, not own-row):

`src/lib/__tests__/trialLedger.contract.test.js` and

**Marketing schema** (`migrate_120`-`124`): `marketing_waitlist`,

**RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER).**
Food: `food_sync_push`, `food_sync_pull`, `food_library_pull`,

Deletion: `delete_user_data`, `record_account_deletion_started` /

`private.sweep_incomplete_account_deletions`.
Partners: `create_partner_invite`, `redeem_partner_invite`,
`end_partnership`.

**Triggers of note.** `_users_profile_merge_column_updates_at`
(migrate_045) — the safe merge behind the `profiles` merge strategy.
`protect_users_profile_tier` (migrate_005/067/070) — rolls back any

`*_touch_updated_at` triggers on `body_metrics`, `weekly_checkins_v2`,

## D.2 Security hardening lineage

- `migrate_005`/`007` RLS hardening; `migrate_061` pinned
  `search_path` on every SECURITY DEFINER function (HP-1).
- `migrate_070` protects trial/entitlement columns from client writes;
  `migrate_071` adds the trial ledger (delete-and-restart abuse guard).
- `migrate_088` dropped the open-insert policy on the debug log.
- **`migrate_119`** closed four trust-boundary holes found by the Codex
  adversarial audit 2026-07-12 — BSEC-01 (a member could self-INSERT an
  `invited` partnership and UPDATE it into a forced, non-consented
  pairing), BSEC-06 (a direct INSERT policy let any user write arbitrary
  telemetry past `record_engine_telemetry`'s allow-list), BSEC-11 (forged
  / backdated `consent_log` rows), BSEC-10 (re-keying
  `partner_weekly_intentions.pair_id` onto someone else's pair).
- `migrate_130` revoked `anon` EXECUTE on the SECURITY DEFINER surface.
- `migrate_069` made the `auth.users` FK cascade.
- Telemetry ingress is an **allow-list**, extended by a long chain of
  migrations (029, 037, 038, 040, 041, 043, 063, 073-080, 084, 085, 093,
  099, 101, 103, 104).

## D.3 Migration discipline

- Every migration is **additive and idempotent** unless its header says
  otherwise; each header records purpose, applied-locally, applied-remotely,
  safe-to-re-run and rollback (`supabase/README.md` header).
- **Founder-gated, Claude-run since 2026-07-10**: production requires the
  founder's exact phrase "run against production" per batch, given AFTER
  an audited apply list, followed by a read-only re-verification of every
  object (`supabase/README.md`). 101-116 were applied under this model on
  2026-07-10 (17/17 object checks green).
- **`migrate_049` and `migrate_059` remain HELD.**
  - 049 (drop `peak_week_plans`) is a DRAFT with a six-step client
    cleanup checklist that is NOT done — `_pushPeakWeekPlans` and
    `_pullPeakWeekPlans` still run and the local table still exists.
    Dropping it while a shipped build still pushes to it would break
    those pushes (`migrate_049:1-32`).
  - 059 (numbered/flexible meal slots) must be applied BEFORE any client
    that writes `meal_N` slot keys reaches production sync, or those
    entries fail the old CHECK on push (caught per-table, so the row
    stays local and the wider run still succeeds, but it never reaches
    the cloud) (`migrate_059:1-31`).
- **`migrate_131` (`mesocycles.block_ledger jsonb`) was applied to
  EU-Dublin production and verified on 2026-08-09** — column present
  (jsonb, nullable, no default), 11 mesocycle rows untouched, ledger
  ordered after 129/130 (`migrate_131:12-21`, `supabase/README.md`).
  Same ORDER-MATTERS law as 129: the migration must precede the build
  that pushes the column.

---

# E. OFFLINE MODEL

## E.1 Fully offline (local-first, no network at all)

**LIVE.** Everything that reads or writes SQLite:

- Workout logging end to end: start session, log sets (weight/reps/RIR/
  RPE/AMRAP/unilateral), rest timer, per-set and session feedback,
  complete session, PRs, history, analytics, volume heatmap.
- Plan library, plan builder, routines, day/exercise reorder, plan
  folders, sample/library routines.
- The exercise library (seeded locally; canonical rows never come from
  the network) and creating custom exercises.
- Mesocycle creation, week progression, planned volume, deload logic, the
  block ledger computation and next-block seeding.
- All deterministic engines — `planEngine`, `nutritionEngine`,
  `weeklyCoach`, `coachApply`, `mesocycle`, `poolGenerator`,
  `cardioEngine`, `edPatternDetector`, `wellbeing`. They are pure, no
  I/O, no LLM.
- Food logging against anything already in the local cache: the bundled
  OFF-UK + CoFID snapshots (~29 k rows), previously logged foods, synced
  foods, and custom foods. Local search is FTS5 first, SQL LIKE as
  fallback (`food/sources/localCache.js`).
- Barcode scanning that HITS the local cache — including a barcode the
  user typed manually onto a custom food, which closes the
  scan-miss → save → rescan loop locally (`database.js:1154-1160`).
- Recipes, saved meals, meal-plan assembly and swaps, water, per-day
  target offsets, diary rollups (recomputed locally).
- Cardio logging, manual steps.
- Progress photos and Progress Scan **entirely** — capture, EXIF strip,
  on-device MLKit/TFLite analysis, estimate, classification history.
  Nothing leaves the device.
- Check-ins, morning weights, body metrics, the weekly coaching run and
  applying its adjustments.
- Notifications scheduling (local notifications), quiet hours.
- CSV export, JSON backup export/import, external CSV import, DB
  snapshots and snapshot restore.

## E.2 Genuinely requires network

- **Authentication.** Sign-in / sign-up (Apple, Google, email+password).
  There is no anonymous mode, so a brand-new user cannot get past auth
  offline.
- **All sync.** Push, pull, the retry drain, the food bulk RPCs.
- **Barcode / food lookup MISSES.** Waterfall steps 4 and 5:
  OpenFoodFacts live (`food/sources/liveOff.js`, 1,200 ms abort timeout,
  no API key) and USDA FoodData Central (`food/sources/usda.js`,
  1,500 ms timeout, requires `EXPO_PUBLIC_USDA_API_KEY` at build time —
  **LIVE-CONDITIONAL**: without the key the source short-circuits to
  empty and the waterfall still returns).
- **Food library delta top-up** (`food_library_pull` RPC).
- **Frequents tab** — server-computed, pulled via `food_frequents_pull`.
- **Push notification token registration** (`device_push_tokens`) and
  any remote push.
- **Partner features** — invites, redemption, unpair, cheers (edge
  function), shared-block proposal/acceptance are online ops in
  `partners/service.js`; only the mirrors read offline.
- **Billing** — purchase, restore, entitlement, the cascade.
- **Account deletion** (edge function → `delete_user_data` RPC fallback).
- **Sign-out**, effectively: the push-first safety aborts sign-out if it
  cannot prove the push reached cloud, unless the user takes the
  "sign out anyway" escape hatch.

**NOT network-dependent, contrary to the obvious guess: label OCR.**
`src/lib/food/ocr.js` is on-device MLKit Text Recognition v2, bundled at
EAS build time — no API key, no network round-trip. An earlier Google
Cloud Vision adapter was removed for violating the free-stack constraint
(`ocr.js:1-30`). **LIVE-CONDITIONAL** on the native module being linked;
`isOcrConfigured()` reports false otherwise and the screen shows the
manual-entry CTA.

## E.3 What degrades (rather than fails)

- Food search falls back from FTS5 to SQL LIKE if FTS5 is not compiled in.
- Food lookup degrades snapshot → local cache → OFF → USDA → manual entry.
- A missing cloud column on `users_profile` degrades to pushing/pulling
  fewer profile columns rather than failing the sync.
- A not-yet-applied cloud table degrades to a benign skip.
- Micronutrients render "unknown", never 0, when a source has no value.
- Sync itself degrades silently and quietly: the user sees a queue depth,
  never a red error badge (§ J).

---

# F. CONFLICT AND MULTI-DEVICE

## F.1 The three strategies

`src/lib/sync/conflict.js`.

- **`last_write_wins`** — compare `updated_at`; strictly-greater local
  wins, otherwise server (`conflict.js:71-77`). Ties go to the SERVER in
  the dispatcher. Timestamps are parsed tolerantly (number or ISO).
- **`server_wins`** — server unconditionally; used for `ed_pattern_flags`,
  `tier_history`, `daily_intake_rollups`. Local edits to these rows are
  stomped by the next pull, by design (`database.js:7600-7606`).
- **`merge`** — `profiles` only. Per-column, driven by the cloud's
  `column_updates_at` jsonb map: for each column the CLIENT touched, keep
  whichever side's timestamp wins; columns the client did not touch keep
  the server's. `id` and `user_id` are never merged. The merged map is
  the union with local taking precedence (`conflict.js:86-102`). If the
  server has no map, it degrades to last-write-wins.

Every `resolve()` call fires `sync_conflict_resolved` for the sync-health
panel (`conflict.js:61-66`).

## F.2 Local-preserved-when-cloud-null cases

These are the places where a plain `INSERT OR REPLACE` would destroy
local data that the cloud cannot carry:

1. **`mesocycles.block_ledger`** — the pull reads the existing local
   value first and falls back to it when the cloud row carries none,
   because the ledger is NOT derivable and a pre-131 cloud row (or one
   pushed by an older build) would otherwise wipe it
   (`database.js:7215-7251`). jsonb arrives as an OBJECT from
   supabase-js and is stringified into the local TEXT column.
2. **`mesocycles.deload_week`** — the cloud has no such column, so
   `?? null` would wipe the locally derived value on every session
   restore. It falls back to `planned_weeks ?? duration_weeks`, which is
   a CERTAIN derivation (the last week is always the deload), not a guess
   (`database.js:7236-7246`).
3. **`mesocycle_weeks.rir_target`** — NOT NULL locally, absent in the
   cloud; re-derived from `is_deload` (`database.js:7270`).
4. **`users_profile.sex`** and **`allergen_excludes`** — never unset on a
   pull (`sync/tables/profiles.js:244-253`).
5. **`userProfile` local-only fields** — the merged profile spreads the
   existing local profile FIRST so meal-plan prefs with no synced column
   survive; rebuilding from mapped columns alone was a real data-loss bug
   (`profiles.js:229-234`).
6. **Food appliers** — F1 last-write-wins gate: `applyFoodEntryFromCloud`
   and siblings read the local `updated_at` and SKIP when
   `local >= cloud`, ties keeping local (`food/db.js:1626-1654`).
   Before this the four core food tables applied unconditionally and an
   older server row could clobber a newer unpushed local edit.

## F.3 Stale-device protections

- **Ledger authority + `LEDGER_VERSION` idempotency.** A stored ledger at
  the current version is returned as-is and never recomputed
  (`blockLedgerRunner.js:110-115`); a version mismatch or unparseable
  JSON triggers a rebuild. `learnedRange` is a pure REPLAY over the
  stored ledgers, so there is exactly one store and no parallel state
  that a stale device could diverge on (`learnedRange.js:15-21`).
  `seedOutcome` records what the user actually chose so the next block's
  explanation and the seeding write cannot disagree.
- **Suppression cannot carry upward.** Ledger entries from blocks trained
  under calm mode or an open ED flag NEVER move the learned ceiling
  upward, though their downward evidence still counts
  (`learnedRange.js:29-34`); `blockSeed` degrades a ledger seed to the
  repeat numbers under suppression rather than discarding it
  (`blockSeed.js:19-24`).
- **Sync cursors are DEVICE state and must never travel.** F1 / audit
  SD-1: they previously rode the `user_prefs` sync keyed by the Supabase
  uid (identical across devices), so device B imported device A's fresher
  push cursor, defeating the advance-only-on-a-clean-push hold-back —
  rows that failed to push were skipped for ever with no error, and the
  sign-out wipe then destroyed them. Now excluded on BOTH the push and
  the pull side (`sync.js:1265-1275`, `:1775-1785`), pinned by
  `src/lib/__tests__/syncPrefExclusions.test.js`.
- **Push watermarks advance only on a fully clean push**, so a row that
  failed to upload is retried rather than skipped (`watermark.js:96-102`,
  `sync.js:705-712`).
- **Boundary re-inclusion.** Pull uses `.gte`, food cursors store
  `ts - 1`; a row written in the same millisecond as the cursor can never
  be skipped permanently.
- **Merge-churn breaker.** `pullProfiles` writes back only when the merge
  actually changed something; writing unconditionally re-stamped every
  `userProfileFieldUpdatedAt` to now, which inflated the local map so the
  NEXT push looked newer, re-triggering the merge every single cycle
  (observed in production) (`profiles.js:256-266`).

## F.4 Deletion propagation

- **Soft deletes** (`deleted_at`) on: `workouts`, `workout_sets`,
  `routines`, `programmes`, `routine_exercises`, `mesocycles`,
  `mesocycle_weeks`, `nutrition_targets`, `body_metric_log`,
  `morning_weights`, `weekly_checkins`, `coach_outputs`, `exercises`,
  `custom_exercises`, `user_body_profile`, `user_insights`,
  `exercise_user_notes`, `peak_week_plans`, `food_entries`,
  `custom_foods`, `saved_meals`, `recipes`, `recipe_ingredients`,
  `food_favourites` (D1-#8), `daily_water` (D1-#8), `cardio_log`,
  `meal_plans`, `plan_folders`, `ed_pattern_flags`. Every pull filters
  `.is('deleted_at', null)` (or applies the tombstone), and
  `fetchByIdsChunked`'s default builder does too
  (`sync.js:171-174`).
- **Hard deletes**: server-side after 30 days per the registry header.
- **The upsert-cannot-express-a-delete hole (AC-04).** The push-first
  sign-out sync re-pushes every table by UPSERT, which cannot express a
  DELETE. The ONLY cloud delete path is the `workout_delete` /
  `workout_set_delete` tombstones in `pending_sync_ops` — and the wipe
  destroys that queue. So sign-out drains the queue first and then
  REFUSES to wipe while any delete op remains unshipped, unless forced
  (`useAppStore.js:425-455`, `syncQueue.getPendingDeleteOpCount`).
- **Sign-out wipe.** `wipeAllUserData(userId)` (`database.js:4882+`)
  deletes from `WIPE_DIRECT_TABLES` (49 named tables,
  `database.js:4806-4851`) by `user_id`, plus four tables with no
  `user_id` column wiped through their parent FK chain, deepest child
  first, inside one transaction: `adaptation_events` →
  `planned_muscle_volume` → `mesocycle_weeks` → `routine_exercises`
  (`database.js:4891-4930`). `FATAL_LOCAL_WIPE_TABLES`
  (`database.js:4853-4863`) names the tables whose wipe failure is fatal
  (photos, scans, all partner tables). `wipeAllUserDataWithRetry`
  (`database.js:5131`) retries 3× with backoff.
- **Account deletion.** `src/hooks/useAccountActions.js:255-285`: the
  `delete-account` edge function first, falling back to the
  `delete_user_data` RPC, with `record_rpc_fallback_deletion` logging the
  fallback. Completeness has been chased across three migrations (025,
  062, 096) plus `migrate_097` (deletion-log anonymisation) and
  `migrate_098` (a sweeper for incomplete deletions). The private trial
  and founder-pro ledgers SURVIVE deletion by design, contract-pinned.
- **Partner purge.** `end_partnership` and the status→ended triggers
  purge shared blocks, intentions and win cards; the delete-account edge
  function sweeps them by `pair_id`; the local §5 purge paths clear the
  mirrors on unpair, on an ended pair seen during a pull, and on sign-out
  (guarded by `src/lib/partners/__tests__/partnerIntentionPurge.guard.test.js`).

## F.5 Sign-out: the full push-first sequence

`src/store/useAppStore.js:313-500+`.

1. Emit `sign_out` funnel telemetry (before the wipe, so the local row
   still exists to be flushed).
2. `cancelScheduledSync()` so the 2 s debounce cannot fire mid-wipe.
3. `syncAll({triggeredBy: 'sign_out'})` — NOT `bulkUploadLocalData`,
   because the legacy bulk skips the food domain and every migrated
   table, and routing through `syncAll` is what stops sign-out wiping
   unsynced meals (`useAppStore.js:343-351`).
4. Bounded to 20 s total, with a retry loop **only** on
   `skipped: 'already_running'` — a routine state right after an edit,
   which used to send every such user to a scary "Sync incomplete" prompt
   (founder device report 2026-07-13). Between attempts it awaits
   `whenSyncIdle({timeoutMs: 2000})` rather than blind-sleeping
   (`useAppStore.js:363-394`).
5. Abort (keep the user signed in) on `status === 'error'`,
   `status === 'skipped'`, or `errored_count > 0`. Deliberately does NOT
   block on `pending` queue depth — that depth is per-entity retry ops
   whose data the same cycle's full push already covers, and blocking on
   it historically locked users out of sign-out entirely
   (`useAppStore.js:395-424`).
6. Drain the delete tombstones and refuse to wipe if any remain (§ F.4).
7. `flushPendingTelemetry()`.
8. `setSignOutWiping(true)` → `whenSyncIdle` → wipe.
9. `force: true` (the user-facing "sign out anyway" escape hatch)
   bypasses steps 5 and 6 after the risk has been shown.

The guard itself: `src/lib/sync/signOutGuard.js` — a module-level boolean
set AFTER the safety push has completed (so the safety push is never
blocked by it), cleared on the next sign-in.

# G. REINSTALL / NEW DEVICE

## G.1 Fully restores from cloud

Via the legacy pull: exercises (custom, restored into local `exercises`
with `is_custom = 1`), completed workouts + their sets, programmes +
`folder_id`, routines + routine_exercises, mesocycles + weeks (including
`planned_weeks`, `block_type`, `rir_ladder`, and — since migrate_131 —
`block_ledger`), morning weights, coach outputs, user body profile, user
insights, exercise user notes, workout notes, exercise goals, peak week
plans, adaptation events, and all `@volyume_*` prefs that pass
`shouldSyncPref`.

Via the registry pull: weekly check-ins, body metrics, nutrition targets,
the user profile (merged), notification preferences, daily steps, cardio
log, partner mirrors, meal plans, plan folders, per-day target offsets,
and the whole food domain (entries, custom foods, saved meals, recipes,
recipe ingredients, favourites/dislikes, water) plus locally recomputed
rollups.

**Custom volume landmarks (MEV/MAV/MRV) DO survive a reinstall** — they
live in AsyncStorage at `@volyume_landmarks_<userId>`
(`effectiveLandmarks.js:107`) and ride the generic `user_prefs` sync.
That contract is deliberately pinned by
`src/lib/__tests__/prefSync.landmarks.test.js`, whose header says: "if a
future exclude pattern ever drops the landmark key, custom targets would
silently stop surviving a reinstall, and this test fails first."

## G.2 Local-only — LOST on reinstall

1. **`planned_muscle_volume` (the primary table), in full.**
   The cloud table has only `planned_sets` and no
   `mev`/`mav`/`mrv`/`source`
   (`supabase/migrate_012_complete_sync.sql:205-214`), AND the pull
   writes into `planned_muscle_volume_sync`, not the primary table
   (`database.js:7583-7598`). So on a fresh device the primary table is
   EMPTY: not just the landmark labels but the planned sets themselves
   are absent from every reader that queries it
   (`coachApply.computeVolumeApply` via `getPlannedMuscleVolume`
   `database.js:4322`, `blockExplain`, `blockLedgerGather.sumPlannedSets`,
   `getPlannedMuscleVolumeForBlock` `database.js:4224-4232`). The
   `_sync` mirror is written but no product reader was found for it.
   **This is the single largest restore gap in this lane.**
2. **`adaptation_events` (the primary table).** Same shape of problem:
   push reads the primary via JOIN, pull writes `adaptation_events_sync`.
   The cloud schema is also lossy — local
   `decision`/`reason_code`/`reason_text`/`signals_json` are folded into
   a cloud `payload` JSON (`sync.js:1211-1232`).
3. **Progress photos, scan sessions, scan assets, scan classification
   history — everything.** By constraint, never synced. A reinstall loses
   the entire physique-photo history unless the user took a JSON backup
   (which carries the metadata rows but NOT the image files — the images
   are private app documents, `database.js:5215-5220`).
4. **`food_slot_recents`** ("Add again" memory) and **`food_frequents`**
   (server-recomputed on demand) — derived/disposable by design.
5. **`is_planned = 1` food entries** — meal-plan scaffolding never
   leaves the device.
6. **`pending_sync_ops`** — the retry queue itself.
7. **`engine_telemetry`** rows not yet pushed.
8. **`sync_meta`** — unused anyway.
9. **The `foods` library cache** — but this RE-DERIVES (see G.3).
10. **Excluded AsyncStorage prefs**, which is correct and intentional:
    sync cursors/watermarks, the active-workout crash snapshot, the
    notification timezone baseline, the Expo push token, the local user
    id, palette recents, the crash/error log, and the Article 9-sensitive
    set — `@volyume_scoff_answers` (raw ED-screening answers, promised
    device-only), `@volyume_cycle_tracking` (menstrual-cycle data),
    `@volyume_last_crash_meta`, `@volyume_feedback_*`,
    `@volyume_pro_onboarding_draft` (`sync.js:1283-1297`).
    Note the model is **allow-by-prefix, i.e. fail-OPEN** — everything
    `@volyume_` ships unless explicitly excluded. The code says so and
    names the follow-up: invert to a fail-closed allowlist (AC-01/H-03).

## G.3 Re-derives on a new device

- The **canonical exercise library** — seeded locally with deterministic
  name-hash IDs, so a routine pushed from device A resolves on device B
  without either device having pushed the library
  (`database.js:654-668`).
- The **food library** — bundled OFF-UK + CoFID snapshots re-import on
  first run, then `food_library_pull` tops up the delta.
- **`daily_intake_rollups`** — server-authoritative but recomputed
  locally per affected date after every food pull
  (`foodDomain.js:409-423`).
- **FTS5 indexes** — external-content, rebuilt from the base tables at
  any time (`rebuildFoodSearchIndex`).
- **`mesocycles.deload_week`** and **`mesocycle_weeks.rir_target`** —
  re-derived on pull (§ F.2).
- **`food_entries.entry_date`** — re-derived from `logged_at` as a LOCAL
  day key on every apply, so a fresh-device pull lands rows on the user's
  calendar day regardless of what the cloud carries (TZ-1).
- **Trends, PRs, weekly volume, adherence, the learned working range** —
  all computed from the restored raw rows (§ H).

---

# H. DERIVED VS STORED

## H.1 Stored (persisted, not recomputed)

- **The Block Ledger** — computed ONCE at block end and stored, because
  the underlying rows drift and the verdict must be stable. Version- and
  algorithm-stamped.
- **`planned_muscle_volume`** — the landmark band is resolved from
  `effectiveLandmarks` at plan time and then STORED alongside the planned
  sets, so the plan does not silently change meaning when the bands move.
- **`coach_outputs.output_json`** — the full coaching run result, plus an
  `applied` flag.
- **`nutrition_targets`** — engine output persisted, with `goal` and
  `protein_approach` moved onto the row specifically so the "Why these
  targets" explanation survives a device change.
- **`daily_intake_rollups`** — a derived total that is nevertheless
  stored and backed up, because historic diary days would otherwise
  render empty (`database.js:5212-5214`).
- **`workouts.set_count` / `total_volume`** — denormalised summaries.
- **`workout_sets.exercise_name` / `routine_exercises.exercise_name`** —
  denormalised so a pull can recover when the exercise id does not
  resolve.
- **`cardio_log.activity_name` / `category` / `met`** — snapshotted from
  the in-code library so the row stays self-describing if the library
  changes.
- **`food_entries` macros** — resolved at log time and stored, so an
  edited food definition never retroactively rewrites history.
- **`food_entries.weight_state`** — a stored LABEL, never a conversion
  factor.
- **`meal_plans.plan_json`** — the exact assembled plan with its prefs
  and engine-target snapshot, so swaps and coach edits survive.

## H.2 Derived on the fly

- Weekly volume per muscle, trends, rate of change, PRs, streaks,
  adherence, calorie bank, macro rings, diary timeline, micronutrient
  coverage, grocery lists.
- **The learned working range** — `computeLearnedRange` is a pure fold
  over the stored ledger history each time it is needed; there is
  explicitly NO parallel store (`learnedRange.js:15-21`).
- **`effectiveLandmarks`** — the manual → adapted → research precedence
  resolved at read time (`effectiveLandmarks.js:14-25`).
  `computeAdaptiveLandmarks` derives from set history.
- **Block status / current week index** — `getBlockStatus`,
  `getCurrentBlockWeekIndex` from dates.
- **Meal-plan assembly** — deterministic from the stored prefs + target
  snapshot + seed, but the exact ACTIVE plan is stored anyway precisely
  so it does not regenerate differently on another device.

## H.3 Provenance and versioning fields

| Field | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PRAGMA user_version` | SQLite | Local schema version (70). Carried in the JSON backup as `schemaVersion` (`dataBackup.js:59`) |
| `LEDGER_VERSION = 1` | `src/lib/interBlock.js:51` | Ledger shape version; drives idempotency and rebuild |
| `LEDGER_ALGORITHM_VERSION` | `interBlock.js:416` | Algorithm identity, distinct from shape |
| `seedOutcome` | `blockLedgerRunner.js:383` | `{intent, recordedAt, perMuscle}` — what the user actually chose from the advisor |
| `planned_muscle_volume.source` | local schema | `'template'` and friends — where a planned number came from |
| `daily_steps.source` | local schema | `'manual'` \| `'health'` |
| `cardio_log.source` / `ext_id` | local schema | manual vs imported, and the platform sample id |
| `progress_scan_sessions.model_version` / `estimator_version` / `estimate_source` / `abstention_reasons_json` / `bias_flags_json` | local schema | Full provenance for an on-device estimate |
| `body_metric_log.body_fat_source` | local schema | Where a body-fat number came from |
| `foods.source` / `source_id` / `verified` / `fetched_at` | local schema | Which database a food came from and when |
| `PLAN_SCHEMA_VERSION` | `food/mealPlanService.js:131` | Meal-plan JSON shape version |
| `BACKUP_FORMAT_VERSION = 1` | `dataBackup.js:18` | Backup envelope version |
| `users_profile.column_updates_at` | cloud (migrate_045) | Per-column write timestamps for the merge strategy |
| `@volyume_exercises_seeded_v7`, `_metadata_backfilled_v1`, `_metadata_rederived_v2`, `_library_topped_up_v3` | AsyncStorage (`seedExercises.js:6-19`) | Seed/backfill idempotency generations |
| `@volyume_off_snapshot_loaded_v1`, `@volyume_cofid_snapshot_loaded_v1` | AsyncStorage (`food/seed.js:123,136`) | Snapshot import idempotency |

# I. BACKUP / EXPORT / IMPORT

## I.1 `src/lib/dataBackup.js` — full JSON backup

**LIVE**, reachable from Settings → Your data.

- `exportBackup()` writes `{format: 'volyume-backup', formatVersion: 1,
  schemaVersion, exportedAt, app, sqlite: {...}, prefs: {...}}` to the
  cache directory and opens the native share sheet.
- Table set: `BACKUP_TABLES` (`database.js:5177-5221`) — 30 tables
  covering training, plans, blocks (including
  **`planned_muscle_volume` and `adaptation_events`, the PRIMARY
  tables**), nutrition, coaching, the whole food domain, meal plans,
  rollups, and the photo/scan metadata rows. The shared `foods` library
  is deliberately excluded (reseedable reference data). Rationale for
  the food inclusion is recorded as a GDPR Article 20 concern: a lapsed
  trial user otherwise had no self-service portability path for 14 days
  of logged food (`database.js:5199-5203`).
- Prefs: every `@volyume_` key except the crash log AND except anything
  matching `/(tier|trial|paid|entitle|subscrip|purchase|billing|
  verified_at)/i` — entitlement state is cloud-authoritative and must
  never travel in a backup, or a crafted file could flip the local tier
  to `pro` (audit F-002, `dataBackup.js:24-31`).
- `importBackup()` validates format, requires a numeric `formatVersion`
  in range (a missing marker fails loudly rather than silently applying
  v0 rows), then `restoreAllTables` + `restorePrefs`.
- `restoreAllTables` (`database.js:5246-5271`) runs in ONE transaction
  (all-or-nothing) and allowlists columns from the LIVE schema via
  `PRAGMA table_info`, so a crafted backup cannot inject arbitrary
  identifiers into the INSERT column list (audit F-005).

## I.2 `src/lib/dbSnapshot.js` — automatic DB snapshots

See § A.4. **INTERNAL**: taken automatically, surfaced through a restore
screen in Settings.

## I.3 `src/lib/food/csvExport.js` — food diary CSV

**LIVE.** Pure formatter + a thin FileSystem/Sharing wrapper. Headers:
`date, meal, food, brand, quantity_g, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g,
fibre_g`. Escapes CSV properly AND neutralises spreadsheet formula
injection by prefixing any cell starting with `= + - @ TAB CR` with a
single quote — a food name from an external database could otherwise
carry one (A2-060, `csvExport.js:19-32`).

## I.4 `src/lib/importExternal.js` — external CSV import

**LIVE.** Bulk-imports training history from **Hevy** and **Strong**
exports.

- Dependency-free CSV parser (quoted fields, escaped quotes, CRLF).
- `detectFormat` → `parseHevy` / `parseStrong` → `analyzeImport` →
  `runImport`.
- Exercise matching is fuzzy on a normalised name; score ≥ 0.7 matches an
  existing exercise, otherwise a custom exercise is created.
- **Idempotent**: a workout is skipped if a local workout with the same
  user and the same `started_at` (to the second) already exists.
- All inserts run inside one transaction, obtained through the app-wide
  `runInTransaction` queue rather than a raw BEGIN (same fix class as
  VOLYUME-1N).

## I.5 `src/lib/food/recipeImport.js`

**LIVE.** Recipe import into the food domain. (Not examined in depth in
this lane; named here for completeness of the import surface.)

**INTERNAL.** Exports scan calibration data for the

to emit NO file paths, filenames, photo names, URIs or user ids

# J. FAILURE MODES

## J.1 What the user actually sees

**Deliberately almost nothing.** `src/lib/syncStatusLabel.js:1-12`:

> "This deliberately does NOT surface a red 'error' state.
> PRODUCTION_READINESS_LOCKED.md section 1: the old header badge's
> transient red error (a pull-side blip with no pending writes, nothing
> lost) was alarming and was removed by founder direction. The signal
> that actually matters to the user is whether their own writes are
> backing up, so we report the queue depth, not the pull status. Quiet,
> factual, no nag."

The rendered line in Settings → Your data is one of:
- `Not synced yet.`
- `Last synced 5 min ago.`
- `Last synced 5 min ago. 3 changes waiting to upload.`

Relative time floors at every bucket so 31 min never reads as "1 h ago",
and a future timestamp (clock skew) clamps to "just now" rather than
going negative. Tested by `src/lib/__tests__/syncStatusLabel.test.js`.

The one place the user IS confronted is **sign-out**: if the push-first
safety cannot prove the data reached cloud, sign-out is aborted with a
"couldn't sign out, try again on a stronger connection" toast and a
"sign out anyway" escape hatch.

## J.2 What retries

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Single-entity push (workout, morning weight, workout/set delete) | Enqueued in `pending_sync_ops`, exponential backoff `[0, 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h]`, 6 attempts, then parked with `last_error` |
| Any table in a sync cycle | Its watermark is NOT advanced, so the same delta re-pulls/re-pushes next cycle |
| A food table in a partial-failure push | The shared food watermark is not advanced; healthy tables re-push idempotently via the RPC's ON CONFLICT |
| A failed migration | `user_version` is not bumped; retries next launch (with the pre-migration snapshot already on disk) |
| A failed DB open (probe close failure, key unavailable) | `initDatabase` resets its promise and the next launch probes again with clean state |
| Health-consent-unresolved skip | Granting consent kicks a fresh sync immediately |
| Dead-session skip | Work stays queued for the next foreground sync, retry counts untouched |

## J.3 What is silently, deliberately benign

- `pull_only` push attempts; `no_handler`; `no_client`.
- Missing cloud TABLE (`PGRST205` / `42P01`) for an additive table whose
  migration is not applied — `errors: 0` so it cannot wedge the sign-out
  guard. This exists because of the cardio_log incident (one handler
  fixed, the pattern not).
- Missing optional profile COLUMN (`sex`, `allergen_excludes`) — retried
  with fewer columns.
- Deleted-account `23503 *_user_id_fkey` — demoted to an info breadcrumb,
  then the session is cleared.
- FTS5 unavailable — search stays on LIKE, permanently, by design.
- USDA API key absent — the source short-circuits to empty.
- `_scheduleSync` when the sync module is unavailable
  (`database.js:52`).
- Every `.catch(() => {})` best-effort path: WAL checkpoints, snapshots,
  telemetry, watermark persistence, pending-consent flush.
- **Not benign, and correctly so**: missing COLUMN (`PGRST204`/`42703`)
  on an existing table is real schema drift and stays an error.

## J.4 AsyncStorage corruption recovery

`src/lib/__tests__/asyncstorage-recovery.test.js` pins the contract that
came out of the infinite-splash bug: corrupt JSON in AsyncStorage must
never leave a loading flag stuck. The test file records that the original
`initLocalUser` describe block was DELETED because the store action no
longer exists under `IDENTITY_AND_OWNERSHIP_LOCKED.md` rules 1/5; the
resilience contract is now scoped to `errorLog` (`loadBuffer` returns `[]`
instead of throwing on non-JSON at `@volyume_error_log_v1`) and to the
auth-state restorer in `RootNavigator.onAuthStateChange`.

Related resilience: watermark reads return `0` on any AsyncStorage
failure and writes never throw (`watermark.js:74-90`); `getPullWatermark`
returning 0 degrades to a FULL pull, which is always safe.

## J.5 DB-lifecycle interruption classification

`src/lib/__tests__/seedChainInterruption.test.js` (VOLYUME-27, founder
clean-slate walk 2026-07-13): a concurrent account switch or sign-out wipe
released the SQLite connection mid-way through the boot seed/derive chain,
and the benign self-healing interruption reported as a Sentry ERROR.
`isDbLifecycleInterruption` (`src/lib/seedExercises.js`) classifies the
released-object chain — including when it is nested in `cause` as expo's
`CodedError` nests it — as benign, while real SQL failures stay errors.

## J.6 The "database is locked" class

R2-11, a production P0 on build 2692 (plan build / sign-out wipe / set
logging). expo-sqlite runs statements on a parallel IO pool with no
per-connection mutex, and only transaction BLOCKS are queued app-side, so
a raw single-statement write colliding with an open BEGIN got
SQLITE_BUSY back instantly and surfaced as a hard rejection. The shipped
mitigation is `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000` — with one shared connection
a wait cannot deadlock (`database.js:161-177`). The deeper fix (queueing
ALL writes + a `runInTransaction` reentrancy flag) is recorded in that
comment as still on the board.

# UNCERTAINTIES

1. **Exact `PRAGMA user_version`.** I derived **70** by mechanically
   scanning the `SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS` array literal and cross-checking that
   entry 54 aligns with the comment "v54"; `dbSnapshot.js:27`'s
   `volyume_v70_to_v71` example corroborates it. I did not execute
   `runMigrations` against a real SQLite build to confirm, and the
   in-comment labels drift by one from v56 onward, so anyone quoting a
   number should re-derive it rather than trust a code comment.
2. **`planned_muscle_volume_sync` and `adaptation_events_sync` readers.**
   I found writers (the cloud-pull appliers) and index migrations but no
   product reader for either mirror. If a reader exists in a screen I did
   not grep, the § G.2 severity changes. Recorded as the most important
   thing to confirm from this lane.
3. **Whether the § G.2 `planned_muscle_volume` restore gap is a known,
   accepted design decision or an unnoticed defect.** The comment at
   `database.js:6874-6878` shows the PUSH side was deliberately fixed to
   read the primary table ("Previously this read from the _sync mirror,
   which was only populated by cloud pulls, so locally-computed planned
   volumes never reached the cloud and were lost on cross-device
   restore") — but the matching PULL-side fix (writing back into the
   primary table) does not appear to have been made, and the cloud has no
   columns for `mev`/`mav`/`mrv`/`source` regardless. I could not find a
   decision record either way, read-only.
4. **`@volyume_food_library_pull_cursor_v1` and
   `@volyume_food_library_pull_last_ms_v1`** (`food/libraryDelta.js:31-32`)
   are device-state cursors of exactly the class F1/SD-1 excluded from
   the prefs sync — but they do NOT match any pattern in
   `PREF_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (`sync.js:1255-1298`), so they appear to sync
   across devices. Worst case is a skipped or repeated library delta, not
   user-data loss, and the library re-derives — but I could not confirm
   whether this is a deliberate exemption or an oversight.
5. **Seed idempotency flags ride the prefs sync too**
   (`@volyume_exercises_seeded_v7`, `@volyume_off_snapshot_loaded_v1`,
   `@volyume_cofid_snapshot_loaded_v1`, the metadata backfill/rederive
   keys). On a new device the seed runs at boot before sign-in, so the
   ordering is probably harmless, but I could not trace every boot/pull
   interleaving read-only to rule out a pulled flag suppressing a needed
   seed or top-up.
6. **`sync_meta`** (`database.js:782-786`) has no reader or writer I could
   find. Labelled LEGACY-UNREACHABLE above; confirmation would need a
   full-tree grep beyond `src/lib` and `src/screens`.
7. **Cloud tables not created by any migration on this tree** —
   `workouts`, `workout_sets`, `routines`, `routine_exercises`,
   `programmes`, `mesocycles`, `mesocycle_weeks`, `exercises`,
   `morning_weights`, `weekly_checkins_v2`, `body_metrics`,
   `users_profile`, `coach_outputs`, `telemetry_events`. They predate
   the numbered migration series and exist only in the stale
   `schema.sql` / `setup_complete.sql` snapshots, so their EXACT live
   column sets could not be established from an authoritative source
   read-only. Everything I state about them is inferred from the push/pull
   payload shapes in `sync.js` and from later `ALTER TABLE` migrations.
8. **`migrate_085` is used twice** (`migrate_085_food_quality_telemetry.sql`
   and `migrate_085_notification_preferences_checkin_missed.sql`). Both
   are additive; whether both were applied, and in what order, is not
   determinable from the tree.
9. **`peak_week_plans`.** The module was removed by founder direction
   2026-05-25 and `migrate_049` (the drop) is HELD pending a six-step
   client cleanup that has not happened. The push and pull still run
   every cycle. Whether the local table still receives writes from any
   live UI surface was not established in this lane.
10. **`weekly_checkins` vs `weekly_checkins_v2`.** The local table is
    `weekly_checkins`; the cloud/registry name is `weekly_checkins_v2`.
    I did not open `sync/tables/weeklyCheckins.js` in full, so the exact
    column mapping and the fate of a `weekly_checkins` v1 cloud table
    (if any) is unverified.

## A.3 Quiet hours (`quietHours.js`)

- Key `@volyume_quiet_hours_v1`; default `{ enabled: true, start 22:00, end 07:00 }` (`quietHours.js:18-26`).
- `isInsideQuietHours` handles the midnight wrap (`:69-81`).
- Two shifters: `shiftHourMinuteOutOfQuietHours` (recurring triggers, shifts to window end) and `shiftDateOutOfQuietHours` (one-shots, advances a day when the same-day end has already passed) (`:90-124`).
- Corrupt stored blobs fall back to the locked default; hour/minute are clamped.
- UI lives in `NotificationSettingsScreen.js:510-540, 762-770`.
- **Exemption:** `rest_end` is deliberately NOT quiet-hours shifted (`restEnd.js:13-14`), matching the locked A2 addendum.

## A.4 Push budget (`budget.js`)

- `EVENT_DAILY_CAP = 2`, `EVENT_WEEKLY_CAP = 8` (`budget.js:35-36`).
- `EVENT_PRIORITY` (highest first, `:43-57`): `cascade_gate` → `weekly_coach_ready` → `activation_nudge` → `checkin_missed` → `trial_day3` → `winback` → `year_of_lifts_unlock` → `monthly_recap` → `planned_meal_confirm` → `partner_cheer`.
- **Drift from the locked addendum:** the locked table orders `…monthly_recap` last with `partner_cheer` above nothing; code inserts `planned_meal_confirm` between `monthly_recap` and `partner_cheer` and inserts `activation_nudge` above `checkin_missed`. Both insertions are documented in-code as founder calls (S6 comment at `:46-49`; F3 comment at `:55`).
- `decideBudget` is pure (`:181-219`): one-per-topic-per-day short-circuit (`duplicate_topic`), then day cap, then week cap. Eviction requires **strictly higher** priority; equal priority never evicts.
- `requestEventPushSlot` (`:235-285`) reads `getAllScheduledNotificationsAsync`, applies the decision, cancels evicted losers, and **fails OPEN** on an unreadable schedule (`reason: 'schedule_unreadable'`).
- Drops/evictions fire `notification_failed` with `reason: 'budget_capped'` / `'budget_evicted'` — no new telemetry event names (`:256-281`).
- Habit pushes (morning/evening weight, training day, weekly check-in, meal reminders) are **not** event categories, so `isEventCategory` returns false and they are exempt.

## A.5 Foreground suppression (`handler.js`) — `configureNotificationHandler()`

Installed from `RootNavigator.js:897`. Delivery-time rules, in order:

| `data.type` | Suppressed when |
|---|---|
| `rest_end` | **always** in foreground (in-app timer owns the moment) — `handler.js:25-27` |
| `morning_weight`, `evening_weight` | weight already logged today **OR** open ED flag — `:33-36` |
| `weekly_checkin` | a real check-in exists this local-Monday week (`energyScore != null`) — `:37-39`, helper `:90-112` |
| `training_reminder` | a completed workout started today — `:40-42`, helper `:149-162` |
| `checkin_missed` | a real check-in in the last 72h **OR** open ED flag — `:47-50`, helper `:117-130` |
| `activation_nudge` | the user has passed the stage the nudge was laid for **OR** open ED flag — `:55-58`, helper `:167-188` |

`_edFlagOpen()` (`:132-147`) **fails CLOSED** — a read error is treated as flag-open and suppresses.
Default return sets `shouldShowAlert`, `shouldShowBanner`, `shouldShowList` all true, `shouldPlaySound: false`, `shouldSetBadge: false` (`:62-72`). The `shouldShowBanner`/`shouldShowList` keys carry an iOS-audit comment (2026-07-13): the legacy `shouldShowAlert` alone silently never shows the banner on iOS 14+.

**Drift (real):** `App.js:130-142` installs its **own** `Notifications.setNotificationHandler` at module scope, keyed on `data.channelId === 'rest-done'` — a channel that does not exist anywhere in the tree (the real channel is `rest-alerts`). Because `configureNotificationHandler()` runs later (RootNavigator mount effect), the App.js handler is overwritten and is dead code, but it is a live footgun: any future change that installs it after mount would silently kill every foreground banner.

## A.6 Listeners + tap telemetry (`listeners.js`)

`installNotificationListeners({ onTap })` (`:59-116`), installed from `RootNavigator.js:930`:
1. `addNotificationReceivedListener` → `trackNotificationSent` with `scheduledFor` from `trigger.date`. Only fires while the JS process is alive; cold-start tray deliveries are never observable (`:12-17`).
2. `addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` → `trackNotificationTapped`, then either routes a `rest_timer` action button into `handleRestTimerAction` (and returns), or hands the response to `onTap` (`:60-87`).
3. `getLastNotificationResponseAsync()` for the cold-start tap (`:105-107`).
Returns an idempotent `dispose`. Every telemetry call is individually try/caught: "notification flows MUST NOT break because telemetry is unavailable".

`installRestActionBridge()` (`restTimerActions.js:305-324`) is installed alongside (`RootNavigator.js:936`) for the native Android FGS chronometer buttons.

## A.7 Permissions (`permissions.js`)

- `requestNotificationPermissions()` returns `'granted' | 'denied' | 'undetermined'`; returns `'denied'` immediately on web; any throw → `'undetermined'` (`:22-38`).
- iOS request opts: `allowAlert: true, allowBadge: true, allowSound: false` — "the in-app surfaces drive every sound or haptic; OS notification audio is not part of the design" (`:28-32`). Note this contradicts several schedulers that set `sound: true` on content (morning/evening weight, training reminder, rest end, year of lifts, monthly recap) — on iOS the sound is requested off at permission level, so those sounds are Android-effective only. See §J.
- Denied state: `restoreNotifications` returns early unless status is exactly `'granted'` (`scheduler.js:1183-1184`); `scheduleTrainingReminders` also checks (`trainingReminders.js:584-585`). No in-app re-prompt; `NotificationSettingsScreen` surfaces the state (`:74-79`).

## A.8 Telemetry (`telemetry.js`)

Three fire-and-forget wrappers over `engineTelemetry.track`, all resolving `userId` lazily from the store and returning silently without one:
- `trackNotificationSent({category|notification, scheduledFor, payload})` → `{category, scheduled_for, delivered_at, ...payload}`
- `trackNotificationTapped(...)` → `{category, tapped_at, ...payload}`
- `trackNotificationFailed({category, reason, payload})` → `{category, reason, ...payload}` — requires an explicit category, never guesses.
`resolveCategory` refuses to misattribute: an unmappable type returns null and telemetry is skipped (`:49-56`).
Event names are on the client allow-list (`src/lib/telemetry/events.js:86-88`, panel 6).

Observed `reason` values across the tree: `schedule_threw` (every scheduler catch block), `budget_capped`, `budget_evicted` (`budget.js:259, 278`), `habit_schedule_refresh_threw` (`trainingHabitSchedule.js:844`).

## A.9 EVERY LOCAL NOTIFICATION — full specification

### 1. Morning weight — `morning_weight`
| | |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | `scheduleMorningWeightNotification(hour=7, minute=0)` — `scheduler.js:102-151`. Called from `ProOnboardingScreen.js:828`, `CoachingRemindersScreen.js:113`, `CoachOutputScreen.js:1825`, and `restoreNotifications` (`scheduler.js:1202`). |
| **Timing** | Seven WEEKLY triggers (one per expo weekday 1-7) at the user's hour, default 07:00 local. NOTIF-4 comment (`:113-116`): one DAILY trigger froze the copy, so per-weekday triggers exist purely so the copy pool rotates. |
| **Conditions** | Quiet-hours shifted. **ED-flag schedule gate** (`weighInEdFlagOpen`, `:184-199`) — never laid while a flag is open, **fails CLOSED**. In `restoreNotifications` it is additionally **Pro-only** and gated on `prefs.morningEnabled` (`:1201-1205`, E10-F4 comment). Not budget-gated (habit class). |
| **Copy** | 4-variant rotating pool, `morningCopies()` `:81-88`. e.g. "Good morning, Sam" / "Whenever you're ready, hop on the scales and log today's weight." Name suffix from `greetName()` (`:62-73`, capped at 20 chars, omitted cleanly). |
| **Destination** | **No route.** `routeForNotificationType('morning_weight')` returns null — the tap opens the app on its default landing screen. |

Stages by completed sessions inside the first `ACTIVATION_WINDOW_DAYS`: 0 → `cold_start` (anchor = account creation + 3 days), 1 → `stalled_1`, 2 → `stalled_2` (anchor = that session + 4 days); ≥ `ACTIVATION_TARGET_SESSIONS` → null. Hard stop at window + 3 grace days (`NUDGE_WINDOW_GRACE_MS`), an elapsed window is never chased.
Gates: toggle `activationNudgeEnabled !== false`; account-creation date read from the **live Supabase session** (`data.session.user.created_at`) — stands down rather than guess if absent (`:890-898`); cheap early-out past window+grace; **ED flag fail-CLOSED**; a workout-read failure stands down rather than compute `cold_start` from an empty list (`:918-924`); quiet hours; **budget rank 3** (above `checkin_missed`).
Copy `activationNudgePush` (`activationNudge.js:99-121`) and the matching in-app Home banner `activationBannerLine` (`:127-149`) come from the same stage value so they cannot drift.
**Tier-blind** (a deliberate deviation, documented in the locked addendum). Single id `volyume_activation_nudge`. `sound: false`. **No route** — `activation_nudge` has no `notificationRoute` case (see §A.14).

### 15. Partner beats — three pushes (NEW-002 rebuild + D5-B2)
`schedulePartnerBeats(userId)` — `scheduler.js:1379-1519`. **Trigger point: the partner sync PULL** (`src/lib/sync/tables/partners.js:242-243`), described as "the only moment a cheer can ARRIVE on device". Fire-and-forget, safe to repeat (watermarks).
Global gates first: not web, userId present; **ED flag fail-CLOSED → silence**; toggle `partnerCheerEnabled !== false`; an **active** partnership must exist. Watermark record in AsyncStorage per user: `@volyume_partner_beats_v1_<userId>` = `{v:1, lastCheerId, lastStreakRun, joinedPairIds[]}` (`partnerBeats.js:916-926`).
Each beat schedules at `now + 5s`, quiet-hours shifted, through a `PARTNER_CHEER` budget slot (rank 10, lowest). **Watermarks advance even when the budget says no** — "a capped beat is dropped for the episode, never re-queued later as stale news" (`:1504-1508`).

| Beat | id | `data.type` | Freshness / rule | Copy (`partnerBeats.js`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheer received | `volyume_partner_cheer` | `partner_cheer` | new cheer id, ≤ 48h old (`cheerToNotify` `:936-942`) | "{Name} cheered you on" / "A tap from your training partner. They can see you're keeping up your training this week." |
| Shared streak kept | `volyume_partner_streak` | `partner_streak` | only when `pair.streakEnabled`, status `counting`, run ≥ 2 **and** run grew past the watermark (`streakRunToNotify` `:950-956`) | "{N} weeks running, together" / "You and {name} both kept up your training this week." |
| Partner joined | `volyume_partner_join_<pairId>` | `partner_joined` | only for `member_a` (the waiting inviter), once per pair, `acceptedAt` ≤ 48h (`joinToNotify` `:970-978`) | "{Name} joined you" / "You are training together now. You'll see their training week here from now on." |

All `sound: false`, channel `coaching-reminders`.
**Drift (real, two-part):** `partner_streak` and `partner_joined` have **no entry in `categoryForDataType`** (`categories.js:190-210`) and **no case in `routeForNotificationType`**. Consequence: tapping either dead-ends (no navigation), and both `notification_sent` and `notification_tapped` telemetry are silently skipped for them (`telemetry.js:63-64` returns early on a null category). Only `partner_cheer` is mapped, and it routes to `ProgressTab` → `Consistency` — a screen that, per `partnerPlacementSpine.guard.test.js:6-9`, deliberately carries **NO partner row** since the founder device-walk of 2026-07-03. So the partner-cheer tap lands on a screen with nothing about the cheer on it.

## A.10 Remote / server push

### pushToken lifecycle — `pushToken.js`
- `registerPushToken(userId)` — called from `RootNavigator.js:1477` after sign-in, fire-and-forget. Upserts `device_push_tokens(user_id, expo_push_token, platform)` with `onConflict: 'user_id,expo_push_token'`; caches the token in AsyncStorage `@volyume_expo_push_token`.
- `unregisterPushToken(userId)` — deletes only **this device's** row, clears the cache unconditionally so a stale token cannot leak into the next account on a shared device.
- `getExpoPushToken()` no-ops (returning null) on web, without granted permission, or without `extra.eas.projectId`. **The projectId IS now present** (`app.json:6-8`: `2f60a6ed-8b37-4cd6-8057-60ee04e39ea8`), so the module's own "the project has no projectId at time of writing" header note (`:295-298`) is **stale documentation**.
- FCM-not-initialised errors are swallowed silently (`isRemotePushNativeSetupError` `:316-323`).

### `send-push` Edge Function — `supabase/functions/send-push/index.ts`
Service-to-service only. Requires the service-role key in `Authorization`, compared in **constant time** via SHA-256 digests (`timingSafeEqualStr` `:67-80`). Reads every live token for a user, POSTs one batch to `https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send`, then **prunes dead tokens** on `DeviceNotRegistered` tickets. `sound` deliberately omitted from messages ("the app's design drives sound/haptics in-app and OS audio is off by policy"). `channelId: 'default'` — note this is not one of the app's four registered Android channels (see §J).

### Payment-failure push — `subscription_payment_failure`
Two senders, identical copy:
- Google Play RTDN: `supabase/functions/play-billing-rtdn/index.ts:295-313` — title "Your payment didn't go through", body "No worries, it happens. Update your billing in **Google Play** to keep your Pro features.", `data: { type: "subscription_payment_failure" }`.
- Apple: `supabase/functions/_shared/appStore.ts:240-258` — same title, body says **the App Store**; fired on `DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW`/GRACE_PERIOD (`app-store-notifications/index.ts:135-140`), with no tier change.
**No `notificationRoute` case** for `subscription_payment_failure` → the tap opens the app with no destination.

### Partner cheer push — `supabase/functions/partner-cheer/index.ts`
Server validates the partnership and the one-per-day rate limit (duplicate → 429, never a second push), then **checks the recipient's open ED/wellbeing flag with the service role**: if a flag is open, delivery **downgrades to in-app only, no push** (`:11-15, 148`). The cheer row is still written — only the recipient's push delivery is restricted. Otherwise it invokes `send-push` with title `"{senderName} sent you a cheer"` and body = the acknowledgement line for the chosen kind (`ACK_LINES[ackKind]`, `:181-183`). A failed push is not a failed cheer (`:188-189`).

### `subscription_expiring`
Category and channel routing exist (`categories.js:107`), `categoryForDataType` maps it (`:208`), but **no sender exists anywhere in the repo**. PLANNED-DOC-ONLY.

## A.11 `restoreNotifications` — the launch re-lay (`scheduler.js:1179-1273`)

Called from `RootNavigator.js:1101` on session restore and from `rescheduleForTimezoneIfChanged` (`:1175`).

1. Early-return unless permission is exactly `'granted'`.
2. `cancelAllNotifications()` — wipes **everything**.
3. Resolves `isPro` from the store, **failing closed** to false when the store is unavailable (`:1195-1199`).
4. Pro + `morningEnabled` → morning + evening weigh-in prompts. Not Pro → `cancelEveningWeightReminder()`. The E10-F4 comment (`:1188-1194`) is explicit: a daily audible weigh-in prompt at someone who cannot act on it "is exactly the pressure pattern the ED rules exist to avoid".
5. Pro + `checkinEnabled` → `scheduleNextCheckinReminder`.
6. If `stageOf(profile) === 'pro_trial'` → re-lay cascade gates + trial day-3.
7. Re-lay win-back, missed-check-in pair, planned-meal confirm, activation nudge — each self-guarding.

**Not re-laid here:** training reminders (own key path, re-laid on foreground via `refreshHabitDerivedTrainingSchedule`), meal reminders, weekly-coach-ready (laid only at check-in submit), partner beats (laid on sync pull). Consequence: **meal reminders are wiped by `cancelAllNotifications()` on every launch and never re-laid** unless the user re-visits the settings screen. See §J.

## A.12 Timezone re-lay
`rescheduleForTimezoneIfChanged(userId)` (`scheduler.js:1165-1177`), called on every `AppState === 'active'` (`App.js:992-994`). Compares `new Date().getTimezoneOffset()` against `@volyume_notif_tz_offset`; on a change it re-runs `restoreNotifications` so quiet hours are recomputed for the new zone. First run records a baseline only. NOTIF-1 comment explains the bug: recurring triggers bake the shifted hour at schedule time.

## A.13 Notification preferences storage
Two parallel stores:
- **AsyncStorage blob** `@volyume_notification_prefs` — the operational source every scheduler reads. Keys observed: `morningEnabled`, `morningHour`, `morningMinute`, `eveningHour`, `eveningMinute`, `checkinEnabled`, `checkinDay`, `checkinHour`, `checkinMinute`, `trainingEnabled`, `missedCheckinEnabled`, `plannedMealConfirmEnabled`, `activationNudgeEnabled`, `partnerCheerEnabled`. Plus separate keys `@volyume_schedule_v1`, `@volyume_reminder_enabled_v1`, `@volyume_reminder_time_v1`, `@volyume_quiet_hours_v1`.
- **SQLite mirror** `notification_preferences(user_id, category, enabled, time_pref, updated_at)` — `preferences.js`, mirroring cloud migration 044 (+085, +125). Synced last-write-wins per row; `applyPreferenceFromPull` only overwrites when the server row is strictly newer (`:117-133`), fixing a Codex 2026-05-26 finding where pulls stamped `Date.now()` and echoed back. `migrateFromLegacyBlob` (`:223-260`) seeds three categories from the blob, backdated 1s. `deletePreferencesForUser` runs on sign-out/delete.

**Nothing reads the SQLite mirror to make a scheduling decision** — it exists for sync/analytics parity only. INTERNAL.

## A.14 Drift ledger — code vs `docs/NOTIFICATIONS_LOCKED.md`

| # | Locked doc says | Code does | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Training-day title "Today's a training day" | "One of your usual training days" (`trainingReminders.js:656`) | Deliberate, D17/founder 2026-08-03; doc stale |
| 2 | Category `daily_checkin_reminder` (19:00 local, configurable) | Enum exists; **no scheduler lays it**. The shipped daily habit prompts are `morning_weight` + `evening_weight` | Doc stale |
| 3 | `coach_trial_ending` via email | No email sender in the repo | PLANNED-DOC-ONLY |
| 4 | `subscription_expiring` push | Category + mapping exist; no sender | PLANNED-DOC-ONLY |
| 5 | Cascade at day 19/21 | Fires at trial-end − 2d and trial-end (day 12/14 of the 14-day trial); ids retained for cancel-matching | Documented in-code (E10-F6) |
| 6 | Budget priority ends `…monthly_recap, partner_cheer` | `planned_meal_confirm` inserted at rank 9; `activation_nudge` inserted at rank 3 | Founder-recorded in-code |
| 7 | Push budget addendum status "PROPOSED, not yet locked" | Fully implemented and enforced | Doc status stale |
| 8 | Activation nudge addendum "PROPOSED" | Fully implemented | Doc status stale |
| 9 | "One notification per topic per day max" | Enforced only for **event** categories inside `decideBudget`; habit categories are exempt by design | Documented deviation |
| 10 | — | `partner_streak` / `partner_joined` unmapped in `categoryForDataType` **and** unrouted | **Real defect** |
| 11 | — | `partner_cheer` routes to `ProgressTab`/`Consistency`, which carries no partner row (guard test pins its absence) | **Real defect** |
| 12 | — | `morning_weight`, `evening_weight`, `training_reminder`, `meal_log_reminder`, `activation_nudge`, `year_of_lifts_unlock`(routed), `subscription_payment_failure` — of these, five have **no route** and dead-end on tap | **Real gap** (the module header at `notificationRoute.js:6-7` states every scheduler type must have a route) |
| 13 | — | `App.js:130-142` installs a second, conflicting `setNotificationHandler` referencing a non-existent `rest-done` channel | **Latent defect** |
| 14 | — | `partnerCheerEnabled` is read by the scheduler but has **no UI toggle anywhere** (the code comment at `scheduler.js:1397-1398` says the screen "can surface it later") | **Missing disable path** vs the locked "every push has a clear unsubscribe path" principle |
| 15 | — | Meal reminders are wiped by `restoreNotifications`' `cancelAllNotifications()` and never re-laid on launch | **Real defect** |
| 16 | iOS permission requests `allowSound: false` | Six schedulers set `sound: true` | Effectively Android-only sound; see §J |

**Locked rules verified HELD in code:** ED-pattern flag never fires via push (no scheduler for `ED_PATTERN_LOCKOUT`; `CATEGORY_CHANNELS` is in-app only); quiet hours applied by every scheduler except the two documented exemptions; ED-flag suppression present at **schedule** time in morning/evening weight, trial day-3, win-back, missed check-in, planned-meal confirm, activation nudge, partner beats, and at **delivery** time in `handler.js`, with every ED read **failing CLOSED**; calm mode softens the monthly-recap body; tier-blindness of the guardrails is preserved (the tier gates decide *whether to schedule outreach*, never a floor or threshold).

# B. WIDGETS + LIVE SURFACES

## B.1 Snapshot pipeline (`src/lib/widgets/`)

`snapshot.js` — pure builder. `WIDGET_SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1`. Shape: `{ v, nextSession: {name, dayLabel, weekLabel} | null, consistency: {completed, planned, streakWeeks, label} | null, computedAt }`. Strings trimmed/clamped (name 40 chars, dayLabel 24), integers clamped 0-9999.
**Privacy (binding, `:16-19`):** "the home screen is semi-public, so the snapshot NEVER carries weight, calories, macros or any body data". `edFlagOpen: true` nulls the entire `consistency` block, and the widget falls back to neutral next-session content (COMP-018 rule).

`writer.js` — `gatherWidgetInputs(userId)` + `writeWidgetSnapshot(userId)`. Local reads only, no network. Suppression is **fail-CLOSED and doubled**: ED flag read → `'read_failed'` sentinel; wellbeing read → `'read_failed'`; `edFlagOpen = !!edFlag || wellbeing === 'read_failed' || isCalm(wellbeing)` (`:83`). `dayLabel` is **always null** (founder ruling 2026-08-03: the product has no scheduled training days — D17). `weekInBlock` suppressed when the block is `awaitingDecision` (Stage 1, 2026-08-09). `streakWeeks` mirrors the persisted **high-water run the user was actually shown this week** rather than re-deriving (T1, comprehension-trust audit 2026-08-06) — until the run is seen in-app that week the widget falls back to its sessions line.

`storage.js` — platform adapter. Always writes an AsyncStorage copy under `@volyume_widget_snapshot_v1` (the canonical source the Android headless task reads). Then:
- iOS: `require('live-activity').writeWidgetSnapshot(json)` → App Group `group.app.volyume.widget`, key `widget_snapshot_v1`, then `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()`.
- Android: `react-native-android-widget` `setWidgetPreferences` + `requestWidgetUpdate` for `NextSession` and `WeeklyConsistency`.
Never throws; a missing module is a benign no-op.

**Update triggers** (`writer.js:22-23` and confirmed call sites): workout finish (`ActiveWorkoutScreen.js:2241`), workout history change (`WorkoutHistoryScreen.js:307`), foreground→background (`App.js:916`). The header also claims "the existing background-fetch date rollover" — the `VOLYUME_DAILY_SYNC` task body (`App.js:102-124`) does **not** call the widget writer, so that trigger does not exist. See §J.

## B.2 Android home-screen widgets — **LIVE**

Configured in `app.json` plugins (`react-native-android-widget`, two widgets):
- `NextSession` — label "Next session", 180×110dp, 3×1 cells, `updatePeriodMillis: 1800000` (30 min), resizable both axes.
- `WeeklyConsistency` — label "Weekly consistency", 110×110dp, 2×1 cells, 30-min period, not resizable.

Renderers: `src/widgets/widgets.js`. Dumb RemoteViews via `FlexWidget`/`TextWidget`. Colours are **literal copies of `theme.js` tokens** because widgets render outside the theme pipeline (`:22-25`) — AMBER `#F5A623`, INK `#0D0D0D`, SURFACE `#191917`, RAISED `#222220`, CHIP `#2A2A27`, HAIRLINE `#2E2E2C`.
- `NextSessionWidget`: eyebrow "NEXT SESSION", plan/routine name, optional day chip (always absent — `dayLabel` is null by ruling), optional "Week N of M". Empty state: "No plan scheduled. Build one in Plans."
- `WeeklyConsistencyWidget`: eyebrow "THIS WEEK", "N of M" hero, neutral session dots (completed amber, remaining raised rings — "count, never judgement (no red, no shame)"), then "{N} weeks running" or the neutral "sessions" fallback. **When `consistency` is null (ED flag / calm mode / no data) it renders `NextSessionWidget` instead** (`:110`).

Task handler: `src/widgets/widgetTaskHandler.js`, registered at `index.js:8-18` behind `Platform.OS === 'android'` + try/catch.

**Tap behaviour:** the task handler header claims "Tapping a widget opens the app via the volyume:// deep link", but **no `clickAction` prop exists anywhere in `src/widgets/widgets.js`**. Grep for `clickAction|openApp|deepLink` in that folder returns nothing. Taps therefore do not carry any explicit action. See §J.

## B.3 iOS Live Activity + iOS home widgets — **LEGACY-UNREACHABLE (parked)**

The Swift and plugin work is complete and in-tree:
- `modules/live-activity/ios/LiveActivityModule.swift` (ActivityKit bridge + `writeWidgetSnapshot`), `ios/VolyumeRestTimerAttributes.swift` (shared), `widget/VolyumeRestTimerLiveActivity.swift`, `widget/VolyumeHomeWidgets.swift` (`VolyumeNextSessionWidget`, `VolyumeConsistencyWidget`), `widget/VolyumeWidgetBundle.swift` (`@main`).
- `plugins/withVolyumeWidget.js` — a real Expo config plugin that creates the `VolyumeWidget` app-extension target (bundle id `app.volyume.widget`, deployment target 16.1), copies the Swift sources + a generated Info.plist (`NSExtensionPointIdentifier = com.apple.widgetkit-extension`, `NSSupportsLiveActivities`) + entitlements, embeds the `.appex`, adds the target dependency, and is idempotent on re-prebuild.

**But the plugin is NOT wired into `app.json`.** `app.json` `plugins` contains no `./plugins/withVolyumeWidget` entry, and `src/lib/__tests__/liveActivity.wiring.test.js:121-129` **actively pins its absence**:

> "the widget extension is UNWIRED from the build as of 2026-07-12 (founder decision: the extension is a separate app identity that needs its own provisioned App ID / App Group profile, which is not set up, so an unprovisioned target fails App Store signing)."

A second guard (`:169-176`) pins that `ios.entitlements['com.apple.security.application-groups']` stays **undefined**, because declaring an App Group the profile does not carry fails archive signing. Universal links (Associated Domains) were dropped in the same decision for the same reason.

Consequences on a shipped iOS build today:
- `isAvailable()` returns false (`requireNativeModule` resolves, but no extension renders), so `Activity.request()` throws and is caught — **no Live Activity ever appears**.
- `writeWidgetSnapshot` reaches the native module but `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` returns nil without the entitlement — a safe no-op, not a crash (plugin header `:36-38`).
- **iOS has no home-screen widgets and no Dynamic Island surface.**

JS wiring is nonetheless complete and guarded: five lifecycle call sites in `useAppStore.js`, each lazy-required inside try/catch with a swallowing catch — `startRestActivity` (start rest, `endTimeMs: endsAt`, **no set numbering** by design), `updateRestActivity` (±15s), `endRestActivity` (stop and natural expiry), `endAllActivities` (launch sweep, also `App.js:598-601` to clear a stale Activity from a force-closed session). Pinned by `liveActivity.wiring.test.js:60-106`.

`docs/LIVE_ACTIVITY_IOS.md` is **stale**: it is headed "SCOPED, NOT BUILT | Date: 2026-06-09", describes the file restructure and plugin as work still to do, and says the plugin is "wired into `app.json` `plugins`" (§3) — neither the "not built" framing nor the wiring claim matches the tree. `modules/live-activity/widget/README.md` carries a correcting status block but still says "No manual Xcode steps are needed for a normal build", which is true only once the plugin is re-wired.

## B.4 Android live rest surfaces — **LIVE-COND (Android)**

Two mutually exclusive paths, chosen by rest length (`RestTimer.js:168-189`):
- **≤ 170s** (`REST_FOREGROUND_MAX_MS`, `restForeground.js:113`): the native `WorkoutForegroundService` hosts an Android **chronometer** notification via `startRestForeground` (`rest-timer-live`). Buys a countdown that stays LIVE on the lock screen while backgrounded, OS-reap protection, and JS execution while backgrounded so the 3-2-1 end cues fire. D34 added `+15s` and `Skip rest` action buttons natively, routed back through `getService` PendingIntents (never `getActivity`, so the app is never foregrounded), emitted to JS as `onRestTimerAction` and landing in the **same** `handleRestTimerAction` seam as the expo sticky.
- **> 170s**: the expo sticky (`presentRestTimerNotification`) with all five buttons.
The JS gate refuses to start a foreground for a rest the ~3-minute shortService window cannot cover end to end — "a countdown that dies mid-rest reads as a broken timer, which is worse than the frozen sticky" (`restForeground.js:109-113`).
`isRestForegroundAvailable()` returns false on older installed builds, which then keep the sticky path.

## B.5 Badge behaviour
- Every foreground handler return sets `shouldSetBadge: false` (`handler.js`, `App.js:139`).
- iOS permission requests `allowBadge: true` but nothing ever sets a badge count — no `setBadgeCountAsync` call exists anywhere.
- Android: only `coaching-reminders` sets `showBadge: true` (`channels.js:48`); all other channels false.
Net: **no numeric badge is ever driven by the app**; only the Android launcher dot for coaching-reminders notifications.
