# C. BACKGROUND BEHAVIOUR

## C.1 Registered background tasks (`App.js`)

| Task | Definition | Registration | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VOLYUME_REST_TIMER_KEEPALIVE` | `App.js:84-90` | **none found** — `defineTask` only, no `registerTaskAsync` | Body is a no-op returning `NEW_DATA`; "the act of waking the JS thread is what matters". **Defined but never registered → LEGACY-UNREACHABLE.** |
| `VOLYUME_DAILY_SYNC` | `App.js:102-124` | `App.js:703-709`, gated on `BackgroundFetch.getStatusAsync() === Available`; `minimumInterval: 12h`, `stopOnTerminate: false`, `startOnBoot: true` | Resolves the Supabase session, then calls **`syncAll({triggeredBy:'periodic'})`**. AC-02 (Codex audit 2026-07-12) rerouted this from `bulkUploadLocalData` so the Article 9 health-consent + sign-out-wipe gate applies; `syncAll` fails closed when consent cannot be proven. Pinned by `src/__tests__/syncConsentTriggerRouting.guard.test.js`. |

`app.json` declares `ios.infoPlist.UIBackgroundModes: ["fetch", "remote-notification"]`.

## C.2 Foreground/lifecycle work (not background tasks)
On `AppState` change (`App.js:900-1010`):
- any state (`active`/`background`/`inactive`) → `maybeSync()` (throttled).
- `background` → `writeWidgetSnapshot(uid)`.
- `active` → `syncAll('foreground')`, `rescheduleForTimezoneIfChanged(uid)`, `refreshHabitDerivedTrainingSchedule(uid)`.
Also on mount: OTA check via `expo-updates` (`checkForUpdateAsync` → `fetchUpdateAsync` → an Alert offering "Restart now", production only, `App.js:653-676`); `endAllActivities()`; `Linking.getInitialURL()`; quick-actions wiring; `ensureNotifChannels()`; year-of-lifts + monthly-recap checks off a single SQLite query.
Four sync triggers per `SYNC_ARCHITECTURE_LOCKED.md`: foreground, network reconnect (NetInfo), debounced write, and a 15-minute in-app interval.

## C.3 Steps + health — **LEGACY-UNREACHABLE (dark)**

`src/lib/health.js` is a full HealthKit / Health Connect wrapper (weight, steps, cardio read scopes; workout write scope planned) — **but**:

```
// Health Connect (Android) and Apple HealthKit (iOS) were removed entirely
// (founder 2026-06-30: the health-platform permissions were a Google Play
// review liability and the integration is not wanted).
function getIosModule() { return null; }
function getAndroidModule() { return null; }
```
(`health.js:100-107`)

Therefore `isHealthAvailable()` is **always false**, and every downstream function (`readStepsToday`, `readDailyStepTotals`, `readLatestWeight`, `readWeightsSince`, `importNewWeights`, `readCardioSessionsSince`, `importNewCardio`, `writeWorkoutToHealth`) returns its "unavailable" value immediately. Neither `react-native-health` nor `react-native-health-connect` is in `package.json` — the null getters are exactly what lets those dependencies stay dropped without a Metro resolution error.

`src/lib/activitySteps.js` is the caller-facing wrapper over that module. `isStepSourceAvailable()` is therefore permanently false, so **every step feature falls back to manual entry** (`database.setDailySteps`). The module writes nothing to the health platform by design.

`getHealthProviderLabel()` still returns "Apple Health"/"Health Connect" for a Settings row — any UI reading it would describe an integration that cannot connect. Permissions: **no health permissions are declared** in `app.json` (Android permission list is CAMERA, VIBRATE, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, WAKE_LOCK, SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM only), consistent with the removal.

`expo-sensors` is a dependency and `NSMotionUsageDescription` is declared for the **shake-to-send-feedback** gesture only — not for step counting.

## C.4 Store review prompts — `src/lib/storeReview.js`

- `incrementSessionCount()` on each completed session (`WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:749`), also stamping `volyume_first_session_at` on first use.
- `shouldPromptReview(now)` requires **both** gates: `REVIEW_PROMPT_AFTER = 10` completed sessions **and** `REVIEW_MIN_DAYS = 14` days since the first counted session. The comment records why: the old 5-session threshold could fire inside a single enthusiastic week and spend the one prompt the OS allows.
- `requestReview()` dynamically imports `expo-store-review`, checks `isAvailableAsync()`, then sets `volyume_review_prompted = 'true'` — **once ever**.
Single call site: `WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:750`. LIVE.

# D. PLATFORM DIFFERENCES

## D.1 Feature matrix

| Capability | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Local scheduled notifications | Yes | Yes |
| Notification **channels** | ignored | 4 registered (§A.2) |
| Notification **action buttons** | via `setNotificationCategoryAsync` (needs native build) | same + native FGS buttons (D34) |
| Foreground banner | needs `shouldShowBanner`/`shouldShowList` (iOS 14+) | legacy `shouldShowAlert` still honoured |
| Notification **sound** | requested OFF at permission level (`allowSound:false`) | channel-driven, `sound:true` effective |
| Live rest countdown | **none** (Live Activity parked) | chronometer FGS (≤170s) or static sticky |
| Rest-end alert | Yes (`rest_end`, "iOS's first lock-screen rest signal") | Yes, `rest-alerts` HIGH channel |
| Exact alarms | n/a (always true) | SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM declared; grant CTA on Android 12+ |
| Home-screen widgets | **none** (extension unwired) | 2 widgets, LIVE |
| Live Activity / Dynamic Island | **parked** | n/a |
| Quick actions (app shortcuts) | config-plugin static + runtime `setItems` | runtime `setItems` only (plugin does not support Android static actions) |
| Universal links (Associated Domains) | **dropped 2026-07-12** (signing) | `https://volyume.app` autoVerify intent filter present |
| Custom scheme `volyume://` | Yes (`expo.scheme`) | Yes (intent filter, autoVerify) |
| Health / steps | dark | dark |
| Tablet | `supportsTablet: false`, `requireFullScreen: true` | no tablet-specific config |
| Web | every notification/widget/push path early-returns `Platform.OS === 'web'`; `permissions` returns `'denied'` | — |
| Billing | App Store (`app-store-verify`, `app-store-notifications`, `_shared/appStore.ts`) | Google Play (`play-billing-rtdn`) |

## D.2 Build configuration

`eas.json` profiles: `development`, `development-device` (both `developmentClient`, internal), `preview` (internal, Android **apk**), `production` (node 20.19.4, `autoIncrement`, Android **app-bundle**, env `EAS_SKIP_AUTO_FINGERPRINT=1`, `RCT_USE_PREBUILT_RNCORE=0`, `RCT_USE_RN_DEP=0`). Submit: Android only, track `internal`. **No iOS submit profile in `eas.json`** — the iOS submit runs through the workflow.

`.github/workflows/build-android.yml`: triggers on push to `main` and `claude/**` (with docs/markdown `paths-ignore`) plus manual dispatch. Free GitHub runner. `main` and manual runs build `armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a`; `claude/**` pushes build `arm64-v8a` only as a compile check. Per-ref concurrency with cancel-in-progress. Pushes a status file back to the branch.

`.github/workflows/build-ios.yml`: **manual dispatch only** — "each EAS iOS build costs build credits, so this never auto-runs on a push". Inputs: `submit` (TestFlight, default true) and `skip_build`. Drives EAS with `EXPO_TOKEN` + App Store Connect API key (`ASC_API_KEY_P8`/`ASC_KEY_ID`/`ASC_ISSUER_ID`). Documents a day-costing gotcha: EAS reuses provisioning profiles, so adding a capability to the App ID later requires deleting the profile on expo.dev to mint a fresh one.

Other workflows: `main-ci.yml`, `deploy-functions.yml`, `deploy-migrations.yml` (manual-dispatch only), `deploy-pages.yml`, `identity-invariant.yml`, `maestro-e2e.yml`, `print-signing-sha.yml`, `refresh-off-snapshot.yml`.

Versions: `app.json` version `1.2.0`, iOS `buildNumber` 10, Android `versionCode` 30, `runtimeVersion.policy: appVersion`, `newArchEnabled: true`, RN 0.81.5 / Expo ~54.0.35 / React 19.1.

Android build properties: compileSdk/targetSdk 35, minSdk 26, `usesCleartextTraffic: false`, manifest queries for WhatsApp/SMS/mailto. iOS deployment target 16.0 (the widget extension would need 16.1).
`android.allowBackup: false`. `blockedPermissions`: RECORD_AUDIO, MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS, SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO.
iOS privacy manifest declares only `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults` reason `CA92.1`.
Two iOS usage strings are explicitly defensive: `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` and `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` both say the permission "is never requested" and exist only because a bundled library requires the key.

## D.3 Platform-branching code worth noting
85 `Platform.OS`/`Platform.select` sites. The load-bearing ones:
- `activeWorkout.js` — entire module Android-only.
- `restForeground.js:128` — Android + native-method presence + window fit.
- `widgets/storage.js:63-88` — the iOS/Android fork.
- `pushToken.js:396` — `platform: Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'ios' : 'android'` written to `device_push_tokens`.
- `permissions.js:23, 44` — web short-circuit.
- `payments/playBilling.js`, `payments/cascade.js`, `storeName.js` — store-specific copy and flows.
- `Chip.js` (via `Chip.a11y.guard.test.js:13-14`) — `minHeight: Platform.select({ android: 48, default: 44 })`.
- Date/time pickers (`PhotoDatePicker`, `EatenTimePicker`, `DiaryDatePicker`) — the usual iOS spinner vs Android dialog fork.

iOS ships via TestFlight (CLAUDE.md; `build-ios.yml` submits to TestFlight). Android is live on Google Play. Nothing in the tree gates features by store.

# E. SOCIAL / PARTNER SYSTEM

## E.1 Shape and intent
A **1:1 (up to 3 on Pro) accountability pairing** built entirely on **derived** signals. Classification from evidence: **accountability-first, motivational-second, and deliberately anti-competitive**. Supporting evidence:
- `sharedStreak.js:10-24` — a partner resting HOLDS the streak; a quiet week HOLDS it and "no copy ever attributes the quiet week to a person… the deliberate inversion of Duolingo's break-and-unpair".
- `intention.js:8-16` — COPY LAW: allowed "aim", "kept your week"; **banned** "must", "don't let them down", "you're behind", any cross-person comparison, any number that ranks one above the other. Pinned at source by `partnerComparison.guard.test.js`.
- `moments.js:26-28` — copy is "first names only, no numbers, no exercise names, full-stop endings, no exclamation marks".
- `partnerBeats.js:12-15` — the cheer push is framed as FROM the partner, never from the app ("the Duolingo nudge lesson"); "no shame framing exists anywhere in the partner system by design".
- `PartnerScreen.js:11-15` — "no cross-pair totals, no ordering by performance… no guilt or urgency or counters-as-pressure. Resting never reads as a fail."
It does **not** feed the coaching engine: no partner module is imported by `planEngine`/`nutritionEngine`/`weeklyCoach`/`coachApply`. The relationship to coaching is one-directional — the coaching engine's *outputs* (week state, deload, PB, block completion) are reduced to booleans that flow outward.

## E.2 Invitation / link flow
1. **Mint** — `createPartnerInvite(userId, {streakEnabled})` (`service.js:189-210`) calls RPC `create_partner_invite`. The server generates the code and stores only its **hash**; the plaintext is returned once. Emits `partner_invite_sent` + `trackInviteMinted()`.
2. **Single-mint cache** — `inviteCache.js`: a module-scoped cache holding the ONE pending code so all four share channels (Text / WhatsApp / Email / share sheet) reuse it. Header records the bug: each channel used to mint its own invite, which could create several simultaneous invites and hidden active partnerships. `INVITE_EXPIRY_DAYS = 7`, exported so UI copy reads the real number.
3. **Links** — `link.js`: `volyume://partner/<CODE>` and `https://volyume.app/partner/<CODE>`. Codes are uppercase alphanumeric, `^[A-Z0-9]{8,}$`, parsed case-insensitively with trailing path/query/fragment stripped. Share message (`inviteShareMessage`): *"Be my training partner on Volyume. You will see whether I trained this week, one daily cheer, and any win I choose to send. No food, photos, body metrics or feed."* — the privacy promise travels with the link. **"NO in-app user search or discovery of any kind"** (`link.js:5-6`).
4. **Deep-link capture** — `App.js:212-229` `handlePartnerDeepLink`: parses the code, calls `rememberPendingPartnerCode`, then polls `navigationRef.isReady()` up to 12 times at 500ms (~6s of cold-start grace) before navigating to `Partner` with the code. Returns true so auth handling is skipped.
5. **Paywall preservation** — `pendingInvite.js`: an invited free/logged-out user hits the Pro guard, which renders ProLocked **without reading the code param**, so the code was silently dropped. `savePendingPartnerCode` persists it to `@volyume_pending_partner_code` with a timestamp **and** fires `trackInviteDiedAtPaywall()`; `readPendingPartnerCode` honours the same 7-day expiry and fails closed to null. `usePartners.js:382` auto-redeems the pending code once the user lands eligible (Pro, no active pair).
6. **Redeem** — `redeemPartnerInvite(userId, code)` (`service.js:219-271`) calls RPC `redeem_partner_invite`, which enforces not-self / not-expired / single-use / not-blocked and **raises one indistinguishable `invite_invalid` on every failure path** (no enumeration oracle). Handles both RPC shapes (pre-102 bare uuid, post-102 `{partnership_id, partner_first_name}`).

## E.3 Consent — `consent.js` + `migrate_102_partner_safety_consent.sql`
Sharing a derived attendance signal with a second named human is treated as a **new processing purpose**. `recordPartnerSharingConsent(userId, {granted})` writes an append-only `consent_log` row through the SECURITY DEFINER RPC `record_partner_consent`, carrying `_notice_version` (`PARTNER_PRIVACY_NOTICE_VERSION = 3`), app version and platform. It rides the **same rail as the Article 9 health-data consent**.

**Fail-closed on accept** (`service.js:242-250`): if the consent write fails, the just-redeemed partnership is rolled back via `end_partnership` (which purges and tombstones it) and the user sees the same calm redemption failure — *"no sharing begins without a recorded consent"*.
Withdrawal is best-effort ("the user must always be able to leave").
Cloud-side only — `consent_log` has no local mirror. Version 3 was bumped when the deletion-promise footer line was restored and the full receipt began rendering on the empty state (L06-F2/F3, D5).

## E.4 What partners see of each other

**The only automatic signal** is the derived week row, `partner_week_signals`: `{pair_id, user_id, week_start, planned_count, done_count, week_met, state}` (+ `completed_block`, `hit_pb`). Written by `weekSignalWriter.writeOwnWeekSignals` (`:132-160`), which reuses `computeWeekState` — "one consistency engine" shared with COMP-018.

| Surface | Module | What crosses |
|---|---|---|
| Week ticks | `signals.ticksLabel` | "3 of 4" **relative to the partner's own plan**; never a raw metric |
| Row state | `signals.partnerRowState` | `empty` / `pending` / `resting` / `active` / `ended` |
| Row line | `signals.partnerRowLine` | one shared derivation used by both PartnerRow and the You-tab row, so copy lives in one place and "a resting partner never reads as a fail" |
| Shared streak | `sharedStreak.computeSharedStreak` | joint week state (met/resting/quiet), run, longest, status; archives after 4 consecutive quiet weeks |
| Weekly intention | `intention.resolveIntention` | your own aim number; the partner's aim is acknowledged **without its number** whenever the two differ, so two figures are never comparable |
| Milestone moments | `moments.getVisibleMoments` | `partner_joined`, `streak_week_kept`, `completed_block`, `hit_pb` — fixed copy, names only, **no numbers** |
| Cheer / acknowledgement | `acknowledgements.ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS` | one of a closed 4-item enum |
| Win cards | `shareWins.*` + `service.sendPartnerWinCard` | one explicitly chosen update at a time |
| Shared blocks | `service.proposeSharedBlock/adopt/leave` | `block_name` (80-char cap), `status`, `proposed_by` |
| Support plan | `supportPlan.buildPartnerSupportPlan` | the "what {Name} sees" receipt |

**Acknowledgement set (closed enum, no free text)** — `acknowledgements.js:22-27`, mirroring the server CHECK in `migrate_106_partner_cheer_kind.sql`:
`proud` "Proud of your week." · `good_back` "Good to see you back." · `strong_both` "Strong week, both of us." · `here` "Here with you." (default). One send per pair per **local day**, mirrored client-side by `signals.cheerAllowed` so the button disables instantly, and enforced server-side by `UNIQUE(pair_id, sender_id, sent_on)`.

**Milestone moments engine** (`moments.js`) — entirely local, never a push, never a new sync surface:
- Kinds + priority: `partner_joined` (−1) > `streak_week_kept` (0) > `completed_block` (1) > `hit_pb` (2).
- Caps: at most **one rendered moment per pair per local day**; `hit_pb` additionally capped at **2 per pair per rolling 7 days**; nothing older than 7 days is ever surfaced.
- Fixed copy: "Another week you both showed up." / "{Name} finished their training block." / "{Name} set a new personal record." / "{Name} joined you."
- **Suppression is FAIL-CLOSED and recipient-side**: open ED flag, a FAILED flag read, SCOFF ≥ 2, calm mode, or a FAILED wellbeing read all return `[]`. The header is explicit that `getWellbeingMode` is **never** used here because it swallows read failures open.
- Deterministic ids (`pair:kind:weekKey`); `markMomentSeen` is the only writer. Persistence keys `@volyume_partner_moments_{seen,shown,pb}_v1`.

**Win cards** (`shareWins.js`) — four types: `workout_summary`, `personal_record`, `block_milestone`, `progress_card`. Each declares explicitly what is shared vs what stays private. `SHARE_WIN_POLICY.defaultState = 'Ask every time'`; `excluded` = "No passive feed, leaderboard, workout history browsing, food diary, coach notes, body metrics or automatic photo sharing." The `progress_card` type shares **a text summary only — "The image itself is never sent."** Review steps: choose → preview exact update → confirm one partner → keep the sender delete control. `SHARE_WIN_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS` + `shareWinDraftHasForbiddenFields` + `validateShareWinDraft` enforce it in code. Revocation: `service.revokePartnerWinCard`.

**Support-plan receipt** (`supportPlan.js`): `PARTNER_SUPPORT_PRIVACY_LINE = 'Private: full workout details, food, Coach check-ins, body metrics and photos.'`

## E.5 Privacy / visibility enforcement
`src/lib/partners/__tests__/partnerPrivacy.guard.test.js` is a **source-level structural guard** over the two client cloud-write surfaces (`service.js`, `sync/tables/partners.js`): the only columns a client may serialise are an explicit allowlist — `pair_id, user_id, week_start, planned_count, done_count, week_met, state, blocker_id, blocked_id, id, created_at, updated_at, block_name, proposed_by, status`. Any new column (a careless `body_weight:` or `avg_kcal:`) fails the test and must be a deliberate reviewed addition. The §5 contract quoted: *"derived only — NEVER raw weights, sets, reps, body weight, measurements, photos, food, calories, diary, check-ins, coach messages, or location"* (`docs/bp-partner-system-rebuild.md:38-41`).

**The ED/wellbeing freeze is at source, outbound** (`weekSignalWriter.js:9-13, 102-108`): an open flag or a positive wellbeing screen freezes the outbound state to `'resting'` — *indistinguishable from a planned deload* — and forces **both** milestone booleans (`completedBlock`, `hitPb`) false through the same freeze, so a celebratory moment can never leak out of a wellbeing hold. The partner cannot tell a wellbeing hold from recovery.

Additional guards in `src/lib/partners/__tests__/`: `partnerNames.guard.test.js`, `partnerCheerEdge.guard.test.js`, `partnerIntentionPurge.guard.test.js`, `weekSignalScoff.guard.test.js`, plus `service.test.js` (621 lines) and `moments.test.js` (303).

## E.6 Tier gating

| Layer | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Route | `Partner` is wrapped in `withProGuard(…, 'Training partner')` | `RootNavigator.js:223, 516` |
| Cap | free = 1 partner, Pro = 3 | `signals.maxPartnersForTier` / `canAddPartner`; used at `usePartners.js:338, 369, 410, 536` |
| Data layer | `tierGate.isLapsedPartner()` — a user whose tier resolves to **`'free'`** has their outbound signal transitioned to `'resting'` with milestones forced false | `tierGate.js`, applied at `weekSignalWriter.js:141-152` and in `sync/tables/partners.js` |
| Entry points | Coach home (`YouScreen`) Partners row is **lock-aware** (`pro={!isPro}`); Analytics promotes a Partners tile; ConsistencyScreen carries **no** partner row; HomeScreen stays free of any partner entry (one-banner invariant) | `partnerPlacementSpine.guard.test.js:5-13` |

`tierGate.js` deliberately does **not** use the ED fail-closed pattern: an UNKNOWN tier (null during bootstrap) does **not** count as lapsed, because "muting a paying Pro on a transient/unresolved read is the worse failure; only an explicit `'free'` resolution (a real churn) mutes" (`:14-19`).

**Tension worth flagging:** the free cap of 1 partner (`maxPartnersForTier`) is unreachable through the UI, because the only partner destination is wholly Pro-gated. The free-tier code path exists for the lapse case and for the lock-aware entry row.

## E.7 Removal / unlink / blocking
- `unpairPartner(userId, pairId)` → RPC `end_partnership` (`service.js:437-441`), which **purges + tombstones** (`migrate_092_partner_end_purge.sql`). Emits `trackUnpair()`.
- `blockPartner(userId, blockedId)` (`service.js:415`) → `partner_blocks` row (`blocker_id`, `blocked_id`).
- Consent withdrawal writes `granted: false` on the same append-only rail; best-effort by design.
- Sign-out clears the invite cache (`clearCachedInvite`) and the pending code.

## E.8 Empty states
- `PartnerScreen` empty state **is the pitch**: the full `PartnerPrivacyReceipt` (D5/L06-F2: the abbreviated summary was replaced by the full receipt, and the deletion promise restored — hence `PARTNER_PRIVACY_NOTICE_VERSION = 3`).
- `signals.partnerRowLine`: `empty` → "Train with a partner"; `pending` → "Invitation sent. Waiting for your partner."; `resting` → "{Name}: resting this week"; `ended` → "Partnership ended."
- Invite journey is a **three-beat full-screen modal** ("what this is" / "what crosses" / "send") that mints exactly one code; each beat emits `trackInviteJourneyStep(1|2|3)`.

## E.9 Partner telemetry (INTERNAL, counts only, no PII, no free text)
`partners/telemetry.js`, riding `engineTelemetry` → `record_engine_telemetry` RPC. Direction-3 adoption set: `partner_surface_view` (`you_row|consistency_row|progress_tile|post_workout`), `partner_invite_journey_step`, `partner_invite_minted`, `partner_invite_redeemed`, `partner_invite_died_at_paywall`, `partner_cheer`, `partner_unpair`, `partner_pair_week_active` (week 2 or 6 only, watermarked once per pair per milestone at `weekSignalWriter.js:113-126`). Sits **alongside** the legacy funnel events `partner_invite_sent`, `partner_invite_accepted`, `partner_cheer_sent`, `partner_blocked`, `partner_block_left`. All on both allow-lists (`src/lib/telemetry/events.js:188-210`; server `migrate_102`).

## E.10 Partner cloud schema
`migrate_081_training_partners.sql` (base), `092` (end purge), `100` (shared blocks), `102` (safety consent + telemetry allow-list + redeem RPC shape), `105` (weekly intention), `106` (cheer kind), `107` (win cards).

# F. SHARING

## F.1 The renderer
`src/lib/shareCard/drawShareCard.js` (923 lines) is a **single pure Skia draw routine used for BOTH the on-screen preview and the exported PNG** — "what you see is exactly what you share". Header (`:4-8`) records the bug it replaced: the preview (RN views) and the export (a hand-coded HTML canvas in a hidden WebView) were two independent renderers that drifted. Written against the JsiSk* API so `scripts/render-share-card.cjs` renders the identical code path under CanvasKit in Node. 1080-wide design space scaled by `s = W/1080`; text is measured with the active font.
Five card types (review correction): `pr`, `milestone`, `weekly`,
`beforeAfter` (`:917-920`) plus the `session` card in the trailing `else`
(`drawShareCard.js:921` → `drawSession`, working sets/duration/tonnage/
exercise list/top set/intensity tier/units) — and `session` is the FIRST
segment and the default on ShareCardScreen (`:422`, `cardType: 'session'`
built at `:224`).
Palette is a documented DESIGN_SYSTEM whitelist exception (an offline canvas, not a screen), tracking `theme.js` values; `border` was corrected from a fill colour to `#6E6E6E` for WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 because outlines vanished under platform re-compression.

## F.2 Surfaces
| Surface | File | Card |
|---|---|---|
| Share card screen (hub) | `src/screens/ShareCardScreen.js` | pr / milestone / weekly |
| Workout summary | `src/screens/WorkoutSummaryScreen.js` | pr / weekly |
| Coach output | `src/screens/CoachOutputScreen.js` | weekly recap (`greatWeek.buildWeeklyRecapParams`) |
| Lift progress | `src/screens/LiftProgressScreen.js` | pr |
| Analytics / Year of Lifts | `src/screens/AnalyticsScreen.js`, `YearOfLiftsScreen.js` | milestone / recap (`recapPayload.buildRecapMilestoneData`) |
| Body metrics | `src/screens/BodyMetricsScreen.js` | — |
| Progress photos | `src/screens/ProgressPhotosScreen.js` → `src/components/BeforeAfterShareSheet.js` | beforeAfter |
| Scan label | `src/screens/ScanLabelScreen.js` | — |

## F.3 Destinations
- **System share sheet** — `expo-sharing` `Sharing.shareAsync(uri, {mimeType:'image/png', UTI:'public.png'})`, guarded by `isAvailableAsync()`.
- **Save to gallery** — `expo-media-library` `requestPermissionsAsync()` then `saveToLibraryAsync(uri)`. Declined permission produces a calm "You can still share it." toast, never a block.
- **Instagram Stories** — `ShareCardScreen.js:374-401`: the `instagram-stories://share` deep link cannot carry the rendered image, so the flow routes through the normal share sheet with a direct-composer intent (`com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_STORY`).
- Outbound app links generally: `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes: ["whatsapp","sms","mailto"]` (iOS) and Android `manifestQueries` for `com.whatsapp` + SENDTO/VIEW sms/mailto.
Every optional native module is `require`d in a try/catch, and a missing one produces "isn't available on your device", never "you're on an incomplete build" (P-16, `BeforeAfterShareSheet.js:401-405`).

## F.4 GDPR ban and the single approved exception — **VERIFIED IN CODE**

CLAUDE.md §2: share cards never include name/bodyweight/measurements/private notes, with **one** founder-approved exception (progress-photos programme, 2026-07-03): the Pro before/after progress card may show bodyweight beside each photo, and is withheld entirely under calm mode or an open ED flag.

`src/components/BeforeAfterShareSheet.js:13-23` states the same contract verbatim, and the code enforces it:

1. **Withheld entirely under suppression.** `usePhotoSuppression()` returns true when **calm mode is on OR an open ED-pattern flag exists**, both **raw fail-closed reads** (`usePhotoSuppression.js:6-9, 44-51`): the wellbeing read uses raw `AsyncStorage.getItem(WELLBEING_KEY)` + `isCalm`, explicitly **never** the failure-swallowing `getWellbeingMode` helper, and a `'read_failed'` sentinel on either side suppresses. `withGeneratedFile` aborts before compose/encode/share: `if (useAppStore.getState().tier !== 'pro' || suppressed) return;` (`:404`). The **whole card is withheld, not merely weight-stripped**.
2. **Pro-gated with a live re-check** — the same line re-reads tier at generation time so a pro→free flip mid-flow cannot generate.
3. **Weight is an explicit per-export opt-in.** `showWeight` defaults to **false** (`:165`), is a `Switch` (`:601`), and `buildBeforeAfterParams` emits a weight string **only** when `showWeight && kg != null && Number.isFinite(kg)` (`beforeAfterParams.js:83-85`).
4. **Export receipt** — the sheet prints "Weight: {included|off}" before sending (`:622`).
5. **Name / measurements / private notes stay banned** — `buildBeforeAfterParams` emits only `date`, `weight`, optional `scanRange`, `elapsedLabel`. No name field exists in the beforeAfter param shape.
6. **One-time confirm** before the first export: "Create an image to share" / "You're making an image from your photos. It stays on your device until you choose to share or save it."
7. **Single composited file, never a multi-attach, never a raw photo file** (`:9-10`, S2 §1). A deleted/corrupt photo aborts with a calm toast rather than compositing a blank cell.
8. Elapsed time is stated plainly and "never framed as a transformation" (`beforeAfterParams.js:13-14`).

## F.5 Other card builders
- `greatWeek.js` — `isGreatWeek(output)` gate + `buildWeeklyRecapParams(output, {suppress, includeProgress, units, …})`; `GREAT_WEEK_HEADLINE` exported.
- `recapPayload.js` — `buildRecapMilestoneData`; note the in-code honesty comment (`:29-32`) that the "kg lifted" label is hard-coded and is "a latent lie for any lbs user".

# G. ACCESSIBILITY

## G.1 Preferences
`src/lib/accessibilityPrefs.js` is a thin AsyncStorage reader (`A11Y_PREFS_KEY = '@volyume_a11y_prefs'`, `loadA11yPrefs()` returns null on any error = "use defaults"). The prefs themselves live in the store (`useAppStore.js:1900-1980`):

| Pref | Effect |
|---|---|
| `largerText` | 1.2× multiplier over the `fontSize` tokens in `applyAccessibility` (`theme.js:440`) |
| `higherContrast` | brightens muted text + thickens borders (`theme.js:436`, `lightHC`/`darkHC` token sets) |
| `colorBlindSafe` | swaps red/green success/error to blue/orange (`theme.js:437`, `lightCVD`/`darkCVD`) |
| `reduceMotion` | **effective** value = `systemReduceMotion \|\| reduceMotionUserPref`; skips PRCelebration particles, RestTimer pulse, big spring animations |
| `reduceMotionUserPref` | the user's own in-app toggle; Settings reads/writes THIS (AX-09) |
| `energyUnit` | `'kcal' \| 'kj'` — food-UI energy **display** unit, read reactively, display-only |
| theme | light/dark/system, resolved by `applyAccessibility` |

`systemReduceMotion` is hydrated from `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` on every cold boot and kept live via a `reduceMotionChanged` subscription (`App.js:560-573`), which recomputes the effective `reduceMotion` (`useAppStore.js:1968-1978`).
A legacy-migration path seeds `reduceMotionUserPref` from the old `reduceMotion` field (`useAppStore.js:1936-1946`).

**Boot ordering matters and is deliberate:** `bootstrapAccessibility()` runs **before** `RootNavigator`/`PRCelebration` are lazily required, because those transitively trigger every screen's `StyleSheet.create` and the tokens must already be mutated (`App.js:143-147, 158-179`). `Appearance.setColorScheme()` is then called to align native surfaces (keyboards, pickers, OS alerts) with the in-app choice — COMP-029, requires `userInterfaceStyle: "automatic"` (present in `app.json`) plus a native rebuild.
CP-10 stage 2: `App()`'s own `StatusBar` reads the **live** `useTheme()` hook so a theme flip re-renders the status bar with no restart.

## G.2 Sheet isolation — `src/lib/sheetA11yIsolation.js`
D36c (2026-07-10). `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` renders through a React **portal** (a sibling of the app tree), not a native `Modal`, so Android does not get the automatic "background is a separate accessibility window" isolation — TalkBack could still reach the screen behind an open sheet. The header records that gorhom exposes **no** accessibility-containment prop, so there was nothing to defer to.
Design: a module-level **counter** (not a boolean), so stacked sheets keep the host screen hidden until *every* sheet has closed. Deliberately outside React context/Zustand ("ephemeral cross-tree UI plumbing, not session state"), avoiding threading a prop through 82 screens. `BottomSheet.js` calls `incrementOpenSheets()`/`decrementOpenSheets()` on visible transitions including unmount-while-open. `SheetIsolationBoundary` (exported here, not inlined in RootNavigator, so it is testable in isolation) sets `importantForAccessibility` (Android) / `accessibilityElementsHidden` (iOS) and restores `'auto'`/`false` the instant the count hits zero. Uses `useSyncExternalStore`. Test: `src/lib/__tests__/sheetA11yIsolation.test.js`.

## G.3 Font scaling / dynamic type
`src/__tests__/accessibilityDesign.guard.test.js` pins app-wide:
- No file uses `allowFontScaling={false}` — "text remains eligible for system font scaling" (`:39`).
- **No screen re-introduces the blanket 1.3× cap** `maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.3}` (EP-14, `:48`).
- Text inputs never use the generic placeholder accessibility label (`:30`).
- Native stack headers stay hidden so screens use the shared app chrome (`:64`).
- Tab-bar border styling flows through the theme token only (`:74`).

`src/components/__tests__/Chip.a11y.guard.test.js` closes a hole that guard missed: `Chip` had smuggled the cap back via a **default function parameter** (`maxFontSizeMultiplier = 1.3`), which the regex-based blanket guard (matching only the JSX form) could not see, and its 36dp geometry was under the 44dp minimum. The guard now pins both the absence of any numeric default and `minHeight: Platform.select({ android: 48, default: 44 })`.

Other component a11y suites: `Stepper.a11y.guard`, `InfoTooltip.a11y`, `ScreenHeader.a11y`, `AppAlert.a11y`, `ExercisePickerModal.a11y`, `BackHeader.a11y`. `eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y` is a devDependency, so role/label conventions are lint-enforced.

## G.4 Haptics vocabulary — `src/lib/haptics.js`
A closed semantic vocabulary over `expo-haptics`, every call wrapped so a failure is silent (`_impact`/`_notify` at `:85-90`):

| Function | Feedback |
|---|---|
| `setLogged()` | Impact Light |
| `warmupLogged()` | Selection |
| `prAchieved()` | custom pattern (`PR_ACHIEVED_PATTERN_IOS`) |
| `restDone()` | custom pattern (`REST_DONE_PATTERN_IOS`) |
| `restAlmostDone()` | Impact Light |
| `restCountdown(stage)` | staged |
| `planReady()` | Notification Success |
| `selection()` | Selection |
| `press()` | Impact Light |
| `workoutComplete()` | composed |
| `error()` | Notification **Warning** (never Error — no alarm framing) |
| `commit()` | Impact Medium |

Screen-reader labels: enforced by convention + the per-component a11y suites above; `PartnerScreen.js:11-15` states the working rule — "every touchable role+labelled".

# H. OBSERVABILITY (INTERNAL)

## H.1 Sentry — `src/lib/sentry.js`
- Initialised as early as possible at module scope (`App.js:56-65`). No-ops when the SDK is absent or `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is unset.
- **DSN pre-validated in JS** against `/^https?:\/\/[^@\s/]+@[^/\s]+\/\d+$/` after trimming, because sentry-android continues init on a background thread and a malformed DSN throws an uncatchable Java exception that kills the process with no log, no tombstone and no event (`:54-71`).
- `environment`: `'development'` under `__DEV__`, else `'production'`.
- `tracesSampleRate`: **0.05 in production**, 1.0 in dev (`:89`).
- `maxBreadcrumbs: 150` (raised from the SDK's 100 because the observability layer emits a crumb per screen change, action, store action and DB query).
- `enableAutoSessionTracking: true`, `attachStacktrace: true`.
- `release`/`dist` deliberately **unset** so the SDK auto-detects and matches the plugin-uploaded source maps (a manual release with no dist previously left every production stack trace minified).
- **`beforeSend` and `beforeBreadcrumb` FAIL CLOSED**: if the scrubber itself throws, the hook returns `null` (drop) rather than the untouched input — "A dropped crash report is an acceptable cost; a leaked event is not." No payload is logged in the catch, only a boolean signal (`:106-135`).

## H.2 Scrubbing — `src/lib/observability/sentryScrub.js`
Single source of truth, locked in `PRIVACY_CONSENT_LOCKED.md:178-191`. `MAX_DEPTH = 6` (bounds a pathological circular ref), replacement token `[redacted]`.
- `SENSITIVE_KEY_PATTERNS` — `^weight`, `^body[._-]?weight`, `^bf[._-]?pct$`, `^body[._-]?fat`, `^ffm`, `^fm[._-]?kg`, `^height`, `^kcal`, `^protein`, `^carbs?`, … plus PII identifiers.
- `SENSITIVE_VALUE_SUBSTRINGS` — table names (`weight_log`, `food_entries`, `custom_foods`, `body_composition_log`, …); a string containing one is redacted wholesale since "it likely carries row data or SQL".
- Photo file paths and base64 image payloads are redacted.
- `ed_pattern_flags` references and `signals_json` are redacted.
- API: `isSensitiveKey`, `scrubValue`, `scrubObject`, `scrubEvent`, `scrubBreadcrumb`.
- A **quarterly CI audit** (also locked) asserts the scrub rules still match the schema; adding a matching field fails the build until the list is updated. Tests: `src/lib/__tests__/sentryScrub.test.js`.

## H.3 Error log — `src/lib/errorLog.js`
- Ring buffer in AsyncStorage, **200 entries**, most recent first; stack capped at 1,800 chars, message at 600. Viewable from Settings → Debug logs.
- `installGlobalHandlers()` (called at `App.js:51`) catches uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections.
- **On-device redaction is at least as wide as the wire-to-Sentry scrub**: the same `scrubValue` + a `redactPII` pass run before anything is written locally (`:41, 90-123`).
- `VERBOSE_LOGGING` is `__DEV__`-only; the buffer + Sentry breadcrumb still fire either way.
- **Sentry flood guard** (`_shouldForwardToSentry`, `:182-213`, from `docs/audit/sentry-triage-2026-07-27.md`), deliberately bounded to the wire only — the on-device buffer is never throttled. `_resetSentryThrottleForTests()` is the test seam.
- API: `logError(scope, error, context)`, `logWarn`, `logInfo`.

## H.4 Engine telemetry
`src/lib/engineTelemetry.js` is a one-line re-export shim: `track = postEvent`, `flushPendingTelemetry = flushPending`, both from `./telemetry/transport`.
`transport.js` gating, in order (`:60-70`):
1. **LB-9 analytics opt-out** — dropped **before persisting**, so "an opted-out user generates no analytics at all". Hydrated before the first foreground (`App.js:576-579`).
2. **Allow-list** — `ALLOWED_EVENTS` (`src/lib/telemetry/events.js`, 267 lines, `{name, deferred, panel}` triples). An unlisted event is dropped.
3. Persist locally, debounce-flush via `record_engine_telemetry`, flushing **only rows belonging to the user whose session signs the RPC** (`:92`); a failed row is skipped and retried next flush rather than breaking the batch.
Notification events: `notification_sent`, `notification_tapped`, `notification_failed` (panel 6). Partner events: 13 names (panel 1), mirrored by the server allow-list in `migrate_102`.
`src/lib/telemetry/sentryBridge.js` and `firsts.js` complete the folder.

## H.5 No-PII verification
- Sentry: `beforeSend`/`beforeBreadcrumb` scrub, fail-closed.
- errorLog: same scrub applied on-device before write.
- Telemetry: closed allow-list + explicit "counts only, NO PII, no free text" contracts (`partners/telemetry.js:1`, `activationNudge` telemetry note in the locked doc: "counts/flags only, never a session date, weight or any body value").
- Widgets: snapshot privacy is structurally guarded (`liveActivity.wiring.test.js:158-167` strips comments and SwiftUI `weight: .bold` modifiers, then asserts the widget source never matches `/weight|kcal|calorie|macro|bodyfat/i`).
- Partner cloud writes: column allow-list guard (§E.5).
- Push tokens: cached under a key `sync.js` explicitly excludes from preference sync, "because tokens are device-bound and must never sync across devices" (`pushToken.js:300-302`).

# I. DEEP LINKS

## I.1 Registration
- `app.json` `expo.scheme: "volyume"`.
- Android intent filters (both `autoVerify: true`): scheme `volyume`, and `https://volyume.app`.
- iOS: custom scheme only. **Universal links / Associated Domains were dropped 2026-07-12** for the same signing reason as the widget extension (`liveActivity.wiring.test.js:21-22`), so `https://volyume.app/...` links do **not** open the iOS app.

## I.2 React Navigation `linking` config (`RootNavigator.js:759-817`)
`prefixes: ['volyume://', 'https://volyume.app']`

| URL | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `volyume://workout/start` | `HomeTab` → `BuildWorkout` | |
| `volyume://diary` / `volyume://diary/:date?` | `DiaryTab` → `Diary` | optional local day-key `YYYY-MM-DD`; invalid values ignored, never a crash |
| `volyume://routine/:planId` | `PlansTab` → `PlanDetail` | param **must** be `planId` — the old `:id` left `planId` undefined and dead-ended on a blank screen (audit 2026-07-01) |
| `volyume://progress` | `ProgressTab` → `Analytics` | |
| `volyume://coach` | `ProfileTab` → `CoachOutput` | defaults to the current week, matching the `weekly_coach_ready` target |
| `volyume://checkin` | `ProfileTab` → `WeeklyCheckIn` | |

Auth gating is **implicit and safe**: the config only names screens inside `MainTabs`, so when the user is signed out or mid-onboarding those routes do not exist and React Navigation leaves them where they are rather than crashing. Pro-gated destinations still render their `withProGuard` prompt — "the link only navigates, it never bypasses a gate".

## I.3 Links handled outside the `linking` config
| Link | Handler |
|---|---|
| `volyume://partner/<CODE>`, `https://volyume.app/partner/<CODE>` | `App.js:212-229` — persists the code, then polls `navigationRef` up to ~6s and navigates to `Partner` |
| Supabase auth callbacks (PKCE `code=`, implicit `access_token` fragment) | `handleIncomingDeepLink` in `App.js`; failure surfaces "Couldn't sign you in / That link may have expired." (`App.js:186-201`, A2-004) |
| `volyume://active-workout` | Passed as `deepLink` to the native rest/workout foreground services (`restForeground.js:148`, `activeWorkout.js:471`). **No `active-workout` route exists in the `linking` config** — see §J |
| `data.url` on any notification | `App.js:684-689` — a second response listener that calls `Linking.openURL(url)` for any `volyume://` value. **No scheduler sets `data.url`**, so this path is currently inert |

## I.4 Quick actions (launcher shortcuts)
`expo-quick-actions`. iOS static actions via the config plugin (`app.json`); both platforms also set them at runtime because the plugin does not support Android static actions (`App.js:621-648`). Two actions:
- `workout` — "Start workout" / "Build today's session" / `symbol:dumbbell.fill` → `HomeTab`/`BuildWorkout`
- `diary` — "Log food" / "Open your food diary" / `symbol:fork.knife` → `DiaryTab`/`Diary` (Pro-gated by `withProGuard`; no special case, the guard renders the upgrade prompt)
`QUICK_ACTION_ROUTES` is kept in lock-step with the equivalent deep links (`App.js:231-241`). Cold launch via `QuickActions.initial`, warm via `addListener`, both polling `navigationRef.isReady()`.

## I.5 Outbound links — `src/lib/links.js`
`privacyPolicy: https://volyume.app/privacy` (hardcoded here per `PRIVACY_CONSENT_LOCKED.md:280` so the marketing site and in-app link change together), `marketing: https://volyume.app`, `supportEmail: support@volyume.app`.

## I.6 Consolidated notification tap destinations
`routeForNotificationType(type, data)` — `notificationRoute.js:25-90`. Navigation happens in `RootNavigator.js:906-928` with `initial: false` (F6b: tabs are lazy; without it a notification tapped before its tab was ever focused would mount the stack with the target as its ONLY route, stranding the tab root for the whole session), retrying up to 20× at 150ms until `navigationRef.isReady()`.

| `data.type` | Destination |
|---|---|
| `weekly_checkin` | `ProfileTab` → `WeeklyCheckIn` |
| `year_of_lifts_unlock` | `ProgressTab` → `YearOfLifts` |
| `monthly_recap` | `ProgressTab` → `Analytics` |
| `cascade_gate` | `ProfileTab` → `CascadeGate` `{variant:'day14'}` |
| `weekly_coach_ready` | `ProfileTab` → `CoachOutput` |
| `winback` | `ProfileTab` → `Subscription` `{fromWinback:true}` |
| `partner_cheer` | `ProgressTab` → `Consistency` **(screen has no partner row — §A.14 #11)** |
| `checkin_missed` (`slot==='followup'`) | `ProgressTab` → `Analytics` |
| `checkin_missed` (evening) | `ProfileTab` → `WeeklyCheckIn` |
| `planned_meal_confirm` | `DiaryTab` → `Diary` |
| `diary_day` | `DiaryTab` → `Diary` `{date}` when `data.date` matches `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, else Diary root. **No scheduler sets this type yet** — the mapping exists so the first one to need it has somewhere to land |
| `trial_day3` (`variant==='S3'`) | `HomeTab` |
| `trial_day3` (other) | `ProfileTab` → `WeeklyCheckIn` |
| **`morning_weight`** | *none* |
| **`evening_weight`** | *none* |
| **`training_reminder`** | *none* |
| **`meal_log_reminder`** | *none* |

# J. UNCERTAINTIES

Recorded, not guessed. Each names what could not be resolved read-only.

1. **iOS sound on push content.** `permissions.js:28-32` requests `allowSound: false` on iOS, yet six schedulers set `content.sound: true` (morning/evening weight, training reminder, rest end, year of lifts, monthly recap). Whether iOS silently drops the sound or whether the request-time flag is later widened by another call could not be determined from the tree. On Android the channel governs, so `rest-alerts` and `coaching-reminders` sound regardless.
2. **Android widget tap target.** `widgetTaskHandler.js:8-9` states "Tapping a widget opens the app via the volyume:// deep link", but no `clickAction` prop exists in `src/widgets/widgets.js`. Whether `react-native-android-widget` supplies a default launch action for a widget with no `clickAction` is a library-behaviour question I cannot answer read-only.
3. **`volyume://active-workout`.** Passed as the `deepLink` to both native foreground services, but the route does not appear in the `linking` config or in `QUICK_ACTION_ROUTES`. Whether the native side falls back to a plain app-launch intent, or whether this is a dead link, needs a device check.
4. **Meal reminders lost on launch.** `restoreNotifications` calls `cancelAllNotifications()` and re-lays eight things, but not `scheduleMealReminders`. On the code as read, a user's opt-in meal reminders are wiped on every launch and only restored if they re-enter the settings screen. I found no compensating re-lay; a device walk should confirm.
5. **`VOLYUME_REST_TIMER_KEEPALIVE`.** Defined at `App.js:84-90` with no `registerTaskAsync` anywhere. Either an intentional retirement or an omission — the intent is not recorded in code.
6. **Widget background-fetch trigger.** `writer.js:22-23` lists "the existing background-fetch date rollover" as an update trigger; `VOLYUME_DAILY_SYNC` does not call the widget writer. It is possible the snapshot updates indirectly via the sync path, but no call chain proves it.
7. **`send-push` channelId.** Server messages use `channelId: 'default'`, which is not one of the four channels the app registers. Whether Android falls back to a system default channel or drops the notification could not be determined from the repo.
8. **`daily_checkin_reminder`.** The locked doc treats it as a shipped category with a 19:00 default; nothing lays it. Whether `morning_weight`/`evening_weight` were intended to supersede it, or whether a scheduler was lost, is not recorded.
9. **`partnerCheerEnabled`.** Read by `schedulePartnerBeats`, no UI toggle. The in-code comment frames this as deferred, but no decision record was located. Against the locked "every push has a clear unsubscribe path" principle this reads as an open gap rather than a decision.
10. **`getHealthProviderLabel()` consumers.** The function still returns "Apple Health"/"Health Connect" although the integration is structurally dead. I did not trace every Settings screen to confirm whether a row still describes a connectable integration.
11. **`docs/LIVE_ACTIVITY_IOS.md` status.** Headed "SCOPED, NOT BUILT (2026-06-09)" and claims the plugin is wired into `app.json`; the tree shows the plugin fully written and deliberately unwired (2026-07-12). Which document the founder considers current is not recoverable read-only — the *test* is authoritative on the build state, but the doc has not been updated to match.
12. **`subscription_expiring`.** Category, channel routing and `categoryForDataType` mapping all exist; no sender does. Whether the sender is planned, was removed, or lives outside this repo is not recorded.

# CHAPTER D2 — DOCUMENTATION ARCHAEOLOGY, BOUNDARIES, LEGACY, TERMINOLOGY, TEST-REVEALED BEHAVIOUR (covers PARTS 25, 27, 28)

# D2 — Documentation archaeology, intentional product boundaries, legacy/dead code, terminology, test-revealed behaviour

Read-only survey of `/home/user/ADPhysique` at commit `1267c568`, branch
`claude/codebase-audit-docs-pv6mjd`, date 2026-08-09. Nothing in the repository
was modified.

**Evidence standard used throughout**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| LIVE | Reachable by a real user on a shipped build; proven by an import/route/call chain in `src/`. |
| LIVE-CONDITIONAL | Reachable only under a named runtime condition (tier, flag, platform, data state). |
| INTERNAL | Exists and runs, but only for developers/CI/scripts, never a user surface. |
| LEGACY-UNREACHABLE | Present in the tree, no non-test caller. Dead by reachability, not by intent. |
| PLANNED-DOCUMENTED-ONLY | Described in a document; no shipping implementation found. |
| UNCERTAIN | Evidence incomplete or contradictory; recorded, not resolved. |

A note on method for Part A: I record only what a document **states**. Where a
document's claim and the code disagree, both are given, and the disagreement is
listed again in Part E.6 (contradictions). I did not infer boundaries from
absence of code.

---

# PART A — INTENTIONAL PRODUCT BOUNDARIES

## A.1 The authority chain (read this first)

Boundaries in this repository are recorded in four places, in descending
authority:

1. `CLAUDE.md` — Section 2 "INVIOLABLE CONSTRAINTS", Section 4 "WORKFLOW RULES".
   Amended in place; the file states which older rules are superseded.
2. `docs/ux-world-class-audit-2026-07-09/DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md` (2,365 lines,
   decisions D8 to D91) — the live founder decision register. Its own preamble
   (lines 4-7): *"These are settled. Do NOT re-surface any REJECTED or HELD item
   as a suggestion in future sessions; the founder's direction is to strengthen
   what exists until it ties together as world class, not to propose additions
   that were ruled out."*
3. `docs/TASKBOARD.md` §4 "HELD / NEVER RE-PROPOSE (visible in one place - do
   NOT build or re-surface)" (lines 1491-1502) — the single consolidated list.
4. `docs/*_LOCKED.md` — 21 locked contract documents, each of which states the
   date it was locked and (in several cases) later founder overrides in a
   banner at the top.

`docs/BACKLOG.md` and `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md` carry their own hard-exclusion
lists but **both are banner-marked SUPERSEDED/CLOSED as of 2026-07-10**
(`docs/BACKLOG.md:1`, `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md:1`). Their exclusions are recorded
below with that provenance flag: they are historical statements of intent, not
current authority. The current authority for the never-list is TASKBOARD §4 plus
the decision register.

## A.2 The boundary register

Format: **NOT IN SCOPE** | RATIONALE IF RECORDED | WHERE RECORDED | code
verification where I ran one.

### A.2.1 Engine and intelligence

**No AI / LLM anywhere in the coaching engine. Deterministic only.**
- Rationale recorded: `CLAUDE.md` Section 2 verbatim: *"The coaching engine is
  deterministic. No AI. Ever. No LLM calls, no randomness, no rewrites that alter
  outputs for identical inputs. Engine modules stay pure (no I/O). If a feature
  seems to need AI: stop and ask."*
- Also recorded in `docs/BACKLOG.md` NEVER table (SUPERSEDED banner):
  *"AI / LLM-assisted plan generation | Coach Builder is deterministic by design
  (same inputs → same plan). LLM integration is explicitly excluded. If
  reconsidered, requires separate consent flow and clear labelling."*
- Re-affirmed at `DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md:418` (D27 addendum): *"The coaching
  engine's no-AI rule was never in question and stands absolutely."*
- Code verification: the adaptive-stage test suites assert engine purity
  directly — `src/lib/__tests__/blockSeed.stage6.test.js:187`,
  `blockExplain.stage8.test.js:250`, `blockLedgerGather.stage6.test.js:273`,
  `learnedRange.stage5.test.js:326` each carry a test named
  *"no clocks, no randomness, no I/O, no store, tier-blind"*. Status: **LIVE**
  boundary, mechanically enforced.

**AI-assisted FOOD input (photo meal-scan, voice logging) — HELD, not rejected.**
- Rationale recorded verbatim, `DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md:414-419` (D27 addendum,
  founder 2026-07-10): *"Hold the AI I'm not sure it's good enough or accurate
  enough for use."* Ruling: *"HELD by founder order - not rejected, not approved;
  do not build and do not re-propose unprompted."*
- Also `docs/TASKBOARD.md:1501`.
- **Important distinction a reviewer must not blur:** this is a separate,
  weaker status from the engine no-AI rule. The engine rule is absolute and
  permanent. This one is a hold that the founder could lift.
- `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md:530` (SUPERSEDED doc) lists *"AI photo logging (never)"* —
  a **stronger** wording than the live D27 addendum. Flagged as a doc-vs-doc
  conflict in Part E.6.

**No auto block transitions. Every mesocycle transition is user-confirmed.**
- Rationale recorded: `docs/blueprint-adaptive-mesocycle-2026-08-09.md:108-110`
  (§1.8, answering a direct founder question): *"Blocks do NOT run forever by
  design - plannedWeeks is fixed (5 standard / 6 advanced) - but **nothing ever
  transitions automatically**. `getBlockStatus` walks active -> recovery ->
  complete -> overdue; PlansScreen shows the advisor's proposal; the user must act
  (`activatePlanWithBlock` creates the next block)."*
- Re-stated as a design constraint at §3.5 (line ~230): *"Transitions stay
  user-confirmed (the advisor's philosophy holds), but the limbo ends"*.
- Also §3.4 (line ~226) for the recovery-window length: the 10-day window is a
  *"proposal, never auto"*.
- Code verification: `src/lib/__tests__/blockLifecycle.stage1.test.js:1-12`
  header pins *"no new mesocycle is ever created without explicit user action"*
  and asserts `completed_awaiting_decision` is a first-class state whose week
  index never wraps back to week 1. **LIVE**, test-pinned.

**Exercise change is never automatic.**
- `docs/blueprint-adaptive-mesocycle-2026-08-09.md:72`: *"Exercise change: never
  automatic; plateau banner suggests, user acts."*

**Research MEV is a landmark, not a recovery-week minimum.**
- FOUNDER RULING verbatim, `DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md:2305-2313` (D91-14):
  *"Research MEV remains a safety reference but should not force a deload UPWARD
  when a percentage-based recovery dose is appropriately lower … MEV is a
  productive-training landmark, not automatically a recovery-week minimum."*
  Recovery-week lower clamp is `deloadFloor` = half of research MEV, never below
  one set (`coachApply.deloadFloor`). Pinned with the founder's sentence:
  *"Greater strain can only make a recovery prescription easier or longer; it can
  never make it harder or shorter"* (`deload.stage7`).

### A.2.2 Identity and account model

**No anonymous mode; no local-user migration path.**
- `docs/IDENTITY_AND_OWNERSHIP_LOCKED.md`, "Four locked decisions" #1:
  *"No anonymous mode. Tapping Free on Welcome routes to sign-up. Every user has
  a real account from the first row they create. There is no `anon:` identity, no
  `@volyume_anonymous_local_id`, no `initLocalUser` flow."*
- "Anti-patterns to never reintroduce" list: anonymous local mode of any kind;
  `migrateLocalUserId` or any function that updates `user_id` on existing rows;
  "Continue locally" or any sign-in-skip path; suppressing 42501 errors;
  "reclaim ownership" of another user's cloud rows; "re-mint id on conflict".
- Rationale recorded (doc preamble): locked 2026-05-24 after *"a 400-row 42501
  cascade exposed three design flaws: row `user_id` was mutated after creation,
  anonymous and account identities were conflated, and row IDs could collide
  between users in the cloud."*
- Header line: *"If code conflicts with this doc, the code is wrong."*
- Enforcement, verified: `scripts/check-identity-invariant.sh` greps
  `SET user_id` across `src/` and fails unless a `LOCKED-OK` comment sits in the
  preceding 10 lines; wired to CI in `.github/workflows/identity-invariant.yml`
  on push to `main` and `claude/**` plus every PR. **LIVE**, CI-enforced.
- Code verification: `src/screens/WelcomeScreen.js:62-74` carries the comment
  *"Per IDENTITY_AND_OWNERSHIP_LOCKED.md decision 1: no anonymous mode"* and the
  single CTA routes to `Login` with `intent: 'pro_signup'`.

**Sign-out wipes local data; `AsyncStorage.clear()` with no carve-outs.**
- Same doc, decision #2 and scenario C: *"App calls `AsyncStorage.clear()` — every
  key gone. No carve-outs for accessibility prefs, crash log, install counters, or
  anything else. Same hammer as delete-account."*

**One deliberate survivor of account deletion: the salted trial-ledger hash.**
- Same doc, "One deliberate exception (migration 071, trial-abuse prevention)":
  a salted SHA-256 hash of the account email in `private.trial_ledger` is NOT
  deleted by `delete_user_data`. Rationale recorded: *"It exists so the 14-day
  cardless trial cannot be restarted by deleting and re-signing-up with the same
  email … Lawful basis: legitimate interest (preventing trial fraud); disclosed
  in the privacy policy."*
- Contract-tested: `src/lib/__tests__/trialLedger.contract.test.js` (Part D).

### A.2.3 Data, privacy and residency

**EU-Dublin data residency is absolute.**
- `CLAUDE.md` Section 1: *"Backend: Supabase EU-Dublin … EU data residency is
  absolute — all user data stays in Dublin. Components NEVER query Supabase
  directly; everything flows through the sync layer."*
- Re-stated in Section 2 under GDPR/Article 9.

**Article 9 health-data consent gate must not be weakened, reordered, or made
skippable; consent flows fail CLOSED for new users.**
- `CLAUDE.md` Section 2 verbatim: *"The un-skippable consent gate in RootNavigator
  (healthConsent) must not be weakened, reordered, or made skippable … Consent
  flows fail CLOSED for new users (a transient read failure must not bypass the
  gate)."*

**Share cards never include name, bodyweight, measurements or private notes —
with exactly one named exception.**
- `CLAUDE.md` Section 2: *"share cards never include name/bodyweight/
  measurements/private notes — with the single founder-approved exception
  (progress-photos programme, 2026-07-03) of the Pro before/after progress card,
  which may show bodyweight beside each photo; that card is withheld entirely
  under calm mode or an open ED flag, and name/measurements/private notes stay
  banned on it."*
- Related audit with lead rulings already made: `docs/audit/share-card-audit-2026-07-27.md`.

**No PII to Sentry or any analytics.**
- `CLAUDE.md` Section 1 Observability: scrubbing in
  `src/lib/observability/sentryScrub.js`, `tracesSampleRate 0.05`, *"No PII to any
  external service."*

**Progress photo image files never leave the device.**
- `docs/BUDGET_POSTURE_LOCKED.md` deferral table: *"Photo progress timeline |
  v1 on-device only, no cloud sync ever | Photos are personal record. OS-level
  backup (iCloud Photos, Google Photos) covers loss protection. No Supabase
  Storage write at any version saves bandwidth and storage permanently."*
- `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md:527` (SUPERSEDED doc) repeats: *"Photo cloud sync (photos
  stay on-device forever)."*
- Code verification: `src/screens/__tests__/privacyTruth.guard.test.js` pins the
  Article 9 consent string *"Progress photo image files stay on this device"* and
  *"Never use your photos or health data for advertising or third-party model
  training"*.

### A.2.4 ED-safety (stated as inviolable, not merely out of scope)

`CLAUDE.md` Section 2, "ED-safety system — do not touch":
- Calorie floors 1,500 kcal men / 1,200 kcal women. *"Never lower."*
- FFM energy floor (30 kcal/kg), rapid-loss gate (1.5% BW/week), max-safe-loss
  (0.8%). *"Never remove, raise thresholds, or make conditional."*
- Beat UK signposting and calm mode: *"never remove or gate."*
- *"Guardrails are tier-blind (proGate.js mandate) — they never consult tier."*
- *"Weight/food-adjacent notifications suppress under an open ED flag; never
  weaken that suppression."*
- Instruction on contact: *"If a task touches any of this: STOP and ask first."*

Two decision-register rulings extend the ED boundary into the new adaptive
system and are worth quoting because they are behaviour, not policy:
- D91-11 (`DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md:2288-2292`): *"§3.8's 'no upward carry-over
  anywhere' binds the learned MEMORY, not just live proposals: a block trained
  under calm mode or an open ED flag never raises the learned ceiling - even
  after the flag clears - while its downward evidence still folds."*
- D91-19 (`:2344-2348`): *"Suppression (calm mode OR open ED flag) withholds
  deloadSets entirely: a flagged user's recovery week stays the flat research-MEV
  week. Block carry-over never raises a recovery week."*

# PART B — LEGACY / DEAD / DUPLICATED CODE

Method: for each candidate, `grep -rn <symbol> src App.js scripts` excluding
`__tests__` and the definition file itself. A symbol referenced only by its own
module and its tests is classified **LEGACY-UNREACHABLE**. I make no deletion
proposals; several of these are deliberately retained, and at least one is
deliberately retained *because* a cloud migration depends on it.

deleted.**
- `src/lib/database.js:4394`: *"Stage 6 (2026-08-09): the dead createMesocycle
  function is DELETED."*
- `src/lib/__tests__/blockLifecycle.stage1.test.js:78-117` contains a test named
  *"createMesocycle stays deleted (Stage 6 resolved the dead code)"* which
  asserts zero occurrences of `createMesocycle(` in `database.js` and scans the
  tree for offenders.
- Status: resolved. This is the model the repo uses for intentional deletion.

## B.9 Duplicated calculations and shadow implementations

### B.9.1 e1RM — three implementations, one ruled canonical
1. **`algorithms.calculate1RM`** (`src/lib/algorithms.js:77-101`) — the mandated
   one. Blended Epley/Brzycki with a **rep clamp at 20**: *"1RM estimators lose
   validity past ~12-15 reps, and Brzycki's denominator runs towards its pole as
   reps climb, so a 25-30 rep set used to return a wildly inflated estimate (≈5x
   the weight at 30 reps) that fired spurious 1RM PRs."* Weighting: `epley*0.6 +
   brzycki*0.4` at ≤10 reps, plain mean above.
2. **`bestLift.epleyE1rm`** (`src/lib/bestLift.js:26-32`) — plain Epley
   `w * (1 + reps/30)`, no clamp. It survives as the **default parameter** of
   `pickBestLift`. Its own header records the ruling that removed it from the live
   path: *"getBestLiftThisWeek (database.js) instead passes calculate1RM
   (algorithms.js) as the third argument: X4 (cross-surface consistency audit
   2026-07-30) ruled that the weekly tally must conform to the SAME
   blended/clamped formula the live in-session PR detector uses, not a separate
   plain-Epley formula, so the featured 'best lift' agrees with the weekly PR
   count on the same card."*
3. **A plain-Epley SQL expression that USED to live in `database.js`** — now a
   comment recording its removal, `database.js:6167-6174`: *"plain-Epley e1RM
   (weight * (1 + reps/30)) in SQL, with no rep clamp, no …"*, and `:6276`,
   `:6297` (*"the NULLIF(...,0)-to-1 SQL gave the plain-Epley formula, so a 0-rep
   row …"*).
- **Assessment:** the duplication is real but is a *default-argument* residue
  plus historical comments, not a live divergence. The ruled-canonical formula is
  `calculate1RM`. `blockMetrics.stage3.test.js` header restates it: *"e1RM via the
  app's single mandated calculate1RM (X4 ruling)"*.

### B.9.2 Week-start — unified, and the unification is pinned
- Canonical: `src/lib/dayKey.js` exports `localDayKey`, `todayLocalKey`,
  `parseLocalDay`, `localWeekStartMs` (:53), `localWeekEndMs` (:73). UK-local,
  Monday-anchored.
- Consumers verified: `useProgressData.js:258,412`, `useWeeklyStreak.js:59`,
  `usePartners.js:197-198,277,651`, `blockLedgerRunner.js:122-123`,
  `checkinDerive.js:17`, `database.js:6`.
- `checkinDerive.getCurrentWeekStart` is a **thin wrapper**, not a second
  implementation: *"Local Monday 00:00 of the current week (UK-local, never UTC).
  Returns a Date so the existing callers … are unchanged in shape."*
- The unification was forced by a real defect and is pinned:
  `src/screens/__tests__/HomeScreen.weekBoundaryConsistency.guard.test.js` header
  (X5/X11, cross-surface consistency audit 2026-07-30): HomeScreen's *"Sessions
  this week"* used a rolling trailing-7-day window while the free coach line on the
  **same screen** used the Monday anchor — *"Sun + Mon + Tue with today Wednesday
  could show '3' and '2' on one screen."* Ruled: *"every 'this week' count goes
  through the shared Monday-anchored dayKey.js helpers … no surface computes its

- Residual local weekday maths that is NOT week-start maths and is legitimately

# PART C — TERMINOLOGY MAP

Scope: what the product **says** versus what the code **calls it**. I record
collisions; I propose no wording changes. Frequencies are `grep -oi` counts over
`src/` excluding `__tests__`.

## C.1 Programme / plan / routine / template — four words, three concepts

| Word | Where it lives | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **programme** | Code identifier and SQL table: `programmes` table (`database.js:252`, `:408`), `programme_id` column on `routines` (`:248`, `:407`), `programmes.is_active`, `programmes.next_workout_index`, `programmes.tags` (`:417-419`). ~208 occurrences in `src/`. | A container of routines. |
| **plan** | The dominant **user-facing** word. ~5,093 occurrences. Screens: `PlansScreen`, `PlanDetailScreen`, `PlanLibraryScreen`, `PlanUpdateScreen`, `PlanPreviewScreen`. Engine: `planEngine.js`, `planAutoGen.js`, `planDisplay.js`, `plan_folders` table. | What the user activates and follows. |
| **routine** | Code + some UI. ~1,142 occurrences. `routines` and `routine_exercises` tables; `RoutineDetailScreen`. | One session template inside a plan. |
| **template** | ~156 occurrences, thinnest of the four. | Used loosely for library/starting-point content. |

**Collision 1 (two words, one thing):** `programme` (data layer) and `plan`
(presentation layer) name the same object. `PlansScreen.js:312` shows both in one
comment: *"'Continue this programme') are true repeats"*. `PartnerScreen.js:1005`
logs `PartnerScreen.loadProgrammes`; `:1670` comments *"suggest one from the
user's programmes"*. The user never sees a "programmes" list; they see Plans.

**Collision 2 (one word, two levels):** "plan" is used both for the whole
multi-week programme *and* for a single day's session ("today's plan"). Also,
`planEngine.js` computes weekly **volume targets**, not the plan object — so
"plan" spans the container, the day, and the volume prescription.

**Live-conditional note:** `PlanPreviewScreen` is a **dark route** (B.4). Its
"plan preview" vocabulary is not currently user-visible.

## C.2 Block / mesocycle / training block / phase — one concept, three surface words and a code word

| Term | Register | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `mesocycle` | **Code only**, ~517 occurrences. Tables `mesocycles`, `mesocycle_weeks`; `src/lib/mesocycle.js`; screen file named `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js`. | `database.js:273`, `:461` |
| "Training block(s)" | **User-facing**, the screen title. | `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js:170` `<BackHeader title="Training blocks" />`; `PlansScreen.js:1176` `accessibilityLabel="Training blocks"`; `ConsistencyScreen.js:113` `<SectionLabel>Training block</SectionLabel>`; `WelcomeScreen.js:37` marketing bullet *"Training blocks and full progress stats"*; `YearOfLiftsScreen.js:377` fallback name `'Training block'` |
| "Block" (bare) | User-facing, ~2,532 occurrences incl. code. | `WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:898` eyebrow `'Block finished'`, `:1418`; `HomeScreen.js:1400` |
| "training phase" | User-facing, a **different** concept (see C.7) but appears beside blocks. | `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js:337` *"Training blocks start when you activate a plan. Activate one to track week-by-week progress across a training phase."* |

**A deliberate unification, worth quoting because it is recent and is the reason
the vocabulary is now consistent.** D91-1 (`DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md:2226-2231`):
*"One finished-block name everywhere: 'Block finished' (chip, sheet, Plans,
ActiveWorkout banner, Training blocks, CoachOutput note, WorkoutSummary
celebration + share eyebrow). The old 'complete' / 'overdue' split and the mixed
'Block complete' labels read as two states and two products; one state, one
name."*
Verified in the tree: `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js:213`, `:385`;
`WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:898-899`, `:1418`; `HomeScreen.js:1400`. The internal
state names remain distinct (`completed_awaiting_decision`, `weeksOverdue` —
`blockLifecycle.stage1.test.js:22-31`), which is exactly the intended split: one
user word, several engine states.

**Residual collision:** the screen file is `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js` and the
route is `MesocycleBuilder`, while its own header renders "Training blocks". A
reviewer navigating by filename will use a word no user sees.

## C.3 Recovery week vs deload — deliberate, and the mapping is one-way

- **User-facing word: "recovery week."** ~112 occurrences of the phrase.
  `HomeScreen.js:1614` *"Recovery week suggested"*; `:1607`
  `accessibilityLabel="Recovery week suggested. Tap to review."`;
  `CoachOutputScreen.js:382` *"Take a recovery week"* / *"Recovery week set for
  next week"*; `:428` *"Next week is your recovery week, so the coach will not add
  sets to it. Recovery weeks stay light on purpose."*;
  `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js:213` *"· recovery week"*.
- **Code word: "deload."** ~742 occurrences. `shouldDeload`, `isDeload`,
  `nextWeekIsDeload`, `deloadApplied`, `handleApplyDeload`, `computeDeloadVolume`,
  `deloadShare`, `deloadFloor`, `deloadSets`, `predictDeloadWeek`,
  `evaluateDeloadTriggers`, `generateDeloadPrescription`, `deload_week` column
  (migrate_129), `deload.stage7.test.js`.
- **A third softer variant exists in prediction copy:**
  `MesocycleBuilderScreen.js:371` *"A lighter week is likely in about N weeks."*
  So the same concept surfaces as **recovery week**, **lighter week**, and
  **deload** depending on the site. The jargon blocklist (Part D.3) is why
  "deload" does not reach copy.
- **Collision:** "deload" also appears in the phrase *"deload flag"* meaning the
  *trigger*, not the week — `blockLedgerGather.stage6.test.js` header:
  *"deloadFlagMidBlock means the flag fired BEFORE the peak week"*. One code word,
  two referents (the prescription and the signal).

## C.4 Sets: working sets / effective sets / direct sets / secondary credit

| Term | Register | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **working set** | Code comments + some copy. `algorithms.js:138` *"counts as a full working set"*; `database.js:2732` *"Only working sets (set_type != 'warmup') are counted"*; `haptics.js:100` *"Logging a working set. Soft confirmation, not loud."* | A non-warm-up logged set. The unit of volume. |
| **effective set** | **Code only, and unreachable.** `algorithms.js:1348` *"Effective set weighting by RIR proximity, continuous curve per Robinson et al. (2024 …)"*; `calculateEffectiveSets` (`:1366`) has **zero callers** (B.2). | RIR-weighted set count. |
| **direct set** vs **secondary half-credit** | Engine-internal, and load-bearing. D91-17 (`DECISIONS:2331-2336`): *"achieved peaks carry secondary half-credit while planned rows count direct sets"*. `algorithms.allocateExerciseVolume` is the allocator. | Primary muscle counts 1, secondary counts 0.5. |
| **fractional working set** | `planEngine.js:305` *"fractional working set (spec phase 3e, RP convention of half a set)"*. | Same 0.5 convention, different name, different module. |

**Collision (one thing, three names):** the half-set convention is called
*secondary half-credit* (interBlock/deload), *fractional working set* (planEngine),
and *indirect volume* (`planEngine.js:360` *"Indirect-volume trim"*).
**Collision (one name, two meanings):** "effective sets" in the code means
RIR-weighted sets, but a reader coming from the training literature may take it
to mean the same thing as "working sets". Since the RIR-weighted implementation
is unreachable, no user ever sees the distinction.

## C.5 RIR — computed internally, deliberately not asked of the user

- The per-set RIR picker was **built and deliberately removed**
  (`docs/BACKLOG.md`: *"Per-set RIR was built and deliberately removed
  (`SetEntry.js:173-176`). `DEFAULT_SET.rir = 2` still set internally so the engine
