- "RIR" is on the **jargon blocklist**: `jargonBlocklist.test.js` asserts
  `checkJargon('leave 2 RIR on the bar').clean === false` and
  `checkJargon('stay at 7 RPE').clean === false`.
- So RIR is a live engine input (`getSetEffectivenessWeight(rir)`,
  `computeSetTargets` RIR contract, deload *"intensity RIR 4 from the ladder"* per
  blueprint §1.7) that the user never enters and never reads.

## C.6 Readiness vs recovery grade — two scales, two owners

| Term | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **readiness** (user-facing, pre-workout) | `WorkoutSummaryScreen.js:183, 405, 449, 474, 659-672` (`preWorkoutReadiness`: soreness24hBefore, sleepQuality); `ReadinessCards.js`; `ConsistencyScreen.js:17` | A pre-session self-report. |
| **readinessSlope** (engine, block-scale) | `blockLedgerGather.stage6.test.js` header: *"readinessSlope is the NORMALISED TOTAL change across the block (last minus first readiness, 0-100 scale, divided by 100): a 30+ point decline reads <= -0.3"* | A 0-100 trend across a block. |
| **recovery grade** (engine, weekly, 1-4) | `weeklyCoach.js:254` *"observed recovery grade 3 in the block's PEAK week"*; `:291` *"`recoveryForPush` is the week-context-adjusted recovery grade"*; `:871` | The recovery axis of the 4x4 recovery × performance matrix. |
| **"Profile readiness"** (a THIRD meaning) | `AthleteProfileScreen.js:193, 200, 206` — `label: 'Profile readiness'` | **How complete the user's profile is.** Nothing to do with fatigue. |

**Collision (one word, three meanings):** "readiness" means a pre-session
self-report, a 0-100 block trend, and **profile completeness** on
`AthleteProfileScreen`. The last is the sharpest collision found in this sweep.
**Collision (two words, one axis):** the user reports "readiness"; the engine
grades "recovery". The mapping is not surfaced.
Note also `blockLedgerGather.stage6.test.js`: `workouts.soreness_24h_before` is
**1-3** while interBlock's `sorenessLateAvg` is **1-5**, remapped 1→2, 2→3, 3→4.
Two scales for one signal, reconciled in one module.

## C.7 Goal vs phase — three parallel vocabularies for the same user answer

`src/lib/coachingGoals.js` is explicit about this and is the single best artefact
in the repo for understanding it. Its header (`:1-20`) states the conceptual
model:
- `PHYSIQUE_GOALS` → *"Which body are you building?"* (volume distribution) —
  *"the optional, secondary question, most users default to 'general'. Competitive
  lifters pick their division."* Values: `general` ("Not competing"),
  `mens_physique`, `classic_physique`, `bodybuilding`, `bikini`, `wellness`, …
- `TRAINING_PHASES` → *"What are you focused on right now?"* (calories + plan
  tuning + emphasis) — *"the primary, prominent question."*
- And it records its own history: *"Previous shape had these two concepts mixed:
  PHYSIQUE_GOALS used to include 'general_hypertrophy' / 'strength_hypertrophy' /
  'weak_point_spec' which weren't physique categories at all. Those moved into
  TRAINING_PHASES … `migrateProfileGoals()` handles the data migration."*

**Each TRAINING_PHASE carries three different keys** (`coachingGoals.js:220-291`),
which is the three-vocabulary structure the brief asked about:

| User label | `value` (profile/UI) | `nutritionKey` (nutritionEngine `PHASE_ADJUSTMENTS`) | `coachingPhaseKey` (planEngine `NUT_MULT`, weeklyCoach `phaseConfig`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build muscle (lean gain) | `lean_gain` | `lean_gain` | `mild_bulk` |
| Build muscle (bulk) | `bulk` | `build` | `bulk` |
| Strength + size | `strength_size` | `build` | `bulk` |
| Bring up a weak point | `weak_point` | `lean_gain` | `mild_bulk` |
| Lose fat (cut) | `cut` | `mild_cut` | `mild_cut` |
| Recomp | `recomp` | `recomp` | `recomp` |
| Maintain | `maintain` | `maintain` | `maint` |

Translators: `phaseToNutritionKey()` (`:299-301`) and `phaseToCoachingKey()`
(`:305+`, which logs a warning before falling back to `maint`, because *"silent
maintenance was masking data corruption / version skew bugs"*).

**Collisions this produces:**
- `bulk` is a user value, a coaching key, and NOT a nutrition key (the nutrition
  key is `build`). `build` and `bulk` therefore mean the same thing in different
  modules.
- `mild_bulk` and `mild_cut` exist only in the coaching vocabulary; `mild_cut` is
  simultaneously the nutrition key for the user-facing `cut`. So the user's "cut"
  is the engine's "mild cut" everywhere.
- `maintain` (user/nutrition) vs `maint` (coaching) — same concept, truncated.
- Two different phases (`bulk`, `strength_size`) collapse to the same nutrition
  and coaching keys; two more (`lean_gain`, `weak_point`) collapse to another
  pair. So the coaching engine sees **five** phases where the user sees **seven**.
- A fourth vocabulary exists in `nutritionEngine.js:1066, 1084`: `phaseType ===
  'maintenance'` — a fifth spelling of the same idea.
- D19/EN-4 note preserved in the data (`:274-278`): *"recomp is coached at its own
  -0.125 %/wk goal rate instead of aliasing to maintenance's 0 %/wk."*
- `GOAL_LABELS` (`:114`) and `PHASE_LABELS` (`:294`) are separate label maps for
  the two axes.

Separately, "goal" has a **third** referent: `exercise_goals` table
(`database.js:609`) — a per-exercise target, unrelated to physique goals or
training phases. And a fourth: `goal_lock_advanced` / `goal_lock_set_at` on
`users_profile` (migration 017) plus `GoalLockConsentScreen`, `GoalChangeSummaryScreen`,
`ProGoalSetupScreen` — the goal-lock consent mechanism.

## C.8 Check-in vs weekly review vs coach output

- **"Weekly check-in"** is the settled user-facing name. `WeeklyCheckInScreen.js`
  uses it as the `BackHeader title` at five separate render branches (`:1395`,
  `:1440`, `:1473`, `:1514`, `:1552`) and as `checkinDayLabel` (`:1621`);
  `CoachingRemindersScreen.js:364` `<SectionLabel>Weekly check-in</SectionLabel>`,
  `:370` *"Weekly check-in reminder"*.
- **"Weekly review"** is not used as a screen name. The nearest sibling surfaces
  are `WeeklyStory` (`WeeklyStoryScreen`) and `CoachOutput` (`CoachOutputScreen`).
- Data-layer names: local `weekly_checkins` (`database.js:521`) **and** cloud
  `weekly_checkins_v2` (registry entry, `migrate_047`, `migrate_050`). Two table
  names for one entity, split by generation.
- **Collision:** "check-in" also names the *daily* reminder category
  (`NOTIFICATIONS_LOCKED.md`: *"Daily check-in reminder"* at 19:00 local vs
  *"Weekly check-in reminder"* Sunday 18:00). And `CoachingRemindersScreen.js:283`
  toasts *"Check-in follow-up on/off"* — a third thing again.

## C.9 Coach vs Precision Coaching

- **"Precision Coaching"** is the branded product name for the Pro coaching
  system, and its use is a locked voice rule: `whyThisTemplates.snapshot.test.js`
  header — *"Also asserts every output passes the jargon blocklist and uses the
  Precision Coaching naming where the synthesis says it should."*
- User-facing sites: `AttentionCard.js:112,116` (*"How Precision Coaching works"*,
  and the same string as its `accessibilityLabel`); `ProGate.js:48` (*"…while
  keeping Precision Coaching in sync."*).
- Engine copy sites: `nutritionEngine.js:402` *"Precision Coaching has held your
  calorie target…"*, `:282`, `:380`, `:611`; `shareCard/drawShareCard.js:663`
  *"Weekly Precision Coaching recap"*; `shareCard/greatWeek.js:5`.
- **"Coach"** unbranded is the navigation/route word: the `Coach` tab
  (`iaNavigation.guard.test.js` pins *"Coach root is deterministic and links
  profile as a separate surface"*), `CoachReview`, `CoachOutput`,
  `CoachHeldHistory`, `CoachingReminders`, `SettingsCoaching`, `coachApply.js`,
  `weeklyCoach.js`, `coachResponse.js`, `coachReport.js`, `coachOutcome.js`,
  `coachingGoals.js`, `coach_outputs` table.
- **Collision:** "Coach" also means the **human B2B coach** in
  `B2B_COACH_PHASE_2_SCOPED.md` (*"A coach is a regular Volyume account with an
  additional `coach_id`"*), and in the tier table row *"Coach link (B2B, phase
  two)"*. One word, an algorithm and a person. This one is currently harmless only
  because the B2B surface does not exist (A.3.1).
- D68 (`DECISIONS:1430`) records a *"Coach page real merge"* ruling, so the Coach
  surface consolidation is itself a decided item.

## C.10 PR vs record vs personal best

Three words for one thing, all live simultaneously:
- **"PR"** — `ShareCardScreen.js:425` `<SegmentBtn label="New PR" …>`;
  `detectPR`, `bestPRPerExercise`, `workoutRecordLine.js`, `PRCelebration`

  `<SectionLabel tone="muted">Personal records</SectionLabel>`;
  `SubscriptionPolicyScreen.js:57` *"Personal records and strength standing."*
- **"personal best"** — `ExerciseDetailScreen.js:151` *"which sessions earned a
  personal best"*, `:535`.
- Data model: `record_type` with three values — `'1rm_estimate'`,
  `'heaviest_weight'`, `'most_reps'` (`ExerciseDetailScreen.js:362-364`,
  `:647-649`). So a single "PR" is actually three record kinds, and the UI labels
  `'1rm_estimate'` as **"Est. max"** and `'heaviest_weight'` as **"Heaviest set"**
  (`:665`), which are two more surface words.
- D87 (`DECISIONS:2070`) added a *"Live personal-record indicator on the logging
  screen"* — using yet another phrasing.
- D91's `blockMetrics.stage3` introduces **"PR density"** (`prDensity`,
  `rawPrCount`, `eligibleExposures`), a fourth sense: a rate, not an event.

## C.11 e1RM vs Est. max vs estimated 1RM

- **Code:** `e1RM` / `e1rm` / `bestE1rm` / `e1rmSlopePct` / `epleyE1rm` /
  `calculate1RM`.
- **User-facing:** **"Est. max"** — `ExerciseDetailScreen.js:90`
  `{ key: 'e1rm', label: 'Est. max' }`, `:665`, `:871` *"Est. max: ~{n}{units}"*.
  The metric key is `e1rm`, the label is `Est. max`; that pairing on one line is
  the clearest single illustration of the code/copy split in this app.
- A third form appears in the record type: `'1rm_estimate'`.
- `LiftProgressScreen.js:82, 412, 454, 469, 658` uses "e1RM" in comments while
  rendering *"the e1RM headline"* — worth a reviewer checking whether "e1RM" ever
  reaches the screen; the comment at `:658` says the headline is *"a weight/e1RM
  readout"*. **UNCERTAIN** whether the literal string "e1RM" is rendered.
- `WindowChips.js:3` comments name the three lenses *"weight trend, e1RM, weekly
  volume"*.
- Note "1RM" is not on the jargon blocklist (which blocks MEV/MAV/MRV/RIR/RPE/
  mesocycle/junk volume), so the abbreviation is permitted; the softened "Est. max"
  is a design choice rather than a lint rule.

## C.12 Learned range vs adaptive band vs adaptive landmarks

Three named systems that all produce per-muscle volume numbers, and the code is
careful to keep them apart:
- **`computeAdaptiveLandmarks`** (`algorithms.js:991`) — session-grain adaptive
  bands learned from feedback. Blueprint §1.2 (`:41-44`): *"DOES learn per-muscle
  bands from session feedback and survives block boundaries - but it feeds only
  the Pro session tweaks and (since D90 #3) the display surfaces. Plan generation
  and block seeding never consume it."*
- **`effectiveLandmarks.js:3`** — *"(founder GO 2026-08-06, D90 #3: adaptive bands
  wired NOW, not queued)."* Consumes `VOLUME_LANDMARKS` + `computeAdaptiveLandmarks`.
- **`learnedRange.js`** (Stage 5) — *"the learned working range … Replay a
  muscle's Block Ledger history into its learned working range"*, explicitly
  distinguished at `:17` from *"session-grain adaptive bands
  (computeAdaptiveLandmarks), which stay …"*.
- **`VOLUME_LANDMARKS`** (`algorithms.js:20`) — the static research MEV/MAV/MRV
  table.
- **Collision (one word, several things):** "band" means the adaptive landmark
  band, and separately a **resistance band** (D10's exercise-equipment exception:
  *"Band Lat Pulldown and Band Assisted Pull-Up"*). Both appear in engine
  vocabulary.
- **Collision (three names, one family):** landmarks / bands / range. The jargon
  blocklist bans MEV, MAV and MRV from copy, so none of the three names reaches the
  user; the user sees only sentences like *"right in the range where muscle adapts
  best"* (`whyThisTemplates.snapshot.test.js:29`).

## C.13 Adherence

- Live user-facing: `FoodInsightsScreen.js:528` *"You hit your protein on N of M
  days you logged."* — the concept is rendered, the word is not.
- `src/lib/food/adherence.js` exports `ADHERENCE_TOLERANCE`, `pctLabel`, `within`.
- Coach side: `mapCalsAdherence` (`weeklyCoach.js`, imported by
  `CoachOutputScreen.js:9`), `deriveCalsAdherence` (`checkinDerive.js`),
  `calsAdherence` on check-in rows, `cardio_adherence` column (migrate_050).
- `checkinDerive.js:1-9` header draws an explicit and important line: *"these are
  DISPLAY-tier pre-selections the user always sees and can override — they are NOT
  the ED safety system (calorie floors, rapid-loss threshold) … deriveCalsAdherence
  is an adherence read against the user's own target, never a floor check."*
- **Collision:** adherence means calorie adherence, cardio adherence, and (in
  `interBlock`) block **dose** adherence — D91-3: *"an UNDELIVERED dose (adherence
  < 0.6 or exposures < 4)"*. Three denominators, one word.
- `FoodInsightsScreen.js:203` records an ED-safety constraint on the concept:
  *"Adherence-neutral, no target, no …"*.

## C.14 Summary of terminology collisions

**Two-or-more words, one thing (11):** programme/plan; mesocycle/training block/
block; recovery week/lighter week/deload; secondary half-credit/fractional working
set/indirect volume; readiness/recovery grade; bulk/build; maintain/maint/
maintenance; weekly_checkins/weekly_checkins_v2; PR/personal record/personal best;
e1RM/Est. max/1rm_estimate; learned range/adaptive band/adaptive landmark.

**One word, two-or-more things (8):** plan (programme / day / volume
prescription); readiness (pre-session / block trend / **profile completeness**);
goal (physique category / training phase / per-exercise goal / goal-lock);
check-in (daily reminder / weekly / follow-up); coach (the algorithm / the future
human B2B coach); deload (the prescribed week / the trigger flag); band (volume
band / resistance band); PR (an event / a density rate).

# PART D — TEST-REVEALED BEHAVIOUR

808 test files under `src/` and `tests/`. **~290 of them use
`fs.readFileSync`**, i.e. they are source-level regression guards that assert on
the text of a source file rather than on runtime behaviour. This is a deliberate,
documented repo convention (`CLAUDE.md` §3: *"Source-level regression guards
(fs.readFileSync + regex) lock founder rules"*), and it is the single richest
source of product behaviour that reading screens will not reveal.

Below: behaviours a screen-reader would miss, each with the test that proves it.

## D.1 Identity and account lifecycle
- **No code may mutate a row's `user_id` at runtime.** `scripts/check-identity-invariant.sh`
  greps `SET user_id` across `src/` (excluding tests) and fails unless a
  `LOCKED-OK` comment appears within the preceding 10 lines. Run by
  `.github/workflows/identity-invariant.yml` on every push to `main` and
  `claude/**` and every PR. *This is a build-breaking product rule with no UI
  representation at all.*
- **Sign-out empties local SQLite and clears AsyncStorage with zero carve-outs.**
  `src/lib/__tests__/wipeAllUserData.test.js`,
  `src/store/__tests__/signOutDeleteTombstones.guard.test.js`.
- **Onboarding cannot be tapped through on biological sex.**
  `src/lib/__tests__/proOnboarding.sexGate.test.js` header: *"Sex drives the
  SACRED ED calorie floor + BMR, so a null must never advance past the profile
  step and must never be silently defaulted (e.g. to male) downstream."* It pins
  three separate things by regex: `advanceFrom2` returns on an invalid sex; the
  step-2 `canContinue` **requires** an explicit `male|female`; and the button is
  actually `disabled` when `canContinue` is false. Sibling:
  `proOnboarding.heightGate.test.js`, `identityGate.proOnboarding.test.js`.

## D.2 ED-safety behaviour that fails CLOSED
- `src/__tests__/edFlagFailClosed.guard.test.js` is the clearest example in the
  repo of test-only behaviour. Its header: several `getOpenEdPatternFlag(...)`
  reads *"still failed OPEN — a transient local-SQLite read error was mapped to
  null / false ('no flag'), so a surface the flag is meant to WITHHOLD would be
  shown or sent to a flagged, vulnerable user."* The fix pinned by the test:
  read the flag with `.catch(() => 'read_failed')` and treat the truthy sentinel
  as **flag-OPEN** (`!!flag`); the two notification helpers return `true`
  (suppress) on read error. Correct sites it names: `HomeScreen.js:737` and `:794`,
  `partners/moments.js:90`, `useWeeklyStreak.js:83`, `coachReport.js:259`,
  `CoachOutputScreen.js:1075`.
  **Behaviour statement: a database read failure makes the app behave as though an
  ED flag is open, not as though it is closed.** No UI shows this.
- `src/screens/__tests__/wellbeingFailClosed.guard.test.js` — same posture for the
  wellbeing/calm reads.
- `src/lib/__tests__/edFloorSeams.f3.test.js`,
  `progressScanSafetyFloorIsolation.test.js`,
  `src/screens/__tests__/goalChangeSummary.edFlag.test.js`,
  `ProSetupCompleteScreen.edSafety.test.js`,
  `CoachOutputScreen.edPatternAnnounce.guard.test.js`.
- **Tier-blindness is asserted as a source property, not a runtime one:**
  `interBlock.stage2.test.js:658` — *"tier-blind: the word tier never appears in
  the module"*. `blockSeed.stage6.test.js:187`, `blockExplain.stage8.test.js:250`,
  `blockLedgerGather.stage6.test.js:273`, `learnedRange.stage5.test.js:326` each
  assert *"no clocks, no randomness, no I/O, no store, tier-blind"*.
- ED-safe exclusion nudge: `DietaryPreferencesEditor.test.js:107-112` — *"the
  exclusion list has no hard cap, only a calm, tier-blind"* nudge, matching D14's
  soft-nudge ruling at ~15 excluded foods.

## D.3 Voice and copy law, enforced two ways

**By lint** (`eslint.config.js`, `no-restricted-syntax`, applied to
`src/screens/**` and `src/components/**`, and repeated verbatim for
`src/screens/HomeScreen.js` and `src/screens/ShareCardScreen.js` because flat
config replaces rather than merges a repeated rule key):
- **Em dash ban** — selectors `Literal[value=/—/]` and
  `JSXText[value=/—/]`, message *"No em dash (—) in user-facing copy. Use a
  full stop, comma, or colon (CLAUDE.md voice rule)."*
- **Machine-tell word ban** — `delve|leverage|utili[sz]e|facilitate|seamless(ly)?|
  streamlin(e|es|ed|ing)|robust|comprehensive`, message *"Machine-tell word in copy
  (CLAUDE.md 'No AI fingerprint'). Rewrite in plain spoken voice."*
- **Clipped-drama tail ban** (founder rule 2026-07-11, D67) —
  `/,\s*(?:always|ever|forever)(?:[.!]|\s*$)/i`, with the rationale in the config:
  *"copy like 'Yours free, always' / 'No ads, ever' reads as AI-register marketing,
  not plain British English."*
- Design-system law in the same rule set: no hex colours, no `rgba()`, no
  hex-alpha concat (`token + '50'`), no hex-alpha template, no raw `fontSize`, no
  raw `fontWeight`, no raw `letterSpacing` (only `letterSpacing.overline` and
  `letterSpacing.wordmark` — *"the two named brand-wordmark sites (SettingsAbout
  app name, PRCelebration hero)"*).
- Accessibility law, deliberately scoped: touchables must carry
  `accessibilityLabel` — **only in `src/screens/HomeScreen.js`**. The config
  records why: *"forcing accessibilityLabel across src/screens + src/components
  trips 53 pre-existing violations today (counted 2026-07-08 …) and would break the
  lint gate outright … widen file-by-file as each screen is swept."*
  **Behaviour statement: the a11y label rule is a one-file beachhead, not a repo
  rule.** Nothing in the UI reveals that.
- `ShareCardScreen.js` is exempt from the colour rules *"only for its
  legitimately-literal offline HTML palette"* but keeps the full copy gate.

**By test** — `src/lib/__tests__/jargonBlocklist.test.js`. `checkJargon()`
(exported from `whyThisTemplates.js`) must reject: `MEV territory`, `MAV ceiling`,
`MRV check`, `leave 2 RIR on the bar`, `stay at 7 RPE`, `this mesocycle ends
Sunday`, `junk volume`, `metabolic adaptation`, and **bare researcher surnames**.
Consumed by `coachResponse.test.js`, `coachRegister.test.js`,
`sessionAdjustments.test.js`.
**Behaviour statement: the words "mesocycle", "MEV", "MAV", "MRV", "RIR" and "RPE"
are mechanically forbidden from generated coaching copy, which is why the code and
the UI use different vocabularies (Part C).**

## D.4 Contract tests against SQL migration files

These read `supabase/*.sql` from the test suite and assert on their contents.
They encode server behaviour a client reader cannot see.

- **`src/lib/__tests__/trialLedger.contract.test.js`** (migration 071). Header:
  *"The 14-day cardless trial was anchored to users_profile.trial_state, which
  account-delete wipes, so delete + re-signup restarted the trial. Migration 071
  adds a private.trial_ledger (salted email hash) that survives deletion and makes
  start_cascade refuse a second cardless trial for the same email."* Pins:
  `private.trial_ledger` and `private.trial_salt` tables exist,
  `private.email_trial_hash` function exists, `digest(` is used (*"The stored value
  is a hash, not the email"*), `email_hash text PRIMARY KEY`, and that the ledger
  is NOT deleted by `migrate_062_delete_user_data_post025_tables.sql`. It also pins
  that the implementation cannot regress *"back to the superuser-only
  session_replication_role bypass that threw on hosted Supabase before 068."*
- **`src/lib/__tests__/founderProLedger.contract.test.js`** (migration 108). Pins
  `private.founder_pro_ledger` with `email_hash text PRIMARY KEY` and **asserts no
  plaintext `email text` column**. Seeds three named founder emails as hashes.
  Pins that founder accounts are applied as `trial_state = 'paid_pro'`,
  `tier = 'pro'`, `pro_trial_ends_at = NULL` — *"not time-limited trial accounts"* —
  and that *"profile creation and later downgrade attempts are corrected by a
  server trigger"*.
  **Behaviour statement: three specific accounts are permanently Pro by
  server-side trigger, invisible to the client.**
- **`src/lib/__tests__/customExerciseSync.contract.test.js`.** Header: *"The whole
  app resolves an exercise by id against the local `exercises` table … The local
  `custom_exercises` table is an orphaned mirror nothing reads … So the cloud
  restore MUST land custom exercises in `exercises` (is_custom=1), not the orphaned
  table, or they vanish from the UI after a reinstall / device swap."* It slices
  `_pullCustomExercises` out of `sync.js` by string offset and asserts
  `insertOrUpdateExerciseFromCloud({...row, is_custom: 1})`.
  **Behaviour statement: reinstall data loss is prevented by one regex.**
- Sibling contract suites: `rtdnWebhook.contract.test.js`,
  `appStoreWebhook.contract.test.js`, `sendPush.contract.test.js`,
  `schema-drift.test.js`, `backupTables.guard.test.js`,
  `src/lib/telemetry/__tests__/allowlistDrift.test.js` (server telemetry
  allow-list vs client catalogue).

## D.5 Snapshot-locked copy
`src/lib/__tests__/whyThisTemplates.snapshot.test.js` header: *"Locks the new
strings so an accidental rewrite or regression fails CI. Updating these snapshots
requires explicit reviewer sign-off. Also asserts every output passes the jargon
blocklist and uses the Precision Coaching naming where the synthesis says it
should."* It uses `toMatchInlineSnapshot`, so the exact sentences are in the test
file. Examples pinned verbatim:
- *"Chest: 6 sets this week. You can add a session or two if you want this muscle growing faster."*
- *"Back: 14 sets this week, right in the range where muscle adapts best."*
- *"Shoulders: 18 sets this week, near the upper end. Good, but watch recovery. Volume pulls back if you get sore."*
- *"Quads: 24 sets this week, more than your body can likely recover from. Next week's plan drops 2-3 sets."*
- *"Your next session moves to 82.5kg. You completed every working set at the current weight."*
- *"Weight drops slightly to rebuild. Quality sets beat grinding reps."*
**Caveat a reviewer must carry:** as established in B.2, **seven** of the
generators this suite locks have no caller. The snapshots protect copy that is not
currently rendered. Two of these snapshots were deliberately re-anchored under
D91-23 (deload copy made qualitative).

## D.6 The adaptive-mesocycle stage suites — pinned invariants as behaviour statements

Ten test-first suites (`blockLifecycle.stage1`, `interBlock.stage2`,
`blockMetrics.stage3`, `weeklyCoach.stage4.fatigueContext`, `learnedRange.stage5`,
`blockLedgerGather.stage6`, `blockSeed.stage6`, `deload.stage7`,
`blockExplain.stage8`, `adaptiveBlock.e2e`). Each was written **before** its
module existed, against `docs/blueprint-adaptive-mesocycle-2026-08-09.md`.
Restated as behaviour:

**Stage 1 — block lifecycle.** A finished block enters an explicit
`COMPLETED_AWAITING_DECISION` state. The week index never wraps back to week 1.
The user is never left silently training deload targets under an "Introduction
week" label. **No new mesocycle is ever created without explicit user action.** An
ignored block three weeks on stays in the SAME state with `weeksOverdue` counting.

**Stage 2 — the Block Ledger classifier.** Per-muscle classification into
RESPONSIVE / OVERREACHED / STALE / STRAINED / INSUFFICIENT_DATA, with evidence,
confidence, proposed start/peak, rationale and optional stimulus-change and
recovery-duration proposals. Founder amendment pinned verbatim: *"do not
automatically define RESPONSIVE as previousStart + 1. A successful dose should
normally be retained. Increase next-block starting volume only when evidence
indicates that higher volume later in the block produced additional useful
progression without excessive recovery cost."* Under calm mode or an open ED flag
there is **no upward carry-over anywhere**; reductions still apply.

**Stage 3 — the performance metric.** e1RM via the single mandated
`calculate1RM`, one best-e1RM point per session per exercise. A **stable** exercise
has ≥3 block sessions and appears in both the early and late halves of the
accumulation phase. Slopes are fitted per exercise (least squares over days,
normalised by the fitted start) and combined as a **weighted mean of slopes** —
*"raw e1RM values are never pooled across exercises."* Weights halve for an
exercise new this block, and halve again if its target rep range shifted mid-block
(null targets are unknown, not a shift). `confidence` = weighted stable
exercise-sessions / raw exercise-sessions; `discontinuity` = stable raw share
< 0.5.

**Stage 4 — fatigue context.** An observed recovery grade 3 **in the block's peak
week only** reads as expected accumulated fatigue, so performance 1 pushes instead
of holding. It never applies in weeks 1..n-1, never to grade 4, never touches the
deload thresholds, and never applies when `consecutivePoorRecoveryWeeks >= 1`
(persistent fatigue predates the peak). **Without block context inputs the engine
is byte-identical.** PR density replaces the single all-time PR for the top
performance grade: ~1 PR per 3 completed sessions, or a caller-supplied block e1RM
slope ≥ 1.5%, or the check-in's own 'exceeded' verdict. *"The safety order is
untouched: a safety hold still caps any push, including a context-softened one."*

**Stage 5 — the learned working range.** Replays per-muscle Block Ledger history
over a profile-adjusted prior — **no parallel store**. Ceiling starts at the
prior's MAV; RESPONSIVE moves it toward `achievedPeak` capped ±2 per block;
OVERREACHED moves it toward `achievedPeak - 2`, downward only; STRAINED toward the
block's start, downward only; STALE does not move it (*"volume was not the
lever"*). Floor starts at prior MEV, nudges ±1 per block, RESPONSIVE blocks only.
Clamps: research MEV is the absolute floor anchor; ceiling never exceeds adapted
MRV (or prior MRV), nor 30; `floor <= ceiling - 2`. Minimum evidence: only ledger
entries with confidence ≥ 0.6, a real classification and observed numbers count.
D91-12: **manual-override blocks are skipped by the replay entirely**, *"so
removing an override can never surface the user's own old numbers dressed up as
coach learning."*

**Stage 6 — gather + seed.** Scale contracts pinned: `workouts.soreness_24h_before`
is 1-3 and remaps 1→2, 2→3, 3→4 into interBlock's 1-5 `sorenessLateAvg`;
`readinessSlope` is the normalised total change across the block (a 30+ point
decline reads ≤ -0.3); `deloadFlagMidBlock` means the flag fired **before** the
peak week; rebound windows are the first week of a block starting within 14 days
of the previous block's end, plus the week after any applied early deload.
Seeding fallback order, founder verbatim: *"1 manual override -> 2 valid ledger ->
3 learned band -> 4 profile-adjusted research -> 5 raw research; Never silently
discard a valid previous-block recommendation."* Advisor button semantics:
`repeat` = a TRUE repeat (the block's own observed start / planned peak);
`adjust` = the full ledger proposal.

**Stage 7 — strain-aware deload.** `computeDeloadVolume(plannedRows, context)`
lands at `max(deloadFloor(mev), share of the muscle's peak CAPPED at the row's own
planned sets)`, share running 60% (strain 0) down to 40% (strain ≥ 4) in 5-point
steps. **Without context the legacy flat-MEV cut is byte-identical.** A deload
never raises a row. Founder monotonicity pin, verbatim: *"Greater strain can only
make a recovery prescription easier or longer; it can never make it harder or
shorter."* An **unreadable strain fails CLOSED to heavy** — the smallest recovery
dose, never the lightest cut. `deloadSets` clamps to
`min(startSets, ABSOLUTE_WEEKLY_SET_CEILING)`. Suppression withholds `deloadSets`
entirely. A true repeat carries no `deloadSets`.

**Stage 8 — explanation honesty.** `summariseSeededPlan` reads the **written**
`planned_muscle_volume` rows — *"the plan as it actually exists — never the seed
map that was merely requested, so a skipped insert can never be narrated as
applied."* D91-13: every row records its source
(`seed_ledger`/`learned`/`manual`/`profile`/`research`/template) and every
explanation surface reads the written rows, *"so no narration can outrun the plan."*
D91-2: the 'adjust' button reads **"Restart this programme"** until an app-side
adjustment is real, *"A button must not promise what the app does not do."*

**e2e — the synthetic athlete.** `adaptiveBlock.e2e.test.js` is the founder's
end-to-end campaign: six muscles / six outcomes, a **permanent** repeat-vs-adjust
regression, suppression / stale / manual / null-ledger variants, gather-extraction
pins, sync-authority and provenance source pins, and chain purity. It also pins
D91-21: *"INSUFFICIENT_DATA never seeds as ledger."*

- `src/screens/__tests__/HomeScreen.bannerPriorityCap.test.js` plus the three

# PART E — DOCUMENTATION INVENTORY

**340 markdown files under `docs/`** plus loose root-level documents and three
sibling documentation trees (`audit/`, `research/`, `marketing/`,
`.volyume-audit/`). Full per-file descriptions follow the trust classification
first, because that is the part a reviewer needs.

## E.1 The trust rule this repository actually uses

On 2026-07-10 a docs-staleness sweep stamped a machine-readable banner on the top
three lines of every non-current document. **The banner is the classification.**
Two banner texts exist:

1. `> ⚠ STATUS (2026-07-10): SUPERSEDED/CLOSED - do not build from this document.
   … Current work runs from docs/ux-world-class-audit-2026-07-09/_HANDOVER-AND-RESUME.md
   and docs/TASKBOARD.md. Pre-campaign items require the D37 triage rule before any
   consideration.` — **50 files.**
2. `⚠ STATUS (2026-07-10): PRE-CAMPAIGN BLUEPRINT/SPEC - GATED` — **26 files.**

Plus three bespoke variants: `docs/EMAIL_AUTH_DELIVERABILITY.md` (*"STALE OPS
REFERENCE - email/password auth was removed …"*),
`docs/design-usability-audit-2026-07-09/_CAMPAIGN-STATUS-AND-RESUME.md`
(*"PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED - do not run this as a standalone campaign"*),
`docs/exercise-planning-2026-07-09/plan-A-library-expansion.md`
(*"PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED - reference only"*).

**Trust classification used below:**
- **CURRENT** — an unbannered live coordination document.
- **LOCKED-CONTRACT** — a `*_LOCKED.md` design contract. Authoritative for its
  surface *except* where a later founder override banner inside it says otherwise.
  Several carry such overrides; they are noted.
- **STALE** — carries the SUPERSEDED/CLOSED banner, or is otherwise verifiably
  overtaken.
- **GATED** — carries the PRE-CAMPAIGN BLUEPRINT/SPEC banner. Not stale, not
  buildable without D37/D38 triage.
- **HISTORICAL** — a completed record kept for provenance (delivery reports,
  research passes, competitor teardowns, closed audits).

## E.7 CONTRADICTIONS — where documents disagree with the code, or with each other

Listed for the map's contradictions section. Each is verified.

**C1. `CLAUDE.md`: "(96 files)" migration count.**
- Claim (Section 1): *"Cloud schema lives in `supabase/migrate_NNN_*.sql` (96
  files …)"*.
- Reality: `ls supabase/migrate_*.sql | wc -l` = **128**, highest number
  `migrate_131_mesocycles_block_ledger.sql`.
- Already independently noticed inside the tree:
  `docs/volyume-elite-audit/10-prioritised-roadmap.md:101` proposes *"correct
  CLAUDE.md's stale '96 migrations' → 99"* — itself now stale by 29.

**C2. `CLAUDE.md`: "applied through `migrate_116`" and "049/059 HELD".**
- Claim (status banner): *"Cloud migrations are CLAUDE-RUN … applied through
  `migrate_116`; 049/059 HELD."*
- Reality per `docs/TASKBOARD.md` R3-0 (2026-07-27), verbatim: *"**CORRECTION to
  the old note below:** production was NOT at 116 with 117-128 pending. The live
  migration history shows repo migrations 117, 118 and 120-124, 126, 127 already
  applied under drifted names."* And the full sweep result at `TASKBOARD.md:1364`:
  *"**Result: ZERO missing. Zero tables, zero columns, zero functions.** Every repo
  migration is applied."* Migration 128 applied 2026-07-27; 129 and 130 applied
  2026-08-06; **131 applied and verified 2026-08-09** (`supabase/README.md`).
- And on the hold: `TASKBOARD.md:1366-1369` — *"migration 059's numbered meal-slot
  CHECK is live (`meal_[0-9]+` present in the pattern), so it **is applied** despite
  the CLAUDE.md header still listing it as HELD - another stale note."*
  **049 remains correctly unapplied** and must stay so (B.6).
- So `CLAUDE.md` is stale on three counts here: the applied ceiling, the 059 hold,
  and by implication the pending set.

**C3. `CLAUDE.md`: "82 screens".**
- Claim (Section 1 data flow): *"UI (src/screens, 82 screens; src/components)"*.
- Reality: `find src/screens -name '*.js' -not -path '*__tests__*'` = **84**.
  Two of those (`QuizScreen`, `PlanPreviewScreen`) are dark routes (B.4), so the
  *live* screen count is 82 — the number may have been correct at the time and
  correct-by-accident now. Recorded as a count to re-derive, not to trust.

**C4. `CLAUDE.md`: "useAppStore.js (~1,700 lines)".**
- Reality: **2,019 lines**.

**C5. `CLAUDE.md` module list omits `modules/progress-scan-image`.**
- Claim: *"native modules only via Expo config plugins — see `modules/live-activity`,
  `modules/rest-timer-live`"*.
- Reality: three local modules exist — `modules/live-activity`,
  `modules/rest-timer-live`, **`modules/progress-scan-image`** — and all three are
  file-linked dependencies in `package.json` (`live-activity`,
  `progress-scan-image`, `rest-timer-live`). There is also a fourth native surface
  not mentioned: `plugins/withVolyumeWidget.js` + `src/widgets/` +
  `react-native-android-widget`.

**C6. `docs/EMAIL_AUTH_DELIVERABILITY.md` banner contradicts `CLAUDE.md` and the code.**
- Banner: *"STALE OPS REFERENCE - email/password auth was removed …"*
- `CLAUDE.md` Section 1 Auth: *"plus email/password (re-added 2026-07-21 on founder
  order for App Review demo accounts and users who prefer email; it is ungated and
  available to everyone). Email/password had been removed 2026-07-01; do not
  'restore' that removal without asking."*
- Code: `src/lib/supabase.js:239` `c.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })`
  and `:245` `c.auth.signUp({ email, password })`. **Email/password is LIVE.** The
  banner is wrong.

**C7. `docs/BACKLOG.md` records a strength-standards drift that no longer exists,
and cites a screen that does not exist.**
- See B.9.3. `getStrengthStandard` is absent from `src/`; `PRWallScreen.js` does
  not exist.

**C8. `docs/BUDGET_POSTURE_LOCKED.md` still carries a RevenueCat cost row.**
- The founder switched to Play Billing direct on 2026-05-25 and RevenueCat is on
  the NEVER list (`BACKLOG.md`). The locked budget doc was not updated.

**C9. `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md` says "AI photo logging (never)" where the live
register (D27 addendum) says HELD.**
- Two different strengths for the same item. The live register governs; the
  SUPERSEDED doc over-states it. See A.2.1.

**C10. `docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md` says "Web app for end users (never at v1)" while a
Next.js web workspace exists at `web/`.**
- Not necessarily a conflict (the workspace is not shipped, and "never at v1" is a
  v1 statement) but a reviewer must not read `web/` as a live product surface, nor
  the GAP_ANALYSIS line as proof no web code exists. See A.3.2.

**C11. `docs/B2B_COACH_PHASE_2_SCOPED.md` overstates its own groundwork.**
- It claims `coach_id` columns exist. `grep -rln coach_id supabase/*.sql` returns
  nothing, and `coach_id` is absent from `src/`. `engine_overrides` does exist.
  See A.3.1.

**C12. `docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_LOCKED.md`'s shipped-status banner stops at migration
024.**
- Its final status line reads *"Tier and subscription domain (Move #5): NOT
  STARTED"*, which is false: the tier/subscription domain shipped and Play Billing
  is live (`CLAUDE.md` Section 1: *"Google Play Billing is live"*), with migrations
  065, 066, 067, 068, 070, 071 and 108 all applied.

**C13. `src/lib/links.js` claims a lock that points at an uncalled module.**
- Its header: *"Locked in PRIVACY_CONSENT_LOCKED.md line 280: the privacy policy
  URL is hardcoded here so the marketing site and the in-app link are updated
  together if the URL ever changes."* Nothing imports `LINKS`. Either the locked
  contract is unenforced, or the URL is duplicated elsewhere. **UNCERTAIN** (B.11).

**C14. `src/lib/food/diaryTimeline.js`'s header states a ruling that was reverted.**
- Its header asserts the timeline replaces *"the meal-bucket card layout for every
  user (June founder ruling …)"*. That ruling was reverted (D37 item 15) and is now
  on the never-re-propose list. A reader of that file alone would conclude the flat
  diary is the shipped design.

**C15. `APP_MAP_COMPLETE_2026-06-06.md` and the root-level map documents.**
- `APP_MAP_COMPLETE_2026-06-06.md` carries the SUPERSEDED banner, so it is at
  least labelled. `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `VOLYUME_DEEPMAP.md`, `APPMAP.md`,
  `CURRENT-STATE-DOSSIER.md` and `AUDIT_REPORT.md` at repo root do **not** — the
  2026-07-10 sweep only covered `docs/`. They predate the July-August campaign
  entirely (last modified 2026-07-27 by checkout, content dated June) and describe
  a product that has since had the logger redesigned (D43/D57-D66), the flat diary
  reverted (D75), the brand font reverted (D53), the adaptive mesocycle system
  built (D91 stages 1-8), and the Coach page merged (D68).

## F.5 CI workflows (`.github/workflows/`, 10)

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `main-ci.yml` | push to `main` + `claude/**` (paths-ignore `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `LICENSE`, `.ci-status/**`), PR to main, `workflow_dispatch` | Jest + lint + Expo Doctor. Node 22.22.2, `npm ci --legacy-peer-deps`. Its header states why it exists: *"the Android build workflow does not run Jest or Expo Doctor, so code that compiles can still ship with broken tests."* Uses `npm ci` deliberately *"so any future package-lock.json drift fails CI loudly"*. |
| `identity-invariant.yml` | push `main` + `claude/**`, PR to main | Runs `scripts/check-identity-invariant.sh`. Explicit minimal `permissions: contents: read` (added after a 403 at checkout). |
| `build-android.yml` | push `main` + `claude/**` | Signed APK + AAB. This is why every push to a `claude/**` branch auto-produces an APK for device walks. |
| `build-ios.yml` | **`workflow_dispatch` only** | EAS iOS. Header: *"Manual only: each EAS iOS build costs build credits, so this never auto-runs on a push … a push-triggered run can no longer submit to TestFlight even if the trigger returns."* |
| `deploy-migrations.yml` | **`workflow_dispatch` only** | Applies Supabase migrations. The push trigger was retired (E0). Blocked historically by an empty `SUPABASE_DB_URL` secret (TASKBOARD R3-0). |
| `deploy-functions.yml` | push to main touching an Edge Function | Auto-deploys Supabase functions. Header records the founder direction: *"I do not deploy anything"*. |
| `deploy-pages.yml` | push to main touching `public/**` | GitHub Pages for the privacy policy / marketing site. |
| `refresh-off-snapshot.yml` | cron Sunday 03:00 UTC + dispatch + on seed-script change | Rebuilds the bundled OpenFoodFacts UK snapshot. This is the *"operational remainder of item 16"* on the founder-actions list. |
| `maestro-e2e.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` (takes a `build_run_id`) | Pre-release Maestro E2E against an APK from a build run. |
| `print-signing-sha.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` | Prints signing SHA fingerprints (for Play OAuth SHA-1 confirmation). |

All workflows set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"` with the same
comment: *"GitHub forces JavaScript actions onto Node 24 on 2026-06-16. Opt in
early so CI proves Node 24 compatibility on our schedule, not on the forced flag
day."*

## F.8 Lint rules that encode product law
Summarised in D.3. In addition, `eslint.config.js` is ~470 lines of flat config
and the repo runs `eslint . --max-warnings 0`, so **every warning is a build
break**. `eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y` is registered repo-wide as a WARN
(therefore also fatal under `--max-warnings 0`); the config explains that its
`has-valid-accessibility-descriptors` rule *"is satisfied by ANY of
role/accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel/accessibilityActions/accessible, so a bare
`accessibilityRole="button"` with no label already passes it, even on an icon-only
button TalkBack cannot describe"* — which is why the stricter label rule exists
separately and is scoped to `HomeScreen.js` alone.

# UNCERTAINTIES (recorded, not resolved)

1. **`getCurrentMesoWeek` reachability.** No screen call site, but the blueprint
   describes its wrapping as user-visible narrative. Needs the training-domain map
   to adjudicate. (B.2, B.11)
2. **`src/lib/progressScanCopy.js`.** Orphaned by import, pinned by a source guard
   test. Whether an inlined equivalent replaced it is unresolved. (B.3, B.11)
3. **`src/lib/links.js`.** A locked contract (`PRIVACY_CONSENT_LOCKED.md` per the
   module header) points at a module with no importers. Either the lock is
   unenforced or the URLs are duplicated. (B.3, C13)
4. **Whether the literal string "e1RM" reaches the screen** on
   `LiftProgressScreen`, or only "Est. max" does. Comments suggest the former;
   I did not render the screen. (C.11)
5. **`docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_LOCKED.md`'s authority today.** Its status banner stops
   at migration 024 and one line is provably false (Move #5 "NOT STARTED"). Whether
   the *body* of the contract is still accurate for the tables it covers was not
   verified table by table. (E.3, C12)
6. **Root-level map documents** (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `VOLYUME_DEEPMAP.md`,
   `APPMAP.md`, `CURRENT-STATE-DOSSIER.md`, `AUDIT_REPORT.md`). Unbannered and
   large. I classified them STALE on date and campaign evidence, not by auditing
   their contents. A reviewer who wants to reuse any of them must re-verify.
7. **`web/` workspace status.** It exists, has real Next.js/Supabase code and a
   vitest setup, and is not covered by the app's lint/test gate. Whether it is
   deployed anywhere, and under what decision, is not recorded in any live
   document I found. (A.3.2)
8. **`docs/GROWTH_STRATEGY_SYNTHESIS_LOCKED.md` vs the `marketing/hq/` apparatus.**
   Two overlapping marketing authorities, one in `docs/` and one outside it, with
   no cross-reference between them. Which governs is not recorded.
9. **The 26 GATED documents.** "PRE-CAMPAIGN BLUEPRINT/SPEC - GATED" is not
   defined anywhere I could find beyond the banner text itself; D37 supplies the
   triage rule but not the gate's exit criteria.
10. **`docs/design-usability-audit-2026-07-09/DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md`.** A second
    file with the same basename as the live register, in a different folder. I did
    not fully reconcile the two; the TASKBOARD treats the design-usability folder as
    complete with only `coverage-00-SYNTHESIS.md` surviving, but a reviewer citing
    "DECISIONS-2026-07-09.md" without its folder path will be ambiguous.
